fn_operations_ai:
declare k record; v_health numeric; n int;
begin
  select * into k from ops_kpis;
  v_health := round(greatest(0, 100
    - least(30, coalesce(k.no_quote_backlog,0)*3)
    - (case when coalesce(k.avg_first_quote_hours,0) > 72 then 20 when coalesce(k.avg_first_quote_hours,0) > 48 then 10 else 0 end)
    - (case when coalesce(k.response_rate_pct,100) < 40 then 15 when coalesce(k.response_rate_pct,100) < 60 then 7 else 0 end)
    - least(15, coalesce(k.overdue_tasks,0)*3)
    - coalesce(k.cron_failures_24h,0)*4
    - least(10, coalesce(k.agent_errors_24h,0)*2)
    - (case when coalesce(k.high_risk_pending,0) > 5 then 8 else 0 end)),1);

  insert into ops_kpi_snapshots(snapshot_date,kpis) values (current_date, to_jsonb(k)||jsonb_build_object('ops_health',v_health))
    on conflict (snapshot_date) do update set kpis=excluded.kpis, created_at=now();

  perform ops_rec('no_quote_backlog', coalesce(k.no_quote_backlog,0) > 0, 'medium', 'Inquiries stuck without quotes',
    k.no_quote_backlog||' inquir(y/ies) older than 7 days have no quotes — a supply/response bottleneck. Chase matched suppliers or onboard supply in those categories.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'These RFQs reached at least one supplier. An RFQ that fanned out to zero suppliers is not a response problem at all, and until fn_rfq_redispatch_sweep shipped today it would have sat here forever looking like one.',
      'Seven days without a quote means the suppliers declined or ignored it, not that they quoted outside the platform and the customer never told us.',
      'The backlog count is of inquiries, not of customers: one buyer with five open RFQs looks like five bottlenecks.'),
    'Clearing '||coalesce(k.no_quote_backlog,0)||' stuck RFQ(s) is the shortest path to revenue on this board — each one is a customer who asked and is still waiting, and a reveal is the only event that earns.',
    'No spend. Chasing costs outreach time; the alternative, onboarding supply in those categories, is free from the existing lead base and gated on invite_enabled.');

  perform ops_rec('slow_first_quote', coalesce(k.avg_first_quote_hours,0) > 48, 'medium', 'First quotes are slow',
    'First quotes are averaging '||coalesce(k.avg_first_quote_hours,0)||' hours. Tighten supplier response SLAs / nudges to speed the funnel.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'The mean is meaningful at this volume. With very few quoted RFQs a single slow outlier moves this average by hours and would raise this alert on its own.',
      'The clock starts when the RFQ was dispatched, so a supplier who was notified late is counted as a supplier who replied slowly.',
      'Suppliers are being measured on hours that include nights and weekends, which no UAE contractor works.'),
    'Every hour cut from the first-quote wait is a buyer less likely to go elsewhere; the first quote is the moment an RFQ stops feeling like it went nowhere.',
    'No spend. Nudges cost supplier goodwill if the SLA is unrealistic, which is why the assumption about nights and weekends above matters before tightening anything.');

  perform ops_rec('low_response_rate', coalesce(k.response_rate_pct,100) < 60, 'medium', 'Supplier response rate is low',
    'Supplier response rate is '||coalesce(k.response_rate_pct,0)||'%. Improve matching quality and supplier enablement.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'The denominator is RFQs actually dispatched to a supplier. A dispatch that reached nobody never enters it, so this rate describes matched suppliers only and says nothing about coverage.',
      'A non-response is a decision not to quote, not a supplier who never saw the RFQ — undelivered mail would read identically here.',
      'The matcher put the right trade in front of them: a bad match produces a silent supplier who was right to stay silent.'),
    'Response rate is the clearest read on whether the matcher is sending the right work to the right companies. Fixing it lifts every RFQ in every category at once, not one queue.',
    'No spend. Supplier enablement is outreach time; improving matching is engineering time against fn_match_capability.');

  perform ops_rec('approvals_backlog', coalesce(k.pending_approvals,0) > 15, 'low', 'Approval queue building up',
    k.pending_approvals||' items are awaiting your decision ('||coalesce(k.high_risk_pending,0)||' high-risk). Clear the queue so the agents can proceed.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'Every pending item is genuinely blocked on a human. An item left pending because nothing consumes that kind would look identical and would not move if you decided it.',
      'The '||coalesce(k.high_risk_pending,0)||' high-risk item(s) carry a risk level set by the routine that raised them, which is a self-assessment and not an audit.',
      'The queue is a founder queue: none of these can be cleared by another agent, or they would already have been.'),
    'Each decision unblocks whatever the raising agent wanted to do next. A queue this size is the company waiting on one person, which is the thing the whole design is meant to avoid.',
    'No spend. Founder attention, which is the scarcest resource here and the reason the queue is worth keeping short.');

  perform ops_rec('overdue_tasks', coalesce(k.overdue_tasks,0) > 0, 'low', 'Overdue tasks',
    k.overdue_tasks||' task(s) are past due. Reschedule or action them.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'The due dates were set deliberately. A task auto-dated by the routine that created it is overdue against a guess, not against a commitment.',
      'These tasks have an owner who could act. org_tasks.assigned_agent had no writer at all until 12 Aug, so anything created before then may be overdue and ownerless — a scheduling problem masking a staffing one.'),
    'Rescheduling honestly is worth as much as finishing: a due date nobody believes makes every other due date meaningless, and this counter is what the health score reads.',
    'No spend. The real cost is that clearing overdue tasks by moving dates, rather than by doing them, hides the department that is short-staffed.');

  perform ops_rec('automation_failures', coalesce(k.cron_failures_24h,0) > 0 or coalesce(k.agent_errors_24h,0) > 5, 'high', 'Automation failures detected',
    coalesce(k.cron_failures_24h,0)||' scheduled-job failure(s) and '||coalesce(k.agent_errors_24h,0)||' agent error(s) in 24h. Investigate the failing jobs.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'agent_runs status=error means a fault. Several routines here write status=error to record a real-world FINDING they were built to report, so a healthy watcher doing its job inflates this count.',
      'The window is the last 24 hours, so a fault repaired hours ago is still counted; read the timestamps before investigating.',
      'A cron failure is the job failing, not the job being absent. A schedule that was never created cannot fail and so cannot appear here at all — which is the more dangerous state.'),
    'Each failing job is something the company does without being asked. Left failing, that work silently stops and this counter is the only place it shows.',
    'No spend. Engineering attention; the diagnosis is usually one note in agent_runs.');

    -- COUNT THE AGENT THIS COMPANY ACTUALLY WRITES TO (13 Aug 2026). Every insert into
  -- agent_actions passes a00_agent_action_resolve_addressee, which rewrites an addressee that is
  -- not an active org_agent through fn_org_agent_resolve. 'operations_ai' is an alias for
  -- 'ops_director', so nothing has been stored under 'operations_ai' since the trigger shipped and
  -- this counter was reading a key the table no longer uses. Measured today: 40 rows under
  -- 'operations_ai' (39 auto_done, 1 done) and 9 under 'ops_director' - one of them PENDING. So
  -- open_recommendations reported 0 while a recommendation was genuinely open. Resolving the alias
  -- here rather than hardcoding both keys keeps the count correct if the mapping changes again.
  select count(*) into n from agent_actions
   where agent in ('operations_ai', coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve('operations_ai'),'operations_ai'))
     and status in ('pending','needs_review');

  return jsonb_build_object('ran_at',now(),'ops_health',v_health,'kpis',to_jsonb(k),'open_recommendations',n);
end

fn_document_controller:
declare k record; v_health numeric; v_ret numeric; v_backup numeric; n int;
begin
  select * into k from document_kpis;
  v_ret := round(100.0*(k.total_documents - coalesce(k.past_retention,0))/nullif(k.total_documents,0),1);
  v_backup := case when coalesce(k.days_since_backup,999) <= 10 then 100 when coalesce(k.days_since_backup,999) <= 20 then 60 else 20 end;
  v_health := round(coalesce(k.ocr_coverage_pct,100)*0.30 + coalesce(v_ret,100)*0.35 + v_backup*0.20 + greatest(0,100-coalesce(k.oversized,0)*5)*0.15,1);

  insert into document_kpi_snapshots(snapshot_date,kpis) values (current_date, to_jsonb(k)||jsonb_build_object('doc_health',v_health))
    on conflict (snapshot_date) do update set kpis=excluded.kpis, created_at=now();

  -- recommendations (founder-visible; the Controller NEVER deletes a document on its own)
  perform doc_rec('past_retention', coalesce(k.past_retention,0) > 0, 'medium', 'Documents past retention period',
    k.past_retention||' document(s) are older than their retention class. Review for archival or deletion — the Controller flags only and never deletes on its own.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'The retention class on each document is right. A document filed under the wrong class ages out early and appears here as safe to delete when it is not.',
      'Past retention means MAY be deleted, never MUST. A document under an open dispute, refund claim or regulatory query outlives its class, and this rule cannot see any of those.',
      'Nothing else depends on these files: a quote PDF, a signed T&C or a redacted drawing still referenced by a live RFQ would read identically here.'),
    'Reviewing '||coalesce(k.past_retention,0)||' document(s) keeps the retention promise made to customers in the T&C, which is a commitment and not housekeeping. It also lifts the retention component of doc_health, currently weighted 0.35.',
    'No spend; storage saved is negligible at this size. The real cost is asymmetric and one-way: deleting a document that was still needed cannot be undone, which is why this routine only ever flags.');

  perform doc_rec('ocr_backlog', coalesce(k.ocr_backlog,0) > 0, 'low', 'Documents pending OCR/processing',
    k.ocr_backlog||' registered document(s) are not fully processed/extracted. Re-run the doc processing pipeline.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'These are processable. A scanned photograph, a CAD original or a password-protected PDF will never extract, and re-running the pipeline on them produces the same backlog tomorrow.',
      'The backlog is pipeline lag, not a pipeline that has stopped — this rule counts unprocessed documents and cannot tell a queue from an outage.'),
    'Extracted text is what makes a document findable and quotable; until then '||coalesce(k.ocr_backlog,0)||' document(s) are stored but effectively invisible to every search and every agent that reads them.',
    'Model spend, small and per document. Re-running on files that can never extract is the wasteful case, which is what the first assumption is there to catch.');

  perform doc_rec('backup_stale', coalesce(k.days_since_backup,999) > 10, 'high', 'Backup may be stale',
    'The last backup to the backups bucket was '||coalesce(k.days_since_backup::text,'never')||' day(s) ago. Confirm the weekly Dropbox backup job is running.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'An object in the backups bucket means a GOOD backup. This rule reads the newest object''s age and never opens it, so a job writing a truncated or empty archive on schedule looks perfectly healthy.',
      'coalesce(days_since_backup, 999) treats "never backed up" as 999 days rather than as unknown — deliberately, because for a backup the safe reading of no evidence is the alarming one.',
      'The Dropbox side is reachable. A backup written locally but never mirrored still ages this counter correctly and still leaves nothing off-site.'),
    'This is the only rule here that protects against total loss. Everything else on this board is tidiness; a stale backup means a bad day becomes an unrecoverable one.',
    'No spend — the backup job and the Dropbox quota are already paid for. The cost of being wrong is the entire company''s records.');

  perform doc_rec('oversized', coalesce(k.oversized,0) > 0, 'low', 'Oversized files',
    k.oversized||' file(s) exceed 30MB. Consider compressing or archiving to control storage cost.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'Size is a proxy for waste. A 40MB drawing set is large because it is a drawing set, and compressing it can destroy exactly the detail a supplier needs to price the job.',
      '30MB is a chosen threshold, not a limit anything enforces — nothing breaks at 31MB.'),
    'Marginal. At this volume the storage saving is pennies; the honest value is spotting an upload path that is storing something it should not, such as an unresized original.',
    'No spend. Compressing costs engineering time and risks degrading a customer''s drawing, which is why this is the lowest-risk item on the board and stays a suggestion.');

  select count(*) into n from agent_actions where agent='document_controller' and status in ('pending','needs_review');
  return jsonb_build_object('ran_at',now(),'doc_health',v_health,'kpis',to_jsonb(k),'open_tasks',n);
end
fn_ws_reports:
select jsonb_build_object(
    'kpis', (select to_jsonb(k) from public.report_kpis k),
    -- THE LATEST EXECUTIVE MEETING, IN SEQUENCE. exec_reports.findings is the ordered transcript of
    -- what each of the ten officers said; report_registry projects only title/period/id, so until
    -- now the body reached nothing the browser could run. `contributions` keeps the array order
    -- the meeting wrote it in — that order IS the replay.
    'meeting', (select jsonb_build_object(
        'id', r.id, 'period', r.period, 'officer', r.officer, 'summary', r.summary,

        'contributions', coalesce(r.findings, '[]'::jsonb),

              'proposal', c.proposal, 'by', c.challenged_by, 'of', c.proposed_by,

          from public.report_registry where created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at() order by report_type, created_at desc
        ) x order by report_type) t),
    'flags', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(f), '[]'::jsonb) from (
        select title, risk, status, to_char(created_at,'YYYY-MM-DD') as created

fn_strategy_risk:
begin
  insert into public.strategy_risks(category,title,likelihood,impact,mitigation)
  values (p_cat,p_title, greatest(1,least(5,p_like)), greatest(1,least(5,p_impact)), p_mit)

    set likelihood=excluded.likelihood, impact=excluded.impact, mitigation=excluded.mitigation, updated_at=now();

fn_strategy_ai:
declare k record; r record; v_recs int := 0;
begin
  perform public.fn_strategy_scan();               -- refresh internal risk signals
  select * into k from public.strategy_kpis;
  insert into public.strategy_kpi_snapshots(kpis) values (to_jsonb(k));

  -- Recommend on material open risks (score >= 12)
  for r in select category,title,score,mitigation from public.strategy_risks
           where status='open' and score >= 12 order by score desc loop
    perform public.fn_strategy_rec('Strategic risk: '||r.title,
      case when r.score>=16 then 'high' else 'medium' end,
      '['||upper(r.category)||' · risk score '||r.score||'/25] '||coalesce(r.mitigation,'Review and decide a mitigation.'),
      jsonb_build_array(
        'The score of '||r.score||'/25 is a self-assessment stored on strategy_risks by whatever raised the risk. It has not been independently reviewed, and 12/25 is a threshold on that self-assessment rather than on measured exposure.',
        'status=''open'' means nobody has closed the row. A risk that has already passed looks identical to one that is still live until someone closes it.',
        case when r.mitigation is null then 'No mitigation is stored with this risk, so the recommendation asks for one rather than proposing one.'
             else 'The mitigation quoted here is the text stored with the risk when it was raised; it may predate the current situation.' end),
      'Deciding it removes the risk this company has scored highest. Left open, the only thing that changes is the score.',
      'No spend to decide. The mitigation itself may cost - that is stated on the strategy_risks row, not here.');
    v_recs := v_recs + 1;
  end loop;

  -- Expansion signal: under-supplied high-demand categories
  if coalesce(k.under_supplied_categories,0) > 0 then
    perform public.fn_strategy_rec('Expansion: recruit suppliers in under-supplied categories','medium',
      k.under_supplied_categories||' categories have demand outstripping supplier coverage. Targeted supplier acquisition here is the highest-ROI growth lever — see the Marketplace supply-gap list.',
      jsonb_build_array(
        'Under-supplied compares demand signals against CONFIRMED supplier coverage per category. With '||(select count(*) from public.leads where coalesce(claimed,false))||' confirmed supplier(s) on file, nearly every category qualifies, so this count currently says more about supply than about demand.',
        'Coverage is counted through the catalogue''s own taxonomy: a supplier who serves a category but has not declared it counts as absent.',
        'It assumes the demand signal is real demand. With 0 inquiries to date the signal is derived from catalogue structure and lead distribution, not from customers asking.'),
      'Supply is the binding constraint on revenue: an RFQ in a category with no supplier cannot be quoted at all, so the request is lost before pricing ever matters.',
      'No spend to decide. Recruiting costs invitation volume and sending reputation, which the invite ramp governs and caps.');
  end if;

  -- Pricing: standing review of the reveal fee vs average job value (recommend, never change)
  perform public.fn_strategy_rec('Pricing review: reveal fee vs average job value','low',
    'Periodically re-test the reveal fee and supplier registration pricing against average job value and willingness-to-pay. Use fn_simulate to model options before any change — pricing changes stay a founder decision.',
    jsonb_build_array(
      'That the live prices are the ones in pricing_config and have not been overridden for an individual customer or supplier.',
      'That average job value can be estimated at all. With no completed jobs on file there is nothing to estimate from, so this is a standing reminder rather than a finding about the current price.',
      'That willingness-to-pay is unknown rather than zero: nobody has been asked to pay the reveal fee yet.'),
    'Pricing is the only lever that changes revenue without changing volume. Untested, today''s fee hardens into a default that nobody ever chose.',
    'No spend. A founder decision; fn_simulate models the options first and costs one model call.');

  -- Market intelligence gap
  if coalesce(k.competitor_intel,0) = 0 then
    perform public.fn_strategy_rec('Add a competitor / market-intelligence source','medium',
      'No competitor records on file (market_intel is empty). Connect a web-research or market-data source, or add competitors manually, so positioning, pricing and expansion calls are evidence-based rather than assumed.',
      jsonb_build_array(
        'An empty market_intel means no competitor has been RECORDED. It is not evidence that no competitor exists, and it is the weaker of the two readings.',
        'That positioning and pricing calls are currently being made without competitor evidence. That follows from the table being empty, but it does not prove the founder holds no such knowledge outside the system.',
        'That a usable source exists for this market. UAE marketplace competitors may not publish the pricing that would make the comparison decisive.'),
      'Every positioning, pricing and expansion decision is currently taken with no recorded evidence about anyone else in this market.',
      'A market-data source or web-research subscription costs money and needs founder approval. Adding competitors by hand costs founder time and nothing else.');
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('open_risks',k.open_risks,'top_risk',k.top_risk,'top_risk_score',k.top_risk_score,
    'new_or_open_recs', v_recs, 'competitor_intel', k.competitor_intel, 'under_supplied', k.under_supplied_categories);
end

fn_edit_inquiry:
declare
  v inquiries%rowtype; v_paid boolean; v_deadline timestamptz;
  v_material boolean := false; v_reason text; v_stale int := 0; v_notified int := 0;
  v_cust_email text; v_admin text;
begin
  select * into v from inquiries where id=p_inquiry;
  if not found then return jsonb_build_object('error','inquiry_not_found'); end if;
  if p_customer is not null and v.customer_id is distinct from p_customer then
    return jsonb_build_object('error','not_your_inquiry'); end if;
  select exists(select 1 from transactions where inquiry_id=p_inquiry) into v_paid;
  if v_paid or v.status in ('revealed','completed','cancelled','closed') or v.pipeline_stage in ('revealed','won','cancelled') then
    return jsonb_build_object('error','not_editable','status',v.status,
      'message','This request can no longer be edited.'); end if;
  v_deadline := v.created_at + interval '1 hour';
  if now() > v_deadline then
    return jsonb_build_object('error','edit_window_closed','editable_until',v_deadline,
      'message','Inquiries can be edited within 1 hour of submitting. Please create a new request for changes after that.'); end if;

  -- Decide materiality BEFORE the update, while the old row is still in hand.
  v_material :=
       (p_patch ? 'spec'       and (p_patch->'spec')       is distinct from v.spec)
    or (p_patch ? 'boq'        and (p_patch->'boq')        is distinct from v.boq)
    or (p_patch ? 'budget'     and (p_patch->>'budget')    is distinct from v.budget)
    or (p_patch ? 'scope_type' and (p_patch->>'scope_type') is distinct from v.scope_type)
    or (p_patch ? 'emirate'    and (p_patch->>'emirate')   is distinct from v.emirate)
    or (p_patch ? 'trades'     and array(select jsonb_array_elements_text(p_patch->'trades')) is distinct from v.trades);

  update inquiries set
    summary   = coalesce(p_patch->>'summary', summary),
    raw_input = coalesce(p_patch->>'raw_input', raw_input),
    budget    = coalesce(p_patch->>'budget', budget),
    emirate   = coalesce(p_patch->>'emirate', emirate),
    scope_type= coalesce(p_patch->>'scope_type', scope_type),
    spec      = case when p_patch ? 'spec' then p_patch->'spec' else spec end,
    boq       = case when p_patch ? 'boq' then p_patch->'boq' else boq end,
    trades    = case when p_patch ? 'trades' then array(select jsonb_array_elements_text(p_patch->'trades')) else trades end,
    keywords  = case when p_patch ? 'keywords' then array(select jsonb_array_elements_text(p_patch->'keywords')) else keywords end
    where id=p_inquiry;

  if v_material then
    v_reason := 'The customer changed the requirements of this request on '
             || to_char(now() at time zone 'Asia/Dubai','DD Mon YYYY HH24:MI')
             || ' (Dubai), after this quote was submitted.';

    -- Stale the live quotes and tell each supplier, in one statement so a quote can never be
    -- reverted without its supplier being told.
    with staled as (
      update quotes q
         set stale_at = now(), stale_reason = v_reason, status = 'draft'
       where q.inquiry_id = p_inquiry
         and q.stale_at is null
         and coalesce(q.status,'') in ('submitted','draft')
      returning q.id, q.supplier_id
    ),
    told as (
      insert into notifications(type, to_email, to_role, lead_id, inquiry_id, quote_id, channel, subject, body, status)
      select 'quote_requirements_changed',
             coalesce(l.claimed_by, l.email), 'supplier', s.supplier_id, p_inquiry, s.id, 'email',
             'The customer changed this request — please re-quote',
             'Hello ' || coalesce(l.company_name,'') || ',' || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
             'A customer has changed the requirements of a request you had already quoted, so your quote has been set back to draft and is no longer being shown to them.' || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
             v_reason || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
             'Please open the request in your supplier portal, review what changed, and submit an updated quote. Your original figures are still there — nothing has been deleted.' || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
             'QuotesDone',
             'queued'
        from staled s join leads l on l.id = s.supplier_id
       where coalesce(l.claimed_by, l.email) is not null
      returning 1
    )
    select (select count(*) from staled), (select count(*) from told) into v_stale, v_notified;

    if v_stale > 0 then
      select email into v_cust_email from customers where id = v.customer_id;
      v_admin := coalesce((select split_part(value,',',1) from app_secrets where key='admin_emails'),
                          'management@quotesdone.com');

      -- The customer must know their edit cost them their quotes, or they will wait for prices
      -- that are never coming back on their own.
      if v_cust_email is not null then
        insert into notifications(type, to_email, to_role, inquiry_id, channel, subject, body, status)
        values ('inquiry_edit_staled_quotes', v_cust_email, 'customer', p_inquiry, 'email',
                'Your change means we have asked for fresh prices',
                'Hello,' || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
                'You changed the requirements on your request, so the ' || v_stale ||
                ' quote(s) already submitted no longer match what you are asking for. We have asked those suppliers to re-quote against your updated requirements.' || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
                'You do not need to do anything — the new prices will appear as they arrive.' || chr(10) || chr(10) ||
                'QuotesDone', 'queued');
      end if;

      insert into agent_actions(agent, kind, status, risk, title, recommendation, detail, target_table, target_id)
      values ('procurement','requote_required','needs_review','medium',
              'Requirements changed after ' || v_stale || ' quote(s) were submitted',
              'Watch that the invited suppliers actually re-quote. If they do not, the customer is left with a request that had prices and now has none.',
              jsonb_build_object('inquiry_id', p_inquiry, 'quotes_staled', v_stale,
                                 'suppliers_notified', v_notified, 'changed_at', now()),
              'inquiries', p_inquiry::text);
    end if;
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('ok',true,'edited',true,'editable_until',v_deadline,
                            'material_change', v_material,
                            'quotes_staled', v_stale,
                            'suppliers_notified', v_notified);
end
fn_enqueue_doc_backups:
declare n integer := 0; m integer;
begin
  with s as (
    select l.*,
      '/QuotesDone Backup/Suppliers/'
        || public.fn_dbx_category(l.id)
        || '/' || fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(l.company_name,'Supplier')) || ' (' || l.id || ')/' as base
    from public.leads l
    where l.approved_at is not null or l.registration_submitted_at is not null
       or l.signed_terms_path is not null or l.company_profile_doc_path is not null
       or l.license_doc_path is not null or coalesce(l.claimed,false)
  ),
  sd as (
    select s.id, s.base, v.doc_type, v.bucket, v.path
    from s cross join lateral (values
      ('Trade licence','supplier-docs', s.license_doc_path),
      ('Bank IBAN','supplier-docs', s.iban_doc_path),
      ('Establishment card','supplier-docs', s.egr_doc_path),
      ('Insurance','supplier-docs', s.insurance_doc_path),
      ('VAT certificate','supplier-docs', s.vat_doc_path),
      ('ISO certificate','supplier-docs', s.iso_doc_path),
      ('Manufacturer authorization','supplier-docs', s.manufacturer_auth_doc_path),
      ('Company profile','supplier-docs', s.company_profile_doc_path),
      ('Signed Terms & Conditions','signed-terms', s.signed_terms_path)
    ) v(doc_type,bucket,path)
    where v.path is not null and length(v.path)>0
  )
  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,bucket,path,file_name,dropbox_path,source,dedupe_key)
  select 'supplier', sd.id::text, sd.doc_type, sd.bucket, sd.path,
         regexp_replace(sd.path,'^.*/',''),
         sd.base || sd.doc_type || ' - ' || regexp_replace(sd.path,'^.*/',''),
         'storage', 'S:'||sd.id||':'||sd.doc_type||':'||sd.path
  from sd on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,bucket,path,file_name,dropbox_path,source,dedupe_key)
  select 'supplier', s.id::text, 'Catalogue', 'supplier-docs', cat,
         regexp_replace(cat,'^.*/',''), s.base || 'Catalogue - ' || regexp_replace(cat,'^.*/',''),
         'storage', 'S:'||s.id||':cat:'||cat
  from ( select l.id,
      '/QuotesDone Backup/Suppliers/'
        || public.fn_dbx_category(l.id)
        || '/' || fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(l.company_name,'Supplier')) || ' (' || l.id || ')/' as base, l.catalog_doc_paths
    from public.leads l
    where (l.approved_at is not null or l.registration_submitted_at is not null
       or l.signed_terms_path is not null or l.company_profile_doc_path is not null
       or l.license_doc_path is not null or coalesce(l.claimed,false)) and l.catalog_doc_paths is not null ) s,
    unnest(s.catalog_doc_paths) cat
  where cat is not null and length(cat)>0 on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,source,gen_kind,gen_ref,dropbox_path,dedupe_key)
  select 'supplier', s.id::text, 'Company Details','generated','supplier_details', s.id::text,
         s.base || 'Company Details.pdf', 'S:'||s.id||':details'
  from ( select l.id,
      '/QuotesDone Backup/Suppliers/'
        || public.fn_dbx_category(l.id)
        || '/' || fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(l.company_name,'Supplier')) || ' (' || l.id || ')/' as base
    from public.leads l
    where l.approved_at is not null or l.registration_submitted_at is not null
       or l.signed_terms_path is not null or l.company_profile_doc_path is not null
       or l.license_doc_path is not null or coalesce(l.claimed,false) ) s
  on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,bucket,path,file_name,dropbox_path,source,dedupe_key)
  select 'customer', c.id::text, 'Signed Terms & Conditions','signed-terms', c.signed_terms_path,
         regexp_replace(c.signed_terms_path,'^.*/',''),
         '/QuotesDone Backup/Customers/'||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(c.full_name,'Customer'))||' ('||left(c.id::text,8)||')/Signed Terms & Conditions - '||regexp_replace(c.signed_terms_path,'^.*/',''),
         'storage', 'C:'||c.id||':terms:'||c.signed_terms_path
  from public.customers c where c.signed_terms_path is not null and length(c.signed_terms_path)>0
  on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,source,gen_kind,gen_ref,dropbox_path,dedupe_key)
  select 'customer', c.id::text, 'Customer Details','generated','customer_details', c.id::text,
         '/QuotesDone Backup/Customers/'||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(c.full_name,'Customer'))||' ('||left(c.id::text,8)||')/Customer Details.pdf',
         'C:'||c.id||':details'
  from public.customers c on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,bucket,path,file_name,dropbox_path,source,dedupe_key)
  select 'inquiry', i.id::text, 'RFQ drawing','drawing-files', i.drawing_file_path,
         coalesce(i.drawing_file_name, regexp_replace(i.drawing_file_path,'^.*/','')),
         '/QuotesDone Backup/Customers/'||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(c.full_name,'Customer'))||' ('||left(c.id::text,8)||')/Inquiries/'
           || to_char(i.created_at,'YYYY-MM-DD')||' '||left(i.id::text,8)||' - '||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(i.status,'inquiry'))
           || '/Drawing - '||coalesce(i.drawing_file_name, regexp_replace(i.drawing_file_path,'^.*/','')),
         'storage', 'I:'||i.id||':drawing:'||i.drawing_file_path
  from public.inquiries i join public.customers c on c.id=i.customer_id
  where i.drawing_file_path is not null and length(i.drawing_file_path)>0
  on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,source,gen_kind,gen_ref,dropbox_path,dedupe_key)
  select 'inquiry', i.id::text, 'Inquiry Summary','generated','inquiry_summary', i.id::text,
         '/QuotesDone Backup/Customers/'||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(c.full_name,'Customer'))||' ('||left(c.id::text,8)||')/Inquiries/'
           || to_char(i.created_at,'YYYY-MM-DD')||' '||left(i.id::text,8)||' - '||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(i.status,'inquiry'))
           || '/Inquiry Summary.pdf', 'I:'||i.id||':summary'
  from public.inquiries i join public.customers c on c.id=i.customer_id
  on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  -- Quote comparison reports: one PDF per distinct quote-set (>=2 live quotes). Anonymized A/B/C.
  insert into public.doc_backups(entity,entity_id,doc_type,source,gen_kind,gen_ref,dropbox_path,dedupe_key)
  select 'inquiry', i.id::text, 'Quote Comparison','generated','comparison', i.id::text,
         '/QuotesDone Backup/Customers/'||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(c.full_name,'Customer'))||' ('||left(c.id::text,8)||')/Inquiries/'
           || to_char(i.created_at,'YYYY-MM-DD')||' '||left(i.id::text,8)||' - '||fn_dbx_safe(coalesce(i.status,'inquiry'))
           || '/Quote Comparison Report '||to_char(now(),'YYYY-MM-DD')||' '||left(sig.sig,8)||'.pdf',
         'CMP:'||i.id||':'||sig.sig
  from public.inquiries i
  join public.customers c on c.id=i.customer_id
  join lateral ( select md5(coalesce(string_agg(q.quote_amount::text||':'||coalesce(q.status,''),'|' order by q.quote_amount),'')) as sig,
                        count(*) as nq
                 from public.quotes q where q.inquiry_id=i.id and q.status<>'draft' ) sig on true
  where sig.nq >= 2
  on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing;
  get diagnostics m = row_count; n := n + m;

  return n;
end
fn_dues_to_escalate:
select d.id, d.supplier_id, d.amount_due, coalesce(d.currency,'AED'), d.reveal_date, d.due_date::date,
         (current_date - d.due_date::date) as days_overdue,
         l.company_name, l.contact_name, coalesce(l.claimed_by,l.email) as email, coalesce(l.phone_e164,l.phone),
         l.trade_license_no, l.emirate,
         coalesce(nullif(btrim(split_part(coalesce(l.categories,''),',',1)),''), nullif(l.sector,''),'Uncategorized') as category,
         l.signed_terms_path, l.claimed_by, l.accepted_terms_at

  join public.leads l on l.id = d.supplier_id

fn_backup_watch:
declare v_last timestamptz; v_status text; v_stale boolean; v_owner text; v_open int;
begin
  select started_at, status into v_last, v_status
    from agent_runs where agent='backup' order by started_at desc limit 1;
  v_stale := (v_last is null) or (v_last < now() - interval '26 hours') or (coalesce(v_status,'')='error');
  if not v_stale then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok',true,'last',v_last,'status',v_status);
  end if;
  select count(*) into v_open from agent_actions
    where kind='backup_alert' and coalesce(status,'') in ('pending','needs_review')
  -- A DEDUPE WINDOW THE SAME LENGTH AS THE CHECK INTERVAL SUPPRESSES ON A KNIFE EDGE (13 Aug 2026).
  -- The backup was broken from 10 to 12 August and this watcher produced exactly ONE alert:
  -- agent_action 2662 at 2026-08-11 08:00:00.63, one email, still pending. The watcher runs daily
  -- at 08:00, and the previous row was 24 hours old minus a fraction of a second, so it was still
  -- inside `created_at > now() - 24 hours` and the second day's alert was skipped. Twenty hours is
  -- strictly shorter than the cadence, so a daily check always re-alerts on a continuing outage
  -- while a ten-minute caller still cannot spam.
      and created_at > now()-interval '20 hours';

  if v_open = 0 then
    insert into agent_actions(agent,kind,status,risk,title,recommendation,target_table,detail)
    values('security','backup_alert','pending','high',
      'Backup may have failed or is overdue',
      'The daily logical backup has not completed successfully in the last 26 hours (last: '||coalesce(v_last::text,'never')||', status: '||coalesce(v_status,'unknown')||'). Check the backup function and logs. Managed daily backups and the Dropbox mirror remain as fallbacks.',
      'agent_runs', jsonb_build_object('last_backup',v_last,'last_status',v_status));
    insert into security_events(kind,severity,source,subject,detail)
    values('backup_overdue','high','backup','logical backup',
      jsonb_build_object('last_backup',v_last,'last_status',v_status));
    select split_part(coalesce(value,'management@quotesdone.com'),',',1) into v_owner
      from app_secrets where key='admin_emails';
    insert into notifications(type,to_email,to_role,channel,subject,body,status)
    values('backup_alert', v_owner, 'admin','email','QuotesDone: backup overdue or failed',
      'The daily logical backup has not completed in the last 26 hours (last: '||coalesce(v_last::text,'never')||', status: '||coalesce(v_status,'unknown')||'). Please check. Managed daily backups + the Dropbox mirror remain as fallbacks.','queued');
    -- AN OUTAGE THAT LASTS MUST GET LOUDER, NOT REPEAT ITSELF. One identical email a day says the
    -- same thing on day one and on day five, and the day-five reader has already filed the day-one
    -- copy. Past 48 hours this also raises a founder_alert and states the age in hours, which is
    -- the number that decides whether this is a hiccup or a company with no restorable backup.
    if v_last is null or v_last < now() - interval '48 hours' then
      insert into founder_alerts(level,event,detail,channel)
      values('crit','backup_outage_prolonged',
        'The daily logical backup has now been failing for '
        || coalesce(round(extract(epoch from (now()-v_last))/3600)::text || ' hours', 'as long as there are records')
        || ' (last run: '||coalesce(v_last::text,'never')||', status: '||coalesce(v_status,'unknown')
        || '). This is past the point where one more day of silence is acceptable: verify the backup '
        || 'function itself, then run dr_drill to prove the newest backup still restores.','system');
    end if;

  end if;
  return jsonb_build_object('alerted',true,'last',v_last,'status',v_status,'existing_open',v_open);
end
kb_match:
with want as (
    select nullif(regexp_replace(lower(p_category),'^cat:',''),'') as c
  ), cats as (
    select c as cat from want where c is not null
    union
    select a.maps_to from kb_category_aliases a, want w where a.category = w.c
  ), src as materialized (
    select k.id, k.category, k.title, k.citation, k.content, k.embedding_gte
    from public.kb_chunks k
    where k.embedding_gte is not null
      and ((select c from want) is null or k.category_norm in (select cat from cats))
  )
  select s.id, s.category, s.title, s.citation, s.content,
         1 - (s.embedding_gte <=> query_embedding) as similarity
  from src s
  order by s.embedding_gte <=> query_embedding
  limit match_count;
fn_ai_quality_watch:
declare v_regs int:=0; v_spikes int:=0; v_detail jsonb; v_open int; v_owner text; v_t0 timestamptz := now();
begin
  -- ONE ROW PER AGENT PER NIGHT. Resolved to the canonical key here rather than left to the BEFORE
  -- INSERT trigger, because the trigger fires per row and therefore turns N raw agents into N rows
  -- that all claim the same identity. The rate is recomputed from the underlying counts, never
  -- averaged from the per-row percentages.
  insert into public.ai_quality_snapshots(agent, override_pct, actions_30d)
  select k.agent,
         round(100.0 * sum(v.rejected_30d)::numeric / nullif(sum(v.actions_30d), 0), 1),
         sum(v.actions_30d)::int
    from public.v_ai_agent_health v
    cross join lateral (select case
             when exists (select 1 from public.org_agents o where o.agent_key = v.agent and o.active)
               then v.agent
             else coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(v.agent), v.agent)
           end as agent) k
   where v.override_pct is not null
   group by k.agent
  having sum(v.actions_30d) > 0;

  with ranked as (
    select prompt_key, score, created_at,
           row_number() over(partition by prompt_key order by created_at desc) rn
    from public.prompt_eval_runs
  ),
  reg as (
    select c.prompt_key, c.score cur, p.score prev
    from ranked c join ranked p on p.prompt_key=c.prompt_key and p.rn=2
    where c.rn=1 and (c.score < p.score - 5 or c.score < 70)
  ),
  ins as (
    insert into public.security_events(kind,severity,source,subject,detail)
    select 'eval_regression', case when cur<70 then 'high' else 'medium' end, 'ai_quality_watch', prompt_key,
           jsonb_build_object('current',cur,'previous',prev)
    from reg returning 1
  )
  select count(*) into v_regs from ins;

  with cur as (
    -- Same resolution rule as the insert above, so `cur` and `hist` speak one vocabulary. Before
    -- this, 17 of 52 agents carried a raw name here and a canonical one in the snapshot, and the
    -- join below could not match them at all.
    select k.agent,
           round(100.0 * sum(v.rejected_30d)::numeric / nullif(sum(v.actions_30d), 0), 1) as override_pct,
           sum(v.actions_30d)::int as actions_30d
      from public.v_ai_agent_health v
      cross join lateral (select case
               when exists (select 1 from public.org_agents o where o.agent_key = v.agent and o.active)
                 then v.agent
               else coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(v.agent), v.agent)
             end as agent) k
     where v.override_pct is not null
     group by k.agent
    having sum(v.actions_30d) >= 5
       and k.agent not in ('security','onboarding','email')
  ),
  hist as (
    -- Weighted by actions, not a flat mean of percentages: the historical rows still contain the
    -- pre-fix duplicates, and a flat avg lets an agent with one action in a month move the trailing
    -- average as much as one with a hundred and sixty.
    select agent,
           sum(override_pct * greatest(actions_30d, 1))::numeric / nullif(sum(greatest(actions_30d, 1)), 0) as avg_prev,
           count(*) n
    from public.ai_quality_snapshots where at < now()-interval '12 hours' group by agent
  ),
  spike as (
    select c.agent, c.override_pct, round(h.avg_prev,1) avg_prev
    from cur c join hist h on h.agent=c.agent
    where h.n>=1 and c.override_pct > coalesce(h.avg_prev,0)+20
  ),
  ins2 as (
    insert into public.security_events(kind,severity,source,subject,detail)
    select 'override_spike','medium','ai_quality_watch', agent,
           jsonb_build_object('override_pct',override_pct,'trailing_avg',avg_prev)
    from spike returning 1
  )
  select count(*) into v_spikes from ins2;

  v_detail := jsonb_build_object('eval_regressions',v_regs,'override_spikes',v_spikes);

  -- Added 10 Aug 2026: this routine has detected quality falling since it was written and never
  -- emitted an event, so nothing downstream could react to it.
  if v_regs + v_spikes > 0 then
    perform fn_emit('ai.confidence_dropped',
                    case when se.kind='eval_regression' then 'prompt' else 'agent' end,
                    se.subject, 'ai_quality_watch',
                    se.detail || jsonb_build_object('finding', se.kind, 'severity', se.severity))
       from public.security_events se
      where se.source='ai_quality_watch' and se.kind in ('eval_regression','override_spike')
        and se.created_at >= v_t0;
  end if;

  if v_regs+v_spikes > 0 then
    select count(*) into v_open from public.agent_actions
      where kind='ai_quality_alert' and coalesce(status,'') in ('pending','needs_review')
        and created_at > now()-interval '24 hours';
    if v_open = 0 then
      insert into public.agent_actions(agent,kind,status,risk,title,recommendation,target_table,detail)
      values('ai_trainer','ai_quality_alert','pending','medium',
        'AI quality alert: '||v_regs||' eval regression(s), '||v_spikes||' override spike(s)',
        'Open the AI Observability dashboard and review security_events of kind eval_regression / override_spike. Consider rolling back the regressed prompt version, or investigating why a human-facing agent''s suggestions are being rejected.',
        'security_events', v_detail);
      select split_part(coalesce(value,'management@quotesdone.com'),',',1) into v_owner
        from public.app_secrets where key='admin_emails';
      insert into public.notifications(type,to_email,to_role,channel,subject,body,status)
      values('ai_quality_alert', v_owner,'admin','email','QuotesDone: AI quality alert',
        'The AI quality watch flagged '||v_regs||' eval regression(s) and '||v_spikes||' override spike(s). Open the AI Observability dashboard and check security_events (kind eval_regression / override_spike).','queued');
    end if;
  end if;
  return v_detail;
end

Suppliers put real effort into quoting, so please only post jobs you intend to follow through on. Repeated cancellations may temporarily pause your account. Thank you for understanding.'
      from customers c where c.id = NEW.customer_id and c.email like '%@%';

declare

  for r in

    from inquiries i
    where i.status = 'sent'
      and i.created_at < (now() - make_interval(hours => v_hours))
      and coalesce(i.scope_type,'') <> 'combined'
      and not exists (
        select 1 from quotes q where q.inquiry_id = i.id
          and coalesce(q.status,'') not in ('draft','rejected','void','cancelled'))
      and not exists (
        select 1 from founder_alerts fa where fa.event='rfq_sla_breach'
          and fa.detail like ('%inquiry '||i.id||':%')
          and fa.created_at > (now() - interval '48 hours'))
    order by i.created_at asc
    limit 50
  loop
    insert into founder_alerts(level, event, detail, channel)
      values('warn','rfq_sla_breach',
        'inquiry '||r.id||': no supplier quote after '||v_hours||'h ('||coalesce(r.category,'?')||' / '||coalesce(r.emirate,'?')||'). Widen the pool or recruit this category.',
        'system');
    insert into notifications(type, to_email, to_role, channel, subject, body, status)
      values('rfq_sla_breach', v_admin, 'admin', 'email',
        'RFQ past SLA — no quotes yet',
        'Inquiry #'||r.id||' ('||coalesce(r.category,'?')||' in '||coalesce(r.emirate,'?')||') has had NO supplier quote for over '||v_hours||' hours. Consider widening the emirate/trade or recruiting suppliers in this category. Open it in the OS to re-dispatch.',
        'queued');
    -- Added 10 Aug 2026. The founder was told and Operations was not, because this routine has
    -- never put anything on the bus.
    perform fn_emit('sla.breached', 'inquiry', r.id::text, 'sla_watch',
      jsonb_build_object('sla_hours', v_hours, 'category', r.category, 'emirate', r.emirate,
