  -- mistake sat in supplier_onboard's telemetry inside a try/catch, where it failed silently for a
  -- day: a swallowed write looks exactly like a feature nobody used.
  insert into public.agent_actions (agent, kind, status, risk, title, detail, assumptions, expected_impact, cost)
  values ('supplier_risk_monitor', v_kind, 'logged',
    case when jsonb_array_length(v_findings) > 0 then 'medium' else 'low' end,
    'Supplier risk scan: ' || p_signal,
    jsonb_build_object('signal', p_signal, 'snapshot', v_now, 'findings', v_findings,
      'comparable', not v_first,
      'note', case when v_first and p_signal = 'performance_drops'
                   then 'first run — a drop needs a previous snapshot, so nothing was compared'
                   else null end),
    -- s36 (13 Aug 2026): what this scan TOOK ON TRUST. The comments in each branch above already
    -- stated it; the row did not carry it, so a reader of the row could not know that
    -- "complaints" is two proxies rather than a complaints table.
    case p_signal
      when 'complaints' then jsonb_build_array(
        'There is no complaints table. This counts two proxies: refunds requested against a supplier, and messages a human or a filter flagged. A dissatisfied customer who neither asked for money back nor was flagged is invisible to it.',
        'A refund request is treated as a complaint about the supplier. Some are about the platform, the price or a change of mind, and this cannot tell them apart.',
        'Flagging is done by whatever set messages.flagged; its precision is not measured here.')
      when 'response_delays' then jsonb_build_array(
        'Slow means slower than the MEDIAN supplier with a measured response time, so half the measured population is flagged by construction and the count says more about the spread than about any threshold.',
        'Suppliers with no avg_response_hours are absent, not fast. A supplier who has never answered anything cannot be slow by this measure.',
        'It assumes avg_response_hours is current; it is whatever supplier_score last computed.')
      else jsonb_build_array(
        'A drop is measured against the PREVIOUS run of this scan, not against a baseline, so a slow decline over many runs never shows as a drop.',
        'avg_reliability averages over suppliers who have a reliability at all; a supplier scored for the first time moves the average without anything changing.',
        case when v_first then 'This is the first run: there was no earlier snapshot, so nothing was compared and no finding here means "could not look", not "looked and found nothing".'
             else 'A previous snapshot existed, so the comparison was genuinely made.' end)
    end,
    case p_signal
      when 'complaints' then 'Each finding is a supplier a customer has asked for money back from and nobody has resolved. Left alone it becomes a refund the platform pays for and a supplier the matcher keeps sending work to.'
      when 'response_delays' then 'A supplier slower than the median is one an RFQ waits on. On a marketplace whose promise is speed, that delay is the product failing quietly.'
      else 'A fall in average reliability is the marketplace getting worse at the one thing a buyer cannot verify themselves before paying.'
    end,
    'No spend. The scan is SQL over existing rows; acting on a finding costs the time to contact a supplier, and in the complaints case may cost a refund, which is the founder''s decision.');

  return jsonb_build_object('signal', p_signal, 'snapshot', v_now,
    'findings', v_findings, 'comparable', not v_first);
end
fn_supplier_negotiation:
with q as (
    select id, inquiry_id, supplier_id, quote_amount, margin_rate, app_fee, customer_price, lead_time, warranty
      from public.quotes where id = p_quote_id
  ),
  -- The inbound side of the conversation only. What the supplier said is not evidence of pressure.
  inbound as (
    select m.id, m.body, m.created_at
      from public.messages m join q on q.inquiry_id = m.inquiry_id and q.supplier_id = m.supplier_id
     where m.sender = 'customer' order by m.created_at desc limit 10
  ),
  scen as (
    select v.pct,
           round((select quote_amount from q) * (1 - v.pct / 100.0), 2) new_quote,
           round((select quote_amount from q) * (1 - v.pct / 100.0)
                 * (1 + coalesce((select margin_rate from q), 0)), 2) new_customer_price,
           round((select quote_amount from q) * (v.pct / 100.0), 2) you_give_up
      from (values (3), (5), (10)) v(pct)
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'quote_id', p_quote_id,
    -- The thread this quote belongs to. Returned because the drafted reply has to be SENDABLE, and
    -- messages_api keys a thread on (inquiry_id, supplier_id) — without both, the draft is a
    -- suggestion the supplier has to retype somewhere else.
    'inquiry_id', (select inquiry_id from q),
    'supplier_id', (select supplier_id from q),
    'quote_amount', (select quote_amount from q),
    'customer_price', (select customer_price from q),
    -- THE PLATFORM'S margin, named as such. app_fee / quote_amount is QuotesDone's cut, and calling
    -- it "your margin" would be a lie by label.
    'margin', jsonb_build_object(
      'whose', 'platform',
      'app_fee', (select app_fee from q),
      'margin_rate', (select margin_rate from q),
      'note', 'This is the QuotesDone fee on the reveal, not your profit.'),
    'supplier_cost_known', false,
    'possible_reduction', jsonb_build_object(
      'available', false,
      'why', 'QuotesDone does not know what this job costs you to deliver, so it cannot tell you how far you can go. The scenarios below are arithmetic, not advice.',
      'scenarios', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'reduction_pct', s.pct, 'you_receive', s.new_quote,
          'customer_pays', s.new_customer_price, 'you_give_up', s.you_give_up)
        order by s.pct) from scen s), '[]'::jsonb)),
    'inbound_messages', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'id', i.id, 'body', i.body, 'created_at', i.created_at) order by i.created_at desc)
      from inbound i), '[]'::jsonb),
    'population', jsonb_build_object(
      'customer_messages', (select count(*) from inbound),
      'note', case when (select count(*) from inbound) = 0
                   then 'the customer has not written anything yet, so there is no discount request to read'
                   else null end),
    'terms', jsonb_build_object('lead_time', (select lead_time from q), 'warranty', (select warranty from q))
  );
fn_supplier_certifications:
with me as (select * from public.leads where id = p_lead_id),
  docs as (
    select * from (values
      ('trade_licence',      'Trade licence',              'critical', 'Approval is impossible without it — the licence gate refuses every profile that has none.'),
      ('insurance',          'Insurance',                  'high',     'Many customers will not award work to an uninsured supplier.'),
      ('vat',                'VAT certificate',            'high',     'Needed before you can invoice with VAT.'),
      ('iso',               'ISO certification',           'medium',   'Strengthens your capability score and unlocks quality-gated requests.'),
      ('manufacturer_auth', 'Manufacturer authorisation',  'medium',   'Proves you are authorised for the brands you carry.'),
      ('establishment',     'Establishment card',          'low',      'Administrative record. Does not gate work.'),
      ('bank_iban',         'Bank details (IBAN)',         'medium',   'We cannot pay you without it.')
    ) d(key, label, impact, impact_why)
  ),
  held as (
    select d.key, d.label, d.impact, d.impact_why,
      case d.key
        when 'trade_licence'      then (select license_doc_path from me)
        when 'insurance'          then (select insurance_doc_path from me)
        when 'vat'                then (select vat_doc_path from me)
        when 'iso'                then (select iso_doc_path from me)
        when 'manufacturer_auth'  then (select manufacturer_auth_doc_path from me)
        when 'establishment'      then (select egr_doc_path from me)
        when 'bank_iban'          then (select iban_doc_path from me)
      end as path,
      case d.key
        when 'trade_licence'     then (select license_expiry from me)
        when 'insurance'         then (select insurance_expiry from me)
        when 'iso'               then (select iso_expiry from me)
        when 'manufacturer_auth' then (select manufacturer_auth_expiry from me)
        else null
      end::date as expiry
    from docs d
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'lead_id', p_lead_id,
    'certifications', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'key', h.key, 'label', h.label,
        'held', h.path is not null,
        'expiry', h.expiry,
        'days_left', case when h.expiry is null then null else (h.expiry - current_date) end,
        -- THE FIELD §16 ASKS FOR. A document with no expiry column is 'valid' when held: it does
        -- not expire, so calling it 'unknown' would invent a problem the supplier cannot fix.
        'document_status', case
          when h.path is null then 'missing'
          when h.expiry is null then 'valid'
          when h.expiry < current_date then 'expired'
          when h.expiry < current_date + 60 then 'expiring'
          else 'valid' end,
        'impact_level', h.impact,
        'impact_why', h.impact_why)
      order by case h.impact when 'critical' then 0 when 'high' then 1 when 'medium' then 2 else 3 end, h.label)
      from held h), '[]'::jsonb),
    'impact_basis', 'impact_level is a stated QuotesDone policy about what each document gates — not a number derived from your history',
    'summary', jsonb_build_object(
      'held', (select count(*) from held where path is not null),
      'total', (select count(*) from held),
      'expired', (select count(*) from held where path is not null and expiry is not null and expiry < current_date),
      'expiring', (select count(*) from held where path is not null and expiry is not null
                     and expiry >= current_date and expiry < current_date + 60),
      -- The one number that decides whether they can trade at all, surfaced on its own.
      'blocking_missing', (select count(*) from held where path is null and impact = 'critical'))
  );
fn_supplier_product_match:
with inq as (
    -- EVERYTHING THE CUSTOMER SAID, not the first field that happens to be non-empty. The first
    -- version preferred raw_input and fell back to summary, and on the demo enquiry that discarded
    -- the only line describing the work — every product scored 0% while the store held a curtain
    -- wall profile and the enquiry was for curtain walling. A brief's title carries meaning too,
    -- and dropping it to honour a precedence rule loses signal for nothing.
    select lower(coalesce(category, '')) cat,
           lower(concat_ws(' ', coalesce(summary, ''), coalesce(raw_input, ''), coalesce(category, ''))) want
      from public.inquiries where id = p_inquiry_id
  ),
  -- Words worth matching on. Anything under four characters is noise ("we", "for", "the"), and a
  -- stop list would be a maintenance burden for no gain at this size.
  terms as (
    select distinct w from inq, unnest(regexp_split_to_array(inq.want, '[^a-z0-9]+')) w
     where length(w) >= 4
  ),
  prod as (
    select p.id, p.name, p.brand, p.model, p.category_slug,
           lower(concat_ws(' ', p.name, p.brand, p.model, p.description, p.category_slug)) hay
      from public.supplier_product p
     where p.supplier_id = p_lead_id
  ),
  -- ── THE DENOMINATOR IS THE PRODUCT, NOT THE BRIEF ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Scoring matched-terms over ALL the brief's words made the exactly-right product read 6%:
  -- "Aluminium curtain wall profile" matched 2 of 32 words in a paragraph that also discussed
  -- square metres, retail units and powder coating. That understates as badly as an inflated score
  -- overstates, and a supplier seeing 6% on their best product would conclude the matching is
  -- broken — which it would be.
  --
  -- The question is not "how much of the brief does this product cover" (no single product covers
  -- a brief) but "how much of THIS PRODUCT does the brief ask for". Aluminium ✓ curtain ✓ wall ✓
  -- profile ✗ is a strong match, and reads as one.
  pterms as (
    select pr.id pid, w from prod pr,
      unnest(regexp_split_to_array(lower(concat_ws(' ', pr.name, pr.category_slug)), '[^a-z0-9]+')) w
     where length(w) >= 4
  ),
  hit as (
    select pr.id, pr.name, pr.brand, pr.model, pr.category_slug, pr.hay,
           (select count(*) from pterms pt, inq where pt.pid = pr.id and position(pt.w in inq.want) > 0) matched_terms,
           (select count(*) from pterms pt where pt.pid = pr.id) total_terms,
           (pr.category_slug is not null and pr.category_slug = (select cat from inq)) cat_hit,
           ((select cat from inq) <> '' and pr.category_slug is not null) cat_askable
      from prod pr
  ),
  scored as (
    select h.*,
      round(100.0 * (
          (case when h.cat_hit then 40 else 0 end)
        + (case when h.total_terms > 0 then 60.0 * h.matched_terms / h.total_terms else 0 end)
      ) / nullif((case when h.cat_askable then 40 else 0 end)
               + (case when h.total_terms > 0 then 60 else 0 end), 0)) match_pct
      from hit h
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'inquiry_id', p_inquiry_id,
    'supplier_id', p_lead_id,
    'basis', 'lexical: the enquiry''s own words against the product record. Not semantic — supplier_product carries no embedding, so a synonym will not match.',
    'population', jsonb_build_object(
      'products', (select count(*) from prod),
      'terms_from_enquiry', (select count(*) from terms),
      'note', case when (select count(*) from prod) = 0
                   then 'you have no products yet — upload a catalog and these become matchable'
                   when (select count(*) from terms) = 0
                   then 'the enquiry has no description to match against, so only category could be asked'
                   else null end),
    'matches', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'product_id', s.id, 'name', s.name, 'brand', s.brand, 'model', s.model,
          'match_pct', s.match_pct,
          'matched_terms', s.matched_terms, 'terms_considered', s.total_terms,
          'category_match', s.cat_hit)
        order by s.match_pct desc nulls last, s.name)
      from scored s), '[]'::jsonb)
  );
fn_supplier_quote_recommend:
with me as (select * from public.leads where id = p_lead_id),
  flag as (select coalesce((select source from me), '') = 'qd_demo_fixture' as is_demo),
  inq as (select * from public.inquiries where id = p_inquiry_id),

  -- The competing bids: what every OTHER supplier has priced this same enquiry at.
  bids as (
    select q.quote_amount amt, q.lead_time, q.warranty, q.payment_terms
    from public.quotes q, flag
    where q.inquiry_id = p_inquiry_id
      and q.supplier_id is distinct from p_lead_id
      and q.quote_amount is not null and q.quote_amount > 0
      and (coalesce(q.source, '') = 'qd_demo_fixture') = flag.is_demo
  ),
  stat as (
    select count(*) n,
           round(percentile_cont(0.5)  within group (order by amt)) mid,
           round(percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by amt)) lo,
           round(percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by amt)) hi,
           min(amt) lowest, max(amt) highest
    from bids
  ),

  -- The supplier's own habit, measured rather than assumed: across every enquiry they have priced,
  -- where did they sit against the midpoint of that enquiry's other bids? An index of 1.04 means
  -- this company prices 4% above the middle of the market, and it is computed from their own rows.
  habit as (
    select round(avg(ratio)::numeric, 3) idx, count(*) n
    from (
      select q.quote_amount / nullif((
               select percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by o.quote_amount)
               from public.quotes o
               where o.inquiry_id = q.inquiry_id and o.supplier_id is distinct from q.supplier_id
                 and o.quote_amount > 0), 0) as ratio
      from public.quotes q, flag
      where q.supplier_id = p_lead_id and q.quote_amount > 0
        and (coalesce(q.source, '') = 'qd_demo_fixture') = flag.is_demo
    ) r where r.ratio is not null
  ),

  -- ── DELIVERY, WARRANTY AND TERMS ARE TEXT, SO THEY ARE PICKED, NOT AVERAGED ───────────────────
  -- The average of "8-10 weeks" and "12-14 weeks" is not a promise anybody made, so the routine
  -- returns an answer a real supplier actually gave.
  --
  -- WHICH answer took two attempts, and the first one was wrong in a way worth recording. Taking
  -- `order by count(*) desc, <text>` looks like "the most common", but when all four bids are
  -- distinct every count is 1 and the tie breaks ALPHABETICALLY — which recommended "12-14 weeks",
  -- the slowest delivery on the board, and "12 months on equipment", the weakest warranty. A
  -- tie-break is not a market consensus, and dressing one up as the modal answer is the same defect
  -- class as an invented percentage: arithmetic that ran correctly over the wrong population.
  --
  -- So: when a value genuinely repeats, that mode is the answer and `agreed_by` says how many said
  -- it. When nothing repeats there IS no consensus, and the answer is the MIDDLE of the observed
  -- range ranked by its leading number — a real bid, neither the fastest nor the slowest — with
  -- `consensus` false so the surface can say the suppliers disagreed.
  ranked as (
    select 'lead' kind, lead_time v, count(*) c,
           min(coalesce(substring(lead_time from '\d+')::int, 999)) ord
    from bids where lead_time is not null group by 1, 2
    union all
    select 'warranty', warranty, count(*),
           min(coalesce(substring(warranty from '\d+')::int, 999))
    from bids where warranty is not null group by 1, 2
    union all
    select 'terms', payment_terms, count(*),
           min(coalesce(substring(payment_terms from '\d+')::int, 999))
    from bids where payment_terms is not null group by 1, 2
  ),
  picked as (
    select kind, v, c, has_mode from (
      select r.kind, r.v, r.c,
             max(r.c) over (partition by r.kind) >= 2 as has_mode,
             row_number() over (partition by r.kind order by r.c desc, r.ord) rn_mode,
             row_number() over (partition by r.kind order by r.ord) rn_ord,
             count(*) over (partition by r.kind) tot
      from ranked r
    ) z
    where (z.has_mode and z.rn_mode = 1)
       or (not z.has_mode and z.rn_ord = (z.tot + 1) / 2)
  ),
  lead_pick  as (select v, c, has_mode from picked where kind = 'lead'),
  warr_pick  as (select v, c, has_mode from picked where kind = 'warranty'),
  terms_pick as (select v, c, has_mode from picked where kind = 'terms'),

  -- ── RISK, AS NAMED SIGNALS RATHER THAN A MOOD ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Each signal is a condition on a real column, each carries the sentence a supplier would need to
  -- act on it, and the level is the count. A risk score with no reasons attached is a number the
  -- supplier can neither check nor fix.
  risk as (
    select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('signal', s.k, 'detail', s.d)) filter (where s.hit), '[]'::jsonb) items,
           count(*) filter (where s.hit) n
    from (
      select 'not_matchable' k,
             not public.fn_is_matchable(m.verified, m.banned, m.matching_blocked,
                                        m.approval_status, m.permanently_closed, m.chat_strikes) hit,
             'Your account cannot currently receive work, so a quote sent now may not reach the customer.' d
      from me m
      union all
      select 'licence_missing',
             (select license_expiry is null from me),
             'No licence expiry is on file, and approval depends on it.'
      union all
      select 'licence_expired',
             (select coalesce(license_expiry < current_date, false) from me),
             'Your trade licence has expired.'
      union all
      select 'brief_incomplete',
             coalesce(((select completeness->>'score' from inq))::int < 60, true),
             'The customer brief is incomplete, so the scope you price may move after you send this.'
      union all
      select 'thin_market',
             (select n from stat) < 3,
             'Fewer than three other suppliers have priced this, so the midpoint is a weak signal.'
      union all
      select 'wide_spread',
             (select case when mid > 0 then (highest - lowest) / mid > 0.4 else false end from stat),
             'The other bids disagree by more than 40%, which usually means the scope is being read differently.'
    ) s
  )

  select case when (select n from stat) = 0
    then jsonb_build_object(
      'available', false,
      'lead_id', p_lead_id, 'inquiry_id', p_inquiry_id,
      'basis', 'quotes from other suppliers on this enquiry',
      'population', 0,
      'note', 'no other supplier has priced this enquiry yet, so there is no market midpoint to '
              'recommend against. A figure taken from a different project of a different size '
              'would look identical on screen and mean nothing.')
    else jsonb_build_object(
      'available', true,
      'lead_id', p_lead_id, 'inquiry_id', p_inquiry_id,
      'summary', (select summary from inq),
      'population', (select n from stat),
      'basis', 'the midpoint of every other supplier''s bid on this enquiry',

      -- The recommended price, with the spread it came from.
      'recommended_price', jsonb_build_object(
        'value', (select mid from stat), 'currency', 'AED',
        'p25', (select lo from stat), 'p75', (select hi from stat),
        'low', (select lowest from stat), 'high', (select highest from stat),
        'basis', 'median of ' || (select n from stat)::text || ' competing bid(s) on this enquiry'),

      -- Where that recommendation sits, and where this supplier usually sits.
      'market_position', jsonb_build_object(
        'verdict', 'at the market midpoint',
        'your_index', (select idx from habit),
        'your_quotes_measured', (select n from habit),
        'detail', case when (select idx from habit) is null
                  then 'You have not priced enough enquiries yet for us to know where you usually sit.'
                  when (select idx from habit) > 1.02
                  then 'You normally price about ' || round(((select idx from habit) - 1) * 100)::text
                       || '% above the middle of the market, so this suggestion is lower than your habit.'
                  when (select idx from habit) < 0.98
                  then 'You normally price about ' || round((1 - (select idx from habit)) * 100)::text
                       || '% below the middle of the market, so this suggestion is higher than your habit.'
                  else 'You normally price close to the middle of the market, in line with this suggestion.' end),

      -- Delivery, suggested from what the competition actually promised.
      'delivery_estimate', jsonb_build_object(
        'value', (select v from lead_pick),
        'agreed_by', (select c from lead_pick),
        'consensus', (select has_mode from lead_pick),
        'observed', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(distinct lead_time), '[]'::jsonb) from bids where lead_time is not null),
        'basis', case when (select has_mode from lead_pick)
                 then 'the lead time most of the competing bids gave'
                 else 'no two bids gave the same lead time, so this is the middle of the range' end),

      -- Warranty, picked the same way and with the same honesty about disagreement.
      'warranty', jsonb_build_object(
        'value', (select v from warr_pick),
        'agreed_by', (select c from warr_pick),
        'consensus', (select has_mode from warr_pick),
        'observed', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(distinct warranty), '[]'::jsonb) from bids where warranty is not null),
        'basis', case when (select has_mode from warr_pick)
                 then 'the warranty most of the competing bids offered'
                 else 'no two bids offered the same warranty, so this is the middle of the range' end),

      'payment_terms', jsonb_build_object(
        'value', (select v from terms_pick),
        'agreed_by', (select c from terms_pick),
        'consensus', (select has_mode from terms_pick),
        'basis', case when (select has_mode from terms_pick)
                 then 'the payment terms most of the competing bids asked for'
                 else 'no two bids asked for the same terms, so this is the middle of the range' end),

      -- ── RISK: A LEVEL, ITS REASONS, AND WHAT TO DO ABOUT IT ───────────────────────────────────
      -- The first version returned a level and its signals and stopped there, which leaves the
      -- supplier holding the word "high" and no next move. Every other figure on this screen is a
      -- proposal, and the risk should be one too: the routine names the single action that would
      -- most reduce it, drawn from the same signals rather than from a phrasebook.
      'risk_level', jsonb_build_object(
        'value', case when (select n from risk) >= 3 then 'high'
                      when (select n from risk) >= 1 then 'medium' else 'low' end,
        'count', (select n from risk),
        'signals', (select items from risk),
        'recommended_action', case
          when (select n from risk) = 0
            then 'Nothing is working against this quote. We suggest sending it as proposed.'
          when exists (select 1 from jsonb_array_elements((select items from risk)) e
                       where e->>'signal' in ('not_matchable', 'licence_expired', 'licence_missing'))
            then 'We suggest fixing your account before you send this: a quote from an account that '
                 || 'cannot be matched may never reach the customer, whatever price is on it.'
          when exists (select 1 from jsonb_array_elements((select items from risk)) e
                       where e->>'signal' = 'wide_spread')
            then 'We suggest asking the customer to confirm the scope before you commit to a price. '
                 || 'The other bids disagree enough that they are probably not all pricing the same job.'
          when exists (select 1 from jsonb_array_elements((select items from risk)) e
                       where e->>'signal' = 'brief_incomplete')
            then 'We suggest putting your assumptions in writing with this quote, so a change of '
                 || 'scope later is a variation rather than an argument.'
          else 'We suggest treating the suggested price as indicative until more suppliers have priced this.'
          end,
        'basis', 'six checked signals on your account, the brief and the shape of the competing bids'))
  end;
fn_supplier_document_impact:
with me as (select * from public.leads where id = p_lead_id),
  flag as (select coalesce((select source from me), '') = 'qd_demo_fixture' as is_demo),

  -- Open enquiries this supplier's trade could serve. This is the population a missing document
  -- is measured against, so it is scoped to their sector and to briefs that are still open.
  reachable as (
    select count(*) n from public.inquiries i, me, flag
    where i.status = 'open'
      and me.sector is not null and i.category = me.sector
      and (coalesce(i.brief_source, '') = 'qd_demo_fixture') = flag.is_demo
  ),
  -- Their own priced history.
  priced as (
    select count(distinct q.inquiry_id) n from public.quotes q, flag
    where q.supplier_id = p_lead_id
      and (coalesce(q.source, '') = 'qd_demo_fixture') = flag.is_demo
  ),

  docs as (
    select d.* from (
      select 'trade_licence' as key, 'Trade licence' as label,
             (select license_doc_path from me) as path,
             (select license_expiry from me) as expiry,
             true as gates_matching
      union all
      select 'iso', 'ISO certification',
             (select iso_doc_path from me), (select iso_expiry from me), false
      union all
      select 'insurance', 'Insurance',
             (select insurance_doc_path from me), (select insurance_expiry from me), false
      union all
      select 'manufacturer_auth', 'Manufacturer authorisation',
             (select manufacturer_auth_doc_path from me), (select manufacturer_auth_expiry from me), false
      union all
      select 'company_profile', 'Company profile',
             (select company_profile_doc_path from me), null::date, false
    ) d
  ),
  scored as (
    select d.key, d.label, d.gates_matching,
           d.path is not null as on_file,
           d.expiry,
           coalesce(d.expiry < current_date, false) as expired,
           (d.path is not null and not coalesce(d.expiry < current_date, false)) as effective
    from docs d
  )

  select jsonb_build_object(
    'lead_id', p_lead_id,
    'open_in_my_trade', (select n from reachable),
    'basis', 'open enquiries in your trade, and the enquiries you have already priced',
    'documents', (
      select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'key', s.key,
        'label', s.label,
        'on_file', s.on_file,
        'expiry', s.expiry,
        'expired', s.expired,
        -- What it has already earned. Only attributable while the document is genuinely in force.
        'unlocked', case when s.effective then (select n from priced) else 0 end,
        -- What its absence is costing. Only the licence blocks matching outright, so only the
        -- licence can claim the whole open population; the others are supporting evidence and
        -- claim nothing they cannot demonstrate.
        'would_unlock', case
          when s.effective then 0
          when s.gates_matching then (select n from reachable)
          else 0 end,
        'note', case
          when s.effective then 'On file and in force.'
          when s.expired and s.gates_matching then 'Expired. Renewing it reopens every open enquiry in your trade.'
          when s.expired then 'Expired. Customers see this as a gap when comparing you.'
          when s.gates_matching then 'Missing. It is the document that decides whether you can be matched at all.'
          else 'Missing. It is optional, but it is what a customer looks for when comparing two similar quotes.'
          end
      ) order by s.gates_matching desc, s.key), '[]'::jsonb)
      from scored s)
  );
fn_graph_supplier_market:
declare n_edges int := 0; n_props int := 0;
begin
  -- Recomputed wholesale, like fn_graph_rebuild does. Only the edges this function owns are
  -- removed, so it can run independently of the nightly rebuild without eating its work.
  delete from graph_edges where rel = 'adjacent_to' and src_kind = 'category';

  -- b.slug > a.slug emits each unordered pair once. Without it every pair appears twice, which
  -- would double every count a reader aggregates and make the graph look denser than it is.
  insert into graph_edges (src_kind, src_ref, rel, dst_kind, dst_ref, props)
  select 'category', a.slug, 'adjacent_to', 'category', b.slug,
         jsonb_build_object('companies', count(distinct a.lead_id))
  from lead_category a
  join lead_category b on b.lead_id = a.lead_id and b.slug > a.slug
  group by a.slug, b.slug
  -- THE FLOOR IS THE HONESTY. Two companies serving both categories is a coincidence, not an
  -- adjacency, and drawing it would fill the graph with lines that mean nothing.
  having count(distinct a.lead_id) >= 5
  on conflict do nothing;
  get diagnostics n_edges = row_count;

  -- How many companies sit in each category, on the node itself, so a reader never has to guess
  -- whether a big-looking category is big.
  update graph_nodes n
     set props = coalesce(n.props, '{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object('companies', c.n),
         updated_at = now()
  from (select slug, count(distinct lead_id) n from lead_category group by 1) c
  where n.kind = 'category' and n.ref_id = c.slug;
  get diagnostics n_props = row_count;

  return jsonb_build_object('adjacency_edges', n_edges, 'categories_counted', n_props);
end
fn_supplier_knowledge_graph:
with mine as (
    select lc.slug, lc.is_primary, lc.score
    from lead_category lc where lc.lead_id = p_lead_id
  ),
  -- Adjacency is stored once per unordered pair, so both directions are recovered here; reading
  -- only src_ref would silently hide half of every supplier's neighbourhood.
  neigh as (
    select case when e.src_ref = m.slug then e.dst_ref else e.src_ref end as slug,
           (e.props->>'companies')::int as companies
    from graph_edges e join mine m on m.slug in (e.src_ref, e.dst_ref)
    where e.rel = 'adjacent_to' and e.src_kind = 'category'
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'lead_id', p_lead_id,
    'basis', 'categories this company is listed in, and the categories its competitors also serve',
    'my_categories', (
      select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'slug', m.slug,
        'label', (select n.label from graph_nodes n where n.kind='category' and n.ref_id=m.slug),
        'companies', (select (n.props->>'companies')::int from graph_nodes n where n.kind='category' and n.ref_id=m.slug),
        'primary', m.is_primary) order by m.is_primary desc nulls last, m.slug), '[]'::jsonb)
      from mine m),
    -- Excludes the supplier's own categories: telling them they are adjacent to themselves is noise.
    'adjacent', (
      select coalesce(jsonb_agg(x order by x->'shared_companies' desc), '[]'::jsonb) from (
        select jsonb_build_object(
          'slug', nb.slug,
          'label', (select n.label from graph_nodes n where n.kind='category' and n.ref_id=nb.slug),
          'shared_companies', max(nb.companies),
          'companies', (select (n.props->>'companies')::int from graph_nodes n where n.kind='category' and n.ref_id=nb.slug)
        ) x
        from neigh nb
        where nb.slug not in (select slug from mine)
        group by nb.slug
        order by max(nb.companies) desc
        limit 12) s),
    'population', jsonb_build_object(
      'category_nodes', (select count(*) from graph_nodes where kind='category'),
      'adjacency_edges', (select count(*) from graph_edges where rel='adjacent_to' and src_kind='category'),
      'listed_companies', (select count(distinct lead_id) from lead_category))
  );
fn_ws_intelligence:
with mat as (
    -- The company maturity index, in measurement order. This is the only series in the estate long
    -- enough to carry a trajectory, and it is rebuilt nightly.
    select measured_on, score from public.company_index
     where index_name = 'company_maturity'
     order by measured_on
  ), steps as (
    select (score - lag(score) over (order by measured_on))::double precision dx from mat
  ), moments as (
    select count(*)::int n,
           avg(dx) mu,
           coalesce(stddev_samp(dx), 0) sd
      from steps where dx is not null
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(

    -- ── OPPORTUNITIES ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'opportunities', jsonb_build_object(
      'open', (select count(*) from public.opportunity where status = 'open'),
      'total', (select count(*) from public.opportunity),
      'newest', (select max(created_at) from public.opportunity),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                 'id', o.id, 'kind', o.kind, 'title', o.title, 'detail', o.detail,
                 'value_score', o.value_score, 'effort', o.effort, 'confidence', o.confidence,
                 'detected_by', o.detected_by, 'created_at', o.created_at)
               order by o.value_score desc nulls last, o.created_at desc)
             from public.opportunity o where o.status = 'open'), '[]'::jsonb)
    ),

    -- ── COMPETITORS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'competitors', jsonb_build_object(
      'total', (select count(*) from public.competitor),
      'by_threat', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('level', t.threat_level, 'n', t.n)
                     order by case t.threat_level when 'high' then 1 when 'medium' then 2 else 3 end)
                   from (select coalesce(nullif(threat_level, ''), 'unrated') threat_level, count(*) n
                           from public.competitor group by 1) t), '[]'::jsonb),
      'anonymity_rivals', (select count(*) from public.competitor where offers_anonymity is true),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                 'id', c.id, 'name', c.name, 'url', c.url, 'kind', c.kind,
                 'threat_level', c.threat_level, 'overlap', c.overlap, 'strength', c.strength,
                 'weakness', c.weakness, 'offers_anonymity', c.offers_anonymity,
                 'verified_at', c.verified_at)
               order by case coalesce(c.threat_level, '') when 'high' then 1 when 'medium' then 2 else 3 end, c.name)
             from public.competitor c), '[]'::jsonb),
      'positions', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                 'dimension', p.dimension, 'quotesdone', p.quotesdone,
                 'market_norm', p.market_norm, 'verdict', p.verdict) order by p.id)
             from public.competitive_position p), '[]'::jsonb)
    ),

    -- ── AI SPENDING ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Every model call the company has paid for, in the window the spec's own cost row (#8) uses.
    'ai_spending', jsonb_build_object(
      'window_days', 30,
      'calls_30d', (select count(*) from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days'),
      'total_aed', (select round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed), 0), 4) from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days'),
      'failed_30d', (select count(*) from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days' and ok is false),
      'cache_hits_30d', (select count(*) from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days' and cached is true),
      'cheaper_available_30d', (select count(*) from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days' and could_be_cheaper is true),
      'by_model', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('model', m.model_used, 'calls', m.calls, 'aed', m.aed)
                    order by m.aed desc)
                  from (select coalesce(nullif(model_used, ''), 'unknown') model_used, count(*) calls,
                               round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed), 0), 4) aed
                          from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days'
                         group by 1) m), '[]'::jsonb),
      'by_dept', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('dept', d.dept_key, 'calls', d.calls, 'aed', d.aed)
                    order by d.aed desc)
                  from (select coalesce(nullif(dept_key, ''), 'unattributed') dept_key, count(*) calls,
                               round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed), 0), 4) aed
                          from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days'
                         group by 1) d), '[]'::jsonb),
      'daily', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('d', x.d, 'aed', x.aed, 'calls', x.calls) order by x.d)
                  from (select occurred_at::date d, round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed), 0), 4) aed, count(*) calls
                          from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days'
                         group by 1) x), '[]'::jsonb)
    ),

    -- ── GROWTH PROBABILITY ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Not a point estimate dressed up as a forecast. The company maturity index is measured
    -- nightly; its daily changes give a drift and a volatility, and those give the probability the
    -- index is higher in 30 days than it is today under a random-walk-with-drift model. The
    -- logistic form is the standard approximation to the normal CDF (max error ~0.01), which is far
    -- below the uncertainty in a 13-point sample — and the sample size travels with the number so
    -- nobody can read it as more than it is.
    'growth_probability', (select jsonb_build_object(
        'horizon_days', 30,
        'observations', m.n,
        'index_name', 'company_maturity',
        'index_now', (select score from mat order by measured_on desc limit 1),
        'index_first', (select score from mat order by measured_on limit 1),
        'window_from', (select min(measured_on) from mat),
        'window_to', (select max(measured_on) from mat),
        'drift_per_day', round(m.mu::numeric, 4),
        'volatility_per_day', round(m.sd::numeric, 4),
        'growth_probability_pct', case when m.n < 3 or m.sd = 0 then null
            else round((100.0 / (1 + exp(-1.702 * (m.mu * sqrt(30.0) / m.sd))))::numeric, 1) end,
        'method', 'P(index in 30d > index today), from the measured daily drift and volatility of the company maturity index; random walk with drift, logistic approximation to the normal CDF'
      ) from moments m),

    'generated_at', now()
  );
fn_ws_exec_home:
with h as (select to_jsonb(public.fn_health_index()) j),
  gh as (
    select coalesce(
      (select 'monthly' where exists (select 1 from public.goal_period where horizon = 'monthly')),
      (select 'quarterly' where exists (select 1 from public.goal_period where horizon = 'quarterly')),
      'annual') hz
  ),
  g as (
    -- THE FOUNDER WAS BEING SHOWN 98% GOAL PROGRESS ON A DAY WITH AED 0 REVENUE AND 0 CUSTOMERS.
    --
    -- This CTE reimplemented fn_goal_attainment and got it wrong four ways:
    --   1. least(100.0, NULL) returns 100.0 in Postgres - least() ignores nulls. 115 of the 122
    --      goal_period rows carry a target and NO actual_value, so every unmeasured goal scored a
    --      perfect 100 and pulled the average UP. Measured on the same rows: 98.0 published,
    --      65.3 honest. For the current period alone: 50.0 from 2 measured of 61.
    --   2. It ignored company_goals.direction, scoring an 'at_most' goal as if it were 'at_least',
    --      so a cost goal that overshot still read as progress.
    --   3. It averaged every period_label of the horizon together - two months at once.
    --   4. count(*) was published as 'goal_count', so 122 goal_period ROWS read as 122 goals.
    --
    -- fn_goal_attainment already handles all four, and its own comment
    -- ("NOT least(100, ...): least() ignores nulls, so an unmeasured goal scored 100%") exists
    -- because this exact bug was found and fixed THERE and not HERE. One copy, not two.
    select (a.j->>'pct')::numeric        pct,
           (a.j->>'goals_total')::int    n,
           (a.j->>'goals_measured')::int measured
      from gh, lateral (select public.fn_goal_attainment(gh.hz) j) a
  ),
  bott as (
    select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
             'department', r.owner_dept, 'resource', r.resource, 'used_pct', r.used_pct,
             'state', r.state, 'committed', r.committed, 'capacity', r.capacity, 'unit', r.unit)
           order by r.used_pct desc nulls last), '[]'::jsonb) j
      from public.v_resource_pressure r where r.state in ('HALT', 'DEGRADE')
  ),
  dept as (
    select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
             'department', coalesce(dh.department, e->>'label', e->>'key'),
             'dept_key', e->>'key',
             'runs', (e->'runs'),
             'busy', coalesce((e->>'runs')::int, 0) > 0,
             'health', dh.score, 'status', dh.status)
           order by coalesce((e->>'runs')::int, 0) desc), '[]'::jsonb) j
      from jsonb_array_elements(public.fn_agents_board()->'departments') e
      left join public.v_department_health dh on dh.dept_key = e->>'key'
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'health_index',     (select (j->>'index')::numeric from h),
    'mood',             (select j->>'band' from h),
    'health_note',      (select j->>'note' from h),
    'revenue_today',    (select coalesce(sum(coalesce(reveal_fee, app_fee, 0)), 0)
                           from public.transactions where revealed_at::date = current_date),
    'revenue_30d',      (select coalesce(sum(coalesce(reveal_fee, app_fee, 0)), 0)
                           from public.transactions where revealed_at > now() - interval '30 days'),
    'goal_progress_pct', (select pct from g),
    'goal_horizon',     (select hz from gh),
    'goal_count',       (select n from g),
    -- THE RULE THIS SESSION ADOPTED: no surface publishes a percentage without the coverage it
    -- rests on. "50%" and "50% across 2 measured goals of 61" are different facts, and only the
    -- second one is safe to act on. The reader decides what to render; it can no longer be
    -- unaware of the denominator.
    'goal_measured',    (select measured from g),
    'customers_active', (select count(*) from public.customers where coalesce(banned, false) = false),
    'suppliers_active', coalesce((public.fn_marketplace_analytics()->>'active_suppliers_30d')::int, 0),
    'employees',        (select count(*) from public.org_agents where active),
    -- COUNTED CRON JOBS AND CALLED THEM EMPLOYEES (10 Aug 2026).
    -- This was count(distinct agent) from agent_runs with NO JOIN TO org_agents, and agent_runs is
    -- the cron and job log: 111 distinct agent values over 30 days, only NINE of them employee keys.
    -- An employee works in three places and agent_runs is the one they use least: agent_memory
    -- (a recorded thought), agent_chats (a reasoning turn), agent_runs (a run). Any of the three
    -- counts, and the count is over org_agents so a cron can never be mistaken for a colleague.
    'employees_working', (select count(*) from public.org_agents o where o.active and (
                             exists (select 1 from public.agent_runs r
                                      where r.agent = o.agent_key and r.started_at > now() - interval '24 hours')
                          or exists (select 1 from public.agent_memory m
                                      where m.agent_key = o.agent_key and m.created_at > now() - interval '24 hours')
                          or exists (select 1 from public.agent_chats c
                                      where c.agent_key = o.agent_key and c.created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'))),
    'bottlenecks',      (select j from bott),
    'departments',      (select j from dept),
    'workflow_runs_24h', (select count(*) from public.workflow_run
                           where coalesce(started_at, created_at) > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    -- HANDOFFS ARE HANDOFFS (16 Aug 2026). See the header. phase_c_handoff_run is the only table
    -- where one employee formally accepts accountable work from another; event_delivery is the
    -- message bus. They are published separately because they are separate facts, and collapsing
    -- them is how 0 read as 26.
    'handoffs_24h', (select count(*) from public.phase_c_handoff_run
                      where opened_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    'events_delivered_24h', (select count(*) from public.event_delivery
                              where delivered_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    'knowledge_revisions_7d', (select count(*) from public.kb_revisions
                                where created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
    'uptime_pct_24h', (select round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where verdict = 'ALIVE')
                                    / nullif(count(*), 0), 1)
                         from public.edge_health_probe where checked_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    -- THE WORKING COMPANY. Added 10 Aug 2026 because seven of the nine business tiles can only be
    -- non-zero once the marketplace transacts, and meanwhile the founder was shown nothing of the
    -- 20,470 leads, 18,000+ runs and 800+ events that already exist.
    'leads_total',      (select count(*) from public.leads),
    'agent_runs_24h',   (select count(*) from public.agent_runs where started_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    'events_24h',       (select count(*) from public.company_event where occurred_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    'decisions_open',   (select count(*) from public.agent_actions where status in ('pending','needs_review')),
    'tasks_open',       (select count(*) from public.org_tasks where status not in ('done','cancelled')),
    'generated_at',     now()
  );
fn_ws_company_os:
select jsonb_build_object(

    -- ── THE TEN OPERATING SYSTEMS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'operating_systems', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'os_key', o.os_key, 'num', o.num, 'name', o.name, 'mission', o.mission,
        'charter', o.charter, 'mandate', o.mandate, 'owner_agent', o.owner_agent,
        'health_score', o.health_score, 'last_health_at', o.last_health_at, 'active', o.active,
        'responsibilities', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(r.responsibility order by r.responsibility), '[]'::jsonb)
                               from public.os_responsibility r where r.os_key = o.os_key),
        'objectives', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                          'objective', j.objective, 'horizon', j.horizon, 'measure', j.measure,
                          'actual_value', j.actual_value) order by j.id), '[]'::jsonb)
                         from public.os_objective j where j.os_key = o.os_key and j.active),
        -- Only 4 of the 72 os_responsibility rows name a department; the rest name capabilities.
        -- So this reports the departments the OS demonstrably owns and the headcount inside THEM,
        -- rather than a company-wide headcount that would read as 0 for Leadership and be wrong.
        'owned_departments', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(d.dept_key order by d.dept_key), '[]'::jsonb)
                                from public.org_departments d
                               where exists (select 1 from public.os_responsibility r2
                                              where r2.os_key = o.os_key and r2.responsibility = d.dept_key)),
        'staff_in_owned_departments', (select count(*) from public.org_agents a where a.active
                    and a.department in (select r2.responsibility from public.os_responsibility r2 where r2.os_key = o.os_key)))
      order by o.num) from public.operating_system o where o.active), '[]'::jsonb),

    -- ── THE COMPANY BRAIN, AS ONE GRAPH ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'graph', jsonb_build_object(
      'node_count', (select count(*) from public.graph_nodes),
      'edge_count', (select count(*) from public.graph_edges),
      'rebuilt_at', (select max(updated_at) from public.graph_nodes),
      'node_kinds', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('kind', k.kind, 'n', k.n) order by k.n desc)
                     from (select kind, count(*) n from public.graph_nodes group by 1) k), '[]'::jsonb),
      'edge_kinds', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('rel', e.rel, 'src_kind', e.src_kind, 'dst_kind', e.dst_kind, 'n', e.n) order by e.n desc)
                     from (select rel, src_kind, dst_kind, count(*) n from public.graph_edges group by 1,2,3) e), '[]'::jsonb),
      'nodes', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('kind', n.kind, 'ref_id', n.ref_id, 'label', n.label) order by n.kind, n.label)
                 from (select * from public.graph_nodes order by kind, label limit 200) n), '[]'::jsonb),
      'edges', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('src_kind', g.src_kind, 'src_ref', g.src_ref, 'rel', g.rel, 'dst_kind', g.dst_kind, 'dst_ref', g.dst_ref) order by g.src_kind, g.rel)
                 from (select * from public.graph_edges order by src_kind, rel limit 300) g), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── THE AI BOARD ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'board', jsonb_build_object(
      'advisors', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'advisor_key', b.advisor_key, 'name', b.name, 'lens', b.lens, 'asks', b.asks, 'weight', b.weight)
        order by b.advisor_key) from public.board_advisor b where coalesce(b.active, true)), '[]'::jsonb),
      'opinion_count', (select count(*) from public.board_opinion),
      'opinions', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'subject', p.subject, 'advisor_key', p.advisor_key, 'recommendation', p.recommendation,
          'rationale', left(p.rationale, 300), 'confidence', p.confidence, 'at', p.created_at)
        order by p.created_at desc)
        from (select * from public.board_opinion order by created_at desc limit 12) p), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── THE INDICES: MATURITY, MARKETPLACE HEALTH, ORGANISATIONAL ENERGY ─────────────────────
    -- THE ENGINE ITSELF HAD NO SCREEN (12 Aug 2026). 238 workflow runs and the only thing any
    -- surface showed was a count tile: "Workflows run today". Which processes are in flight, where
    -- each one is parked and WHO it is waiting on were not on any screen in the company, so the
    -- engine going from 5 completed runs to 131 was invisible except in the database.
    -- waiting_on is the resolved employee, not the raw actor_role - the whole point of the
    -- resolver work is that a step now names somebody the company can actually reach.
    'workflow_state', jsonb_build_object(
      'by_status', coalesce((select jsonb_object_agg(s.status, s.n)
          from (select status, count(*) n from public.workflow_run group by 1) s), '{}'::jsonb),
      'steps_delivered', (select count(*) from public.workflow_step_run
                             where output->>'worked_by' = 'workflow_dispatch'),
      'ready_now', (select count(*) from public.workflow_step_run sr
                      join public.workflow_run r on r.id = sr.workflow_run_id
                     where sr.status = 'ready' and r.status = 'running'),
      'in_flight', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
            'run_id', r.id,
            'workflow', coalesce(w.name, r.workflow_key),
            'step_no', sr.step_no,
            'step', sr.input->>'step',
            'gate', nullif(sr.input->>'gate', 'none'),
            'waiting_on', public.fn_workflow_actor_resolve(r.id, sr.actor),
            'addressed_as', coalesce(sr.input->>'addressed_as', sr.actor),
            'waiting_since', sr.started_at,
            'hours_waiting', round(extract(epoch from (now() - sr.started_at))/3600.0)
          ) order by sr.started_at)
        from (select r2.id, r2.workflow_key, sr2.step_no, sr2.input, sr2.actor, sr2.started_at
                from public.workflow_run r2
                join public.workflow_step_run sr2
                  on sr2.workflow_run_id = r2.id and sr2.status = 'ready'
               where r2.status = 'running'
               order by sr2.started_at
               limit 25) q
        join public.workflow_run r on r.id = q.id
        join public.workflow_step_run sr on sr.workflow_run_id = q.id and sr.step_no = q.step_no
        left join public.workflow w on w.workflow_key = r.workflow_key), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- WHAT THE COMPANY'S PROCESSES ACTUALLY PRODUCED (11 Aug 2026).
    -- workflow_step_run.output holds 3,700-4,700 characters of real analysis per step, written by
    -- the named employee who owns that step. Before this key, the ONLY readers of that column were
    -- the two functions that write it; this surface counted rows per day and showed none of the
    -- work. A deliverable nobody reads is the defect this estate keeps reproducing.
    -- The outcome line is surfaced, not the body: the founder wants to see what his company decided,
    -- and the full text stays one query away for anything that needs it.
    'process_work', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'at', sr.finished_at,
        'workflow', coalesce(w.name, r.workflow_key),
        'step_no', sr.step_no,
        'step', sr.input->>'step',
        'employee', coalesce(sr.output->>'employee', sr.actor),
        'outcome', left(coalesce(sr.output->>'outcome',''), 400),
        'chars', length(coalesce(sr.output->>'deliverable','')),
        'confidence', sr.output->>'self_confidence',
        'mode', sr.output->>'mode') order by sr.finished_at desc)
      from public.workflow_step_run sr
      join public.workflow_run r on r.id = sr.workflow_run_id
      left join public.workflow w on w.workflow_key = r.workflow_key
     where sr.status = 'done'
       and coalesce(sr.output->>'deliverable','') <> ''
       and sr.finished_at > now() - interval '14 days'
     limit 40), '[]'::jsonb),

    'indices', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'index_name', c.index_name, 'score', c.score, 'band', c.band,
        'measured_on', c.measured_on, 'dimensions', c.dimensions) order by c.index_name)
      from public.company_index c
      where c.measured_on = (select max(measured_on) from public.company_index c2 where c2.index_name = c.index_name)), '[]'::jsonb),
    'marketplace_health', (select jsonb_build_object('score', c.score, 'band', c.band, 'measured_on', c.measured_on, 'dimensions', c.dimensions)
        from public.company_index c where c.index_name = 'marketplace_health'
        order by c.measured_on desc, c.id desc limit 1),

    -- ── EXECUTIVE REPLAY ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'replay', jsonb_build_object(
      -- THE SIX TRACKS OF THE CHOSEN DAY, in one place for the first time. The day is the newest
      -- company_snapshot day, which is the chip the Replay card is already showing, so these
      -- counts describe what the founder is looking at rather than a different day's activity.
      'tracks', (select jsonb_build_object(
          'day', dd.day,
          'decisions',     (select count(*) from public.decision_log      x where x.created_at::date = dd.day),
          'conversations', (select count(*) from public.agent_chats       x where x.created_at::date = dd.day),
          'approvals',     (select count(*) from public.agent_actions     x where coalesce(x.decided_at, x.created_at)::date = dd.day),
          'workflows',     (select count(*) from public.workflow_step_run x where coalesce(x.started_at, x.finished_at)::date = dd.day),
          'kpis',          (select count(*) from public.metric_snapshot   x where x.taken_at::date = dd.day),
          'outcomes',      (select count(*) from public.outcome_record    x where coalesce(x.observed_at, x.created_at)::date = dd.day))
        from (select coalesce(max(snapshot_on), current_date - 1) as day from public.company_snapshot) dd),
      'days_on_file', (select count(*) from public.company_snapshot),
      'newest', (select max(snapshot_on) from public.company_snapshot),
      'company_snapshot', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('snapshot_on', s.snapshot_on, 'state', s.state) order by s.snapshot_on desc)
        from (select * from public.company_snapshot order by snapshot_on desc limit 8) s), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── REPUTATION ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'reputation', jsonb_build_object(
      'graded', (select count(*) from public.agent_reputation),
      'by_tier', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('tier', t.tier, 'n', t.n) order by t.n desc)
                   from (select coalesce(tier, 'ungraded') tier, count(*) n from public.agent_reputation group by 1) t), '[]'::jsonb),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'agent_key', r.agent_key, 'score', r.score, 'tier', r.tier, 'correctness', r.correctness,
          'reliability', r.reliability, 'cost_efficiency', r.cost_efficiency,
          'learning_speed', r.learning_speed, 'collaboration', r.collaboration)
        order by r.score desc nulls last)
        from (select * from public.agent_reputation order by score desc nulls last limit 20) r), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── STRUCTURAL PROPOSALS AND THE LESSON LEDGER ───────────────────────────────────────────
    'evolution_proposals', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'id', e.id, 'trigger_kind', e.trigger_kind, 'subject', e.subject,
        'observation', left(e.observation, 240), 'proposal', left(e.proposal, 240),
        'change_class', e.change_class, 'status', e.status, 'decided_by', e.decided_by, 'at', e.created_at)
      order by e.created_at desc)
      from (select * from public.evolution_proposal order by created_at desc limit 12) e), '[]'::jsonb),
    -- THE FOUR STRATEGIC QUEUES, named by their own tables so the screen and the store cannot drift
    -- apart: evolution_proposal, challenge_record, opportunity and board_opinion. The spec's
    -- "strategic decisions rather than operational tasks" is exactly this set against the pending
    -- agent_actions queue the founder was being shown instead.
    'strategic_queues', jsonb_build_object(
      'evolution_proposal', (select count(*) from public.evolution_proposal where status = 'proposed'),
      'challenge_record', (select count(*) from public.challenge_record where responded_at is null),
      'opportunity', (select count(*) from public.opportunity where status = 'open'),
      'board_opinion', (select count(*) from public.board_opinion),
      'operational_pending', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions where status in ('pending','needs_review'))),
    'opportunity', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'id', o.id, 'kind', o.kind, 'title', o.title, 'detail', left(o.detail, 240),
        'value_score', o.value_score, 'effort', o.effort, 'confidence', o.confidence, 'at', o.created_at)
      order by o.value_score desc nulls last)
      from (select * from public.opportunity where status = 'open'
             order by value_score desc nulls last limit 10) o), '[]'::jsonb),

    -- The AI disagreeing with the founder, and what it offered instead. 47 challenges on file, 31
    -- carrying alternatives, and no surface has ever shown one.
    'challenge_record', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'id', h.id, 'proposal', h.proposal, 'proposed_by', h.proposed_by, 'challenged_by', h.challenged_by,
        'stance', h.stance, 'confidence', h.confidence, 'reasoning', left(h.reasoning, 320),
        'alternatives', h.alternatives, 'violates_principle', h.violates_principle,
        'violates_rank', h.violates_rank, 'founder_response', h.founder_response,
        'responded_at', h.responded_at, 'at', h.created_at)
      order by h.created_at desc)
      from (select * from public.challenge_record order by created_at desc limit 12) h), '[]'::jsonb),

    'institutional_memory', jsonb_build_object(
      'lessons', (select count(*) from public.institutional_memory),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'kind', m.kind, 'headline', m.headline, 'outcome', m.outcome, 'lesson', left(m.detail, 240),
          'os_key', m.os_key, 'confidence', m.confidence, 'occurred_at', m.occurred_at)
        order by m.occurred_at desc nulls last)
        from (select * from public.institutional_memory order by occurred_at desc nulls last limit 12) m), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── RESILIENCE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'resilience', jsonb_build_object(
      'critical_capability', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'capability_key', c.capability_key, 'capability', c.capability, 'owner_dept', c.owner_dept,
          'test_kind', c.test_kind, 'last_verdict', c.last_verdict, 'last_checked', c.last_checked)
        order by c.capability_key) from public.critical_capability c), '[]'::jsonb),
      'continuity_plan', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'service', p.service, 'criticality', p.criticality, 'failure_mode', p.failure_mode,
          'fallback', p.fallback, 'recovery', p.recovery, 'rto_minutes', p.rto_minutes,
          'owner_agent', p.owner_agent, 'last_tested', p.last_tested)
        order by p.criticality, p.service) from public.continuity_plan p), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── THE OPERATING MANUAL ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'operating_manual', jsonb_build_object(
      'runbooks', (select count(*) from public.os_runbooks),
      'by_category', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('category', k.category, 'n', k.n) order by k.n desc)
                      from (select coalesce(category, 'uncategorised') category, count(*) n from public.os_runbooks group by 1) k), '[]'::jsonb),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'slug', r.slug, 'title', r.title, 'category', r.category, 'when_to_use', left(r.when_to_use, 200), 'os_key', r.os_key)
        order by r.sort nulls last, r.slug)
        from (select * from public.os_runbooks order by sort nulls last, slug limit 24) r), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── RESOURCE MOVEMENT, AUTONOMY, SUPPLY AND THE EVENT BUS ────────────────────────────────
    'allocation_change', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'resource', a.resource, 'subject', a.subject, 'from_value', a.from_value, 'to_value', a.to_value,
        'reason', left(a.reason, 200), 'policy', a.policy, 'reverted', a.reverted, 'at', a.created_at)
      order by a.created_at desc)
      from (select * from public.allocation_change order by created_at desc limit 12) a), '[]'::jsonb),
    'autonomy', jsonb_build_object(
      'changes', (select count(*) from public.autonomy_control_audit),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'object', u.object, 'op', u.op, 'direction', u.direction, 'old_value', u.old_value,
          'new_value', u.new_value, 'reason', left(u.reason, 160), 'at', u.at)
        order by u.at desc)
        from (select * from public.autonomy_control_audit order by at desc limit 10) u), '[]'::jsonb)),
    'supply_health', jsonb_build_object(
      'snapshots', (select count(*) from public.supply_health_snapshots),
      'latest_period_end', (select max(period_end) from public.supply_health_snapshots),
      'coverage_gaps', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(s) order by s.period_end desc)
        from (select * from public.supply_health_snapshots order by period_end desc limit 6) s), '[]'::jsonb)),
    'invite_schedule', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'day', i.day, 'planned', i.planned, 'sent', i.sent, 'status', i.status) order by i.day desc)
      from (select * from public.invite_schedule order by day desc limit 10) i), '[]'::jsonb),
    'events', jsonb_build_object(
      'total', (select count(*) from public.company_event),
      'last_7d', (select count(*) from public.company_event where occurred_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
      'by_class', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('event_type', c.event_type, 'n', c.n) order by c.n desc)
                   from (select event_type, count(*) n from public.company_event
                          where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days' group by 1) c), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- ── MODEL MIX ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    'model_mix', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'model_used', m.model_used, 'calls', m.calls, 'aed', m.aed, 'latency_ms', m.latency_ms,
        'cache_hits', m.cache_hits) order by m.aed desc)
      from (select coalesce(nullif(model_used,''),'unknown') model_used, count(*) calls,
                   round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed),0),4) aed,
                   round(avg(latency_ms)) latency_ms,
                   count(*) filter (where cached) cache_hits
              from public.ai_cost_log where occurred_at > now() - interval '30 days' group by 1) m), '[]'::jsonb),

    -- ── INFORMATION FLOWING BETWEEN THE TEN SYSTEMS ─────────────────────────────────────────
    -- Derived from what was actually DELIVERED, not from what os_interface declares: the declared
    -- outputs and inputs are disjoint sets and join to zero cross-OS edges. The consumer is
    -- event_delivery.os_key; the producer is company_event.actor resolved through its department,
    -- or the actor itself when the actor IS a department. Deliveries whose actor is machinery
    -- (system, a cron, the brief) are counted as unattributed rather than assigned to a system.
    'flow', (with res as (
        select d.os_key as to_os, d.event_type, d.delivered_at,
               coalesce((select od.os_key from public.org_agents a
                          join public.os_department od on od.dept_key = a.department
                         where a.agent_key = e.actor limit 1),
                        (select od2.os_key from public.os_department od2
                          where od2.dept_key = e.actor limit 1)) as from_os
          from public.event_delivery d
          join public.company_event e on e.id = d.event_id
         where d.os_key is not null and d.delivered_at > now() - interval '7 days')
      select jsonb_build_object(
        'window_days', 7,
        'deliveries', (select count(*) from res),
        'attributed', (select count(*) from res where from_os is not null),
        'unattributed', (select count(*) from res where from_os is null),
        'unroutable', (select count(*) from public.event_delivery
                        where unroutable_reason is not null
                          and delivered_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
        'nodes', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
            'os_key', o.os_key, 'num', o.num, 'name', o.name,
            'received', (select count(*) from res where res.to_os = o.os_key),
            'sent', (select count(*) from res where res.from_os = o.os_key)) order by o.num)
          from public.operating_system o where o.active), '[]'::jsonb),
        'edges', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(x) from (
            select from_os, to_os, count(*) as n,
                   count(distinct event_type) as event_types,
                   max(delivered_at) as newest,
                   (array_agg(distinct event_type))[1:3] as kinds
              from res where from_os is not null
             group by from_os, to_os order by count(*) desc limit 40) x), '[]'::jsonb))),

    'generated_at', now()
  );
fn_os_memory:
with b as (select coalesce(nullif(btrim(p_q), ''), '') q,
                    coalesce(p_from, '-infinity'::date) lo,
                    coalesce(p_to, 'infinity'::date) hi)
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'subject', (select q from b), 'from', p_from, 'to', p_to,

    -- Every decision about a subject, over a period.
    'decisions', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'id', l.id, 'actor', l.actor, 'kind', l.kind, 'decision', l.decision,
          'confidence', l.confidence, 'reasons', l.reasons, 'route_to', l.route_to, 'at', l.created_at)
        order by l.created_at desc)
      from (select l.* from public.decision_log l, b
             where (b.q = '' or l.decision ilike '%'||b.q||'%' or l.actor ilike '%'||b.q||'%'
                    or l.kind ilike '%'||b.q||'%' or l.ctx::text ilike '%'||b.q||'%')
               and l.created_at::date between b.lo and b.hi
             order by l.created_at desc limit 25) l), '[]'::jsonb),

    -- Why something was rejected: the recorded reasoning behind a past decision.
    'rejection_reason', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'id', d.id, 'problem', d.problem, 'recommendation', d.recommendation,
          'risks', d.risks, 'options', d.options, 'status', d.status,
          'decided_by', d.decided_by, 'actual_outcome', d.actual_outcome, 'at', d.created_at)
        order by d.created_at desc)
      from (select d.* from public.decision_record d, b
             where (b.q = '' or d.problem ilike '%'||b.q||'%' or d.recommendation ilike '%'||b.q||'%'
                    or d.context ilike '%'||b.q||'%')
               and d.created_at::date between b.lo and b.hi
             order by d.created_at desc limit 15) d), '[]'::jsonb),

    -- When something changed, and who changed it. undo_log is the row-level change history.
    'changes', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'id', u.id, 'table_name', u.table_name, 'row_id', u.row_id, 'op', u.op,
          'actor', u.actor, 'reverted', u.reverted, 'at', u.created_at)
        order by u.created_at desc)
      from (select u.* from public.undo_log u, b
             where (b.q = '' or u.table_name ilike '%'||b.q||'%' or u.actor ilike '%'||b.q||'%')
               and u.created_at::date between b.lo and b.hi
             order by u.created_at desc limit 25) u), '[]'::jsonb),
    'change_subjects', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('table_name', t.table_name, 'n', t.n) order by t.n desc)
      from (select table_name, count(*) n from public.undo_log group by 1) t), '[]'::jsonb),

    -- Lessons, scoped to a period.
    'lessons', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
          'id', m.id, 'headline', m.headline, 'detail', left(m.detail, 300), 'outcome', m.outcome,
          'kind', m.kind, 'os_key', m.os_key, 'confidence', m.confidence, 'occurred_at', m.occurred_at)
        order by coalesce(m.occurred_at, m.created_at) desc)
      from (select m.* from public.institutional_memory m, b
             where (b.q = '' or m.headline ilike '%'||b.q||'%' or m.detail ilike '%'||b.q||'%'
                    or m.category_slug ilike '%'||b.q||'%')
               and coalesce(m.occurred_at, m.created_at)::date between b.lo and b.hi
             order by coalesce(m.occurred_at, m.created_at) desc limit 20) m), '[]'::jsonb)
  );
fn_ws_notifications:
select jsonb_build_object(
    -- CRITICAL — a founder alert raised at critical/high, or a critical action still waiting.
    'critical', jsonb_build_object(
      'tier', 'critical',
      'count', (select count(*) from public.founder_alerts
                 where lower(coalesce(level,'')) in ('critical','high')
                   and created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
                   and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at())
             + (select count(*) from public.agent_actions
                 where status in ('pending','needs_review') and lower(coalesce(risk,'')) = 'critical'
                   and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at()),
      -- THE ROW LIST HAD NO TIME FILTER AT ALL while its count had a 7-day one, so the list showed
      -- alerts older than the number above it claimed to measure. Both now share one window.
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('title', a.event, 'detail', left(a.detail::text, 200),
                          'level', a.level, 'at', a.created_at) order by a.created_at desc)
                from (select * from public.founder_alerts
                       where lower(coalesce(level,'')) in ('critical','high')
                         and created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
                         and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at()
                       order by created_at desc limit 8) a), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- IMPORTANT — waiting on the founder, but not critical.
    'important', jsonb_build_object(
      'tier', 'important',
      'count', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions
                 where status in ('pending','needs_review')
                   and lower(coalesce(risk,'')) in ('high','medium')
                   and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at()),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('title', a.title, 'detail', left(coalesce(a.recommendation,''), 200),
                          'risk', a.risk, 'agent', a.agent, 'at', a.created_at) order by a.created_at desc)
                from (select * from public.agent_actions
                       where status in ('pending','needs_review') and lower(coalesce(risk,'')) in ('high','medium')
                         and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at()
                       order by created_at desc limit 8) a), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- SUGGESTED — nothing is blocked, but the company thinks the founder should look.
    'suggested', jsonb_build_object(
      'tier', 'suggested',
      'count', (select count(*) from public.opportunity where status = 'open'
                 and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at())
             + (select count(*) from public.evolution_proposal where status = 'proposed'
                 and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at()),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('title', o.title, 'detail', left(coalesce(o.detail,''), 200),
                          'kind', o.kind, 'at', o.created_at) order by o.value_score desc nulls last)
                from (select * from public.opportunity where status = 'open'
                       and created_at >= public.fn_os_fresh_start_at()
                       order by value_score desc nulls last limit 6) o), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- COMPLETED TODAY — closed since midnight, whoever closed it.
    'completed_today', jsonb_build_object(
      'tier', 'completed_today',
      'count', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions where decided_at::date = current_date),
      'rows', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('title', a.title, 'status', a.status,
                          'decided_by', a.decided_by, 'at', a.decided_at) order by a.decided_at desc)
                from (select * from public.agent_actions where decided_at::date = current_date
                       order by decided_at desc limit 8) a), '[]'::jsonb)),

    -- THE SHARE THE AI HANDLED WITHOUT THE FOUNDER. Not a boast: an action that was never escalated
    -- is one the founder never had to see, and that ratio is the whole promise of the OS.
    -- Deliberately NOT watermarked: it is a measure of the machine's behaviour over a real time
    -- window, not a list of his outstanding work, and truncating its denominator at the reset would
    -- make it read 100% of 0 on the first day.
    'auto_cleared_24h', (select round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where coalesce(escalated, false) = false)
                                 / greatest(count(*), 1))
                           from public.agent_actions where created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    'auto_handled_30d', (select round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where coalesce(escalated, false) = false)
                                 / greatest(count(*), 1))
                           from public.agent_actions where created_at > now() - interval '30 days'),
    'actions_24h', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions where created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
    'actions_30d', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions where created_at > now() - interval '30 days'),
    -- The outbound queue, which is what public.notifications actually is.
    'outbound_queue', (select count(*) from public.notifications where coalesce(status,'') not in ('sent','delivered')),
    'fresh_start_at', public.fn_os_fresh_start_at(),
    'generated_at', now()
  );
fn_owning_os:
with a as (select coalesce(nullif(btrim(p_agent), ''), '~none~') k),
  stripped as (
    -- widened from _(ai|director|ops|monitor|watch|agent|bot) so a role title resolves too
    select regexp_replace(a.k, '_(ai|director|ops|monitor|watch|agent|bot|controller|curator|analyst|engineer|manager|lead|head|specialist)$', '') s
    from a)
  select coalesce(
    (select o.os_key from public.operating_system o, a where o.owner_agent = a.k and o.active limit 1),
    (select r.os_key from public.os_responsibility r, a where r.responsibility = a.k limit 1),
    (select r.os_key from public.os_responsibility r
       join public.org_agents g on g.department = r.responsibility, a
      where g.agent_key = a.k limit 1),
