               from public.founder_release_approval a
              where a.approved_at > now() - interval '30 days'
              order by a.approved_at desc limit 1),
            'no approval recorded inside 30 days; this is his signature and nothing else can supply it'))
) t(gate, verdict, evidence);
fn_org_task_execute_sweep:
declare t record; v_q int := 0; v_key text;
begin
  for t in
    select k.id, k.dept_key, k.title, k.action_class, e.target, e.risk_tier, e.reversible
      from public.org_tasks k
      join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = k.action_class
     where k.status in ('assigned','in_progress')
       and e.kind = 'edge' and e.active
       and e.risk_tier = 'low' and e.advisory_safe and e.reversible
       and not e.notifies_human
       and coalesce(e.required_authority,'') <> 'founder'
       -- ALL statuses. idempotency_key is UNIQUE, so a task whose invocation FAILED once collides on
       -- the next sweep: org_task:260 failed org_task_execute_sweep_hourly at 14:45, 15:45 and 16:45
       -- on 10 Aug. A failed attempt is a recorded attempt.
       and not exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                        where x.idempotency_key = 'org_task:' || k.id)
     order by k.id
     limit greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 5), 1)
  loop
    v_key := 'org_task:' || t.id;
    insert into public.action_execution(id, correlation_id, action_class, executor, idempotency_key,
                                        risk_tier, reversible, request, status, attempts)
    values (gen_random_uuid(), gen_random_uuid(), t.action_class, t.target, v_key,
            t.risk_tier, t.reversible,
            jsonb_build_object('org_task_id', t.id, 'dept_key', t.dept_key,
                               'title', left(coalesce(t.title,''), 300),
                               'source', 'fn_org_task_execute_sweep'),
            'queued', 0)
    on conflict (idempotency_key) do nothing;

    update public.org_tasks set status = 'in_progress', last_run_at = now(), updated_at = now()
     where id = t.id and status = 'assigned';
    v_q := v_q + 1;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object('queued', v_q, 'ran_at', now(),
    'eligible_remaining', (select count(*) from public.org_tasks k
                             join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = k.action_class
                            where k.status in ('assigned','in_progress') and e.kind='edge' and e.active
                              and e.risk_tier='low' and e.advisory_safe and e.reversible
                              and not e.notifies_human
                              and not exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                                               where x.idempotency_key = 'org_task:' || k.id)));
end
fn_agent_action_work_sweep:
declare v_q int := 0; r record; v_key text;
begin
  for r in
    select a.id, a.kind,
           (select count(*) from public.action_execution x
             where x.idempotency_key in ('agent_action:' || a.id, 'agent_action:' || a.id || '#2')
               and x.status = 'failed') as failures
      from public.agent_actions a
      join public.org_agents o on o.agent_key = a.agent and o.active
      join public.agent_action_kind_policy p on p.kind = a.kind and p.policy = 'auto'
     where a.status = 'pending'
       -- Nothing live and nothing already settled for this item...
       and not exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                        where x.idempotency_key in ('agent_action:' || a.id, 'agent_action:' || a.id || '#2')
                          and x.status in ('queued','running','succeeded'))
       -- ...and fewer than two attempts have failed. Equality, not LIKE: `_` is a single-character
       -- wildcard in LIKE and 'agent_action:' is full of them, so `like 'agent_action:'||id` would
       -- also match keys this function never wrote.
       and (select count(*) from public.action_execution x
             where x.idempotency_key in ('agent_action:' || a.id, 'agent_action:' || a.id || '#2')
               and x.status = 'failed') < 2
     order by a.created_at
     limit greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 10), 1)
  loop
    v_key := 'agent_action:' || r.id || case when r.failures >= 1 then '#2' else '' end;
    insert into public.action_execution(id, correlation_id, action_class, executor, idempotency_key,
                                        risk_tier, reversible, request, status, attempts)
    values (gen_random_uuid(), gen_random_uuid(), 'agent_action_work', 'action_worker',
            v_key, 'low', true,
            jsonb_build_object('action_id', r.id, 'kind', r.kind,
                               'source', 'fn_agent_action_work_sweep',
                               'attempt', r.failures + 1),
            'queued', 0)
    on conflict (idempotency_key) do nothing;
    v_q := v_q + 1;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object('queued', v_q, 'ran_at', now(),
    'eligible_remaining', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions a
                             join public.org_agents o on o.agent_key = a.agent and o.active
                             join public.agent_action_kind_policy p on p.kind = a.kind and p.policy = 'auto'
                            where a.status = 'pending'
                              and not exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                                               where x.idempotency_key in ('agent_action:' || a.id, 'agent_action:' || a.id || '#2')
                                                 and x.status in ('queued','running','succeeded'))
                              and (select count(*) from public.action_execution x
                                    where x.idempotency_key in ('agent_action:' || a.id, 'agent_action:' || a.id || '#2')
                                      and x.status = 'failed') < 2),
    -- Named separately so "we have stopped trying" is never counted as "we are working on it".
    'exhausted_two_attempts', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions a
                                 join public.agent_action_kind_policy p on p.kind = a.kind and p.policy = 'auto'
                                where a.status = 'pending'
                                  and (select count(*) from public.action_execution x
                                        where x.idempotency_key in ('agent_action:' || a.id, 'agent_action:' || a.id || '#2')
                                          and x.status = 'failed') >= 2),
    'never_auto_settled', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions a
                             join public.agent_action_kind_policy p on p.kind = a.kind and p.policy = 'founder'
                            where a.status = 'pending'),
    'unrouted', (select count(*) from public.agent_actions a
                  where a.status = 'pending'
                    and not exists (select 1 from public.agent_action_kind_policy p where p.kind = a.kind)));
end
fn_org_agent_resolve:
select coalesce(
    (select o.agent_key from public.org_agents o
      where o.agent_key = p_addressee and o.active),
    (select a.agent_key from public.org_agent_alias a
       join public.org_agents o on o.agent_key = a.agent_key and o.active
      where a.alias = p_addressee),
    -- THE TITLE ARM (11 Aug 2026). 30 of the 66 workflow actor_role values are job titles, and
    -- five of them are a second spelling of an employee the alias table already knew by key.
    -- Ordered so a title held by more than one employee resolves to the senior holder rather than
    -- to whichever row the planner returned first.
    (select o.agent_key from public.org_agents o
      where lower(btrim(o.title)) = lower(btrim(p_addressee)) and o.active
      order by case o.seniority
                 when 'executive' then 0 when 'chief' then 1 when 'director' then 2
                 when 'lead'      then 3 when 'manager' then 4 when 'senior' then 5 else 6 end,
               o.agent_key
      limit 1),
    (select o.agent_key from public.org_agents o
      where o.department = p_addressee and o.active
      order by case o.seniority
                 when 'executive' then 0 when 'chief' then 1 when 'director' then 2
                 when 'lead'      then 3 when 'manager' then 4 when 'senior' then 5 else 6 end,
               o.agent_key
      limit 1)
  );
fn_workflow_step_sweep:
declare s record; v_settled int := 0; v_q int := 0; v_key text; v_res text; v_out jsonb; v_parked int; v_noclass int;
        v_cap int; v_reflection_today int; v_throttled int; v_true_stall int; v_status text; v_note text;
        v_ineligible int; v_why text;
begin
  -- 1. SETTLE what the invoker has already finished.
  for s in
    select x.status, x.response, r.id sid, r.workflow_run_id, r.step_no
      from public.action_execution x
      join public.workflow_step_run r on r.id = x.workflow_step_run_id
     where x.workflow_step_run_id is not null
       and x.status in ('succeeded','failed')
       and r.finished_at is null
     order by r.id
     limit 50
  loop
    v_res := public.fn_workflow_step_done(
      s.workflow_run_id, s.step_no,
      coalesce(s.response, '{}'::jsonb),
      case when s.status = 'succeeded' then 'done' else 'failed' end);
    v_settled := v_settled + 1;
  end loop;

  -- 2. QUEUE the ready steps a registered, low-risk, reversible edge executor can run WITHOUT
  --    delivering a message to a person. See the note above: that last clause is why this exists.
  for s in
    select r.id, r.workflow_run_id, r.step_no, r.actor, r.action_class, r.input,
           e.target, e.risk_tier, e.reversible
      from public.workflow_step_run r
      join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = r.action_class
     where r.status = 'ready' and r.finished_at is null
       and e.kind in ('edge','rpc') and e.active
       and e.risk_tier = 'low' and e.advisory_safe and e.reversible
       and not e.notifies_human
       and coalesce(e.required_authority,'') <> 'founder'
       and not exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                        where x.idempotency_key = 'workflow_step:' || r.id)
     order by r.id
     limit greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 5), 1)
  loop
    v_key := 'workflow_step:' || s.id;
    insert into public.action_execution(id, correlation_id, action_class, executor, idempotency_key,
                                        risk_tier, reversible, request, status, attempts,
                                        workflow_step_run_id)
    values (gen_random_uuid(), gen_random_uuid(), s.action_class, s.target, v_key,
            s.risk_tier, s.reversible,
            jsonb_build_object('workflow_step_run_id', s.id,
                               'workflow_run_id', s.workflow_run_id,
                               'step_no', s.step_no,
                               'actor', s.actor,
                               'input', coalesce(s.input, '{}'::jsonb),
                               'source', 'fn_workflow_step_sweep'),
            'queued', 0, s.id)
    on conflict (idempotency_key) do nothing;

    update public.workflow_step_run set status = 'running' where id = s.id and status = 'ready';
    v_q := v_q + 1;
  end loop;

  -- IT KNEW ALL OF THIS AND TOLD NOBODY (12 Aug 2026). This function already computed
  -- ready_runnable, ready_held_notifies_human and never_finished, and returned them to
  -- `select public.fn_workflow_step_sweep(5);` in cron - which discards the value. So it has run
  -- every ten minutes computing an accurate diagnosis of a stalled engine and writing it nowhere.
  --
  -- Measured on production the day this line was added: 2,655 workflow_step_run rows, 195 ready and
  -- unfinished, and ZERO of the 195 executable - 132 carry no action_class at all and the other 63
  -- match no eligible executor. Every one of the 195 in-flight workflow runs is parked on a step
  -- nothing can pick up, which is why the whole table holds 5 'done' against 195 'running'.
  --
  -- The row below does not fix that. It makes it VISIBLE, which is the precondition: silence and
  -- health looked identical from outside this function.
  -- IT CALLED A WORKING THROTTLE A STALLED ENGINE (12 Aug 2026). The verdict below used to be
  --     case when v_parked > 0 and v_q = 0 and v_settled = 0 then 'error' else 'ok' end
  -- which reads "something is ready and this tick moved nothing, therefore the engine is stuck".
  -- That was true when it was written. It stopped being true the moment the reflection ceiling
  -- shipped: once the day's non-demand allowance is spent, moving nothing is the CORRECT behaviour
  -- and it stays correct until midnight UTC.
  --
  -- Measured on production today: 108 ready steps. 67 carry no action_class. The other 41 -
  -- health_report 21, knowledge_fill 19, coordinate 1 - pass every predicate in
  -- fn_workflow_step_claim: parent running, not employee_task, not founder-gated, actor resolves,
  -- and no safe executor owns them. They are unclaimed for exactly one reason:
  -- fn_task_is_demand() is false for all three, 24 reflection steps have already run today, and the
  -- cap is 6. The gate the founder asked for on 11 Aug is doing its job.
  --
  -- The old message asserted the opposite - "the rest match no eligible executor" - and raised
  -- status='error' on it every ten minutes, 144 times a day. it_health reads those rows, and I
  -- found its incident in decision_log verbatim: "10 agent run(s) failed in last 24h review failing
  -- jobs: workflow_step_sweep", risk medium, routed to the CTO. A whole escalation chain standing
  -- on a misread of a deliberate throttle.
  --
  -- So the verdict now separates three populations that were being added together:
  --   * throttled  - explained by the ceiling, a named policy with a number. Not an error.
  --   * unclassed  - steps no executor can EVER pick up. A real defect, but a standing backlog
  --                  rather than a ten-minute incident, so it is counted, named in the note, and
  --                  carried by one deduplicated org_task instead of 144 error rows a day.
  --   * true stall - ready, classified, and NOT explained by either. That is the only thing left
  --                  that nobody has accounted for, and it is the only thing that still raises.
  -- Nothing is hidden: every count stays in the payload and in the note. Only the severity changed,
  -- and it changed to match what the numbers actually say.
  select count(*), count(*) filter (where action_class is null)
    into v_parked, v_noclass
    from public.workflow_step_run where status = 'ready' and finished_at is null;

  select coalesce((value #>> '{}')::int, 6) into v_cap
    from public.decision_policy where key = 'workflow_reflection_steps_per_day';
  v_cap := coalesce(v_cap, 6);

  select count(*) into v_reflection_today
    from public.action_execution x
   where x.workflow_step_run_id is not null
     and x.created_at >= date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'utc') at time zone 'utc'
     and not public.fn_task_is_demand(x.action_class);

  -- Classified, unfinished, ready, and held back only because the day's reflection budget is gone.
  select count(*) into v_throttled
    from public.workflow_step_run sr
    join public.workflow_run r on r.id = sr.workflow_run_id
   where sr.status = 'ready' and sr.finished_at is null
     and sr.action_class is not null
     and r.status = 'running'
     and r.workflow_key <> 'employee_task'
     and coalesce(sr.input->>'gate','') <> 'founder'
     and not public.fn_task_is_demand(sr.action_class)
     and v_reflection_today >= v_cap;

  -- "UNEXPLAINED" WAS A SUBTRACTION, AND THE EXPLANATION WAS ONE JOIN AWAY (13 Aug 2026).
  --
  -- v_true_stall was parked - noclass - throttled: whatever is left after the two known reasons,
  -- declared a stall and raised every ten minutes. Measured on production, ALL 56 of those steps
  -- were three action_classes, and every one is refused by a deliberate rule this same function
  -- already knows how to read - it uses exactly this join for ready_runnable two lines below:
  --
  --   coordinate      25 ready   risk_tier=medium, advisory_safe=false  -> the dispatcher takes
  --                                                                        only low-risk advisory-safe
  --   health_report   18 ready   notifies_human=true                    -> the gate added 13 Aug so
  --                                                                        an executor cannot email him
  --   knowledge_fill  13 ready   kind=rpc, not edge                     -> the dispatcher invokes edge
  --
  -- A count reached by subtracting the reasons you thought of is a count of the reasons you did
  -- not, and calling that a stall pages a human 144 times a day about a policy working correctly.
  -- The reasons are now named, and only a step that is ready, classified, and ineligible for NO
  -- stated reason still raises - which is the thing nobody has accounted for.
  select count(*), string_agg(distinct why, '; ') into v_ineligible, v_why from (
    select sr.id,
           case when e.action_class is null then 'no executor is mapped to ' || sr.action_class
                when e.kind not in ('edge','rpc') then sr.action_class || ' is a ' || e.kind || ' executor and no invoker handles that kind'
                when not e.active then sr.action_class || ' executor is inactive'
                when e.risk_tier <> 'low' then sr.action_class || ' is risk_tier ' || e.risk_tier
                when not e.advisory_safe then sr.action_class || ' is not advisory_safe'
                when not e.reversible then sr.action_class || ' is not reversible'
                when e.notifies_human then sr.action_class || ' notifies a human'
           end as why
      from public.workflow_step_run sr
      left join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = sr.action_class
     where sr.status = 'ready' and sr.finished_at is null and sr.action_class is not null
  ) q where why is not null;
  v_ineligible := coalesce(v_ineligible, 0);
  v_true_stall := greatest(v_parked - v_noclass - v_throttled - v_ineligible, 0);

  v_out := jsonb_build_object(
    'settled', v_settled, 'queued', v_q, 'ran_at', now(),
    'parked', v_parked, 'parked_without_action_class', v_noclass,
    'parked_throttled_by_reflection_ceiling', v_throttled,
    'reflection_worked_today', v_reflection_today, 'reflection_cap', v_cap,
    'parked_ineligible_by_policy', v_ineligible,
    'parked_ineligible_because', coalesce(v_why, ''),
    'parked_unexplained', v_true_stall,
    'ready_runnable', (select count(*) from public.workflow_step_run r
                         join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = r.action_class
                        where r.status = 'ready' and e.kind in ('edge','rpc') and e.active
                          and e.risk_tier='low' and e.advisory_safe and e.reversible
                          and not e.notifies_human),
    'ready_held_notifies_human', (select count(*) from public.workflow_step_run r
                                    join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = r.action_class
                                   where r.status = 'ready' and e.notifies_human),
    'never_finished', (select count(*) from public.workflow_step_run where finished_at is null));

  v_status := case when v_true_stall > 0 and v_q = 0 and v_settled = 0 then 'error' else 'ok' end;
  v_note := 'settled ' || v_settled || ', queued ' || v_q || ', parked ' || v_parked
         || ' (' || v_noclass || ' awaiting an action_class, ' || v_throttled
         || ' held by the reflection ceiling at ' || v_reflection_today || '/' || v_cap || ' today, '
         || v_ineligible || ' ineligible by policy'
         || case when v_why is null or v_why = '' then '' else ' (' || left(v_why, 300) || ')' end
         || ', ' || v_true_stall || ' unexplained)';
  if v_status = 'error' then
    v_note := 'STALLED: ' || v_true_stall || ' workflow step(s) are ready, carry an action_class, '
           || 'and are not explained by the reflection ceiling. ' || v_note;
  end if;

  insert into public.agent_runs(agent, status, counts, note, started_at, finished_at)
  values ('workflow_step_sweep', v_status, v_out, v_note, now(), now());

  -- The unclassified backlog is a real defect and must not become invisible again just because it
  -- stopped shouting. One task, deduplicated on title, carries it.
  if v_noclass > 0 then
    begin
      insert into public.org_tasks (dept_key, title, detail, status, tier, needs_founder, action_class)
      select 'exec', 'Classify the workflow steps no executor can run',
             v_noclass || ' workflow_step_run row(s) are ready with no action_class, so nothing can '
             || 'ever pick them up and their runs never complete. The gap is in the DEFINITIONS: '
             || 'employee_task, rfq_handling, payment, refund, complaint, supplier_onboarding, '
             || 'customer_registration, invoice_approval, campaign_publishing and '
             || 'supplier_suspension carry no action_class on any step. Classifying them will make '
             || 'the queued backlog FIRE, so check org_action_executor.notifies_human, risk_tier '
             || 'and reversible per class first - refund reaches Stripe and needs the founder.',
             'proposed', 'gated', false, 'incident_fix'
      where not exists (select 1 from public.org_tasks
                         where title = 'Classify the workflow steps no executor can run'
                           and status <> 'done');
    exception when others then null; end;
  end if;

  return v_out;
end
fn_llm_log:
declare v_cost numeric := 0; v_in numeric; v_out numeric; v_cr numeric; v_cw numeric;
        v_cheaper boolean := false; v_reason text; v_alt text; v_class text;
        v_plain int; v_read int; v_write int;
        -- Added 11 Aug 2026 for the could_be_cheaper rewrite below.
        v_alt_model text; v_alt_rate numeric; v_used_rate numeric;
begin
  v_class := coalesce(nullif(trim(coalesce(p_task_class,'')), ''), case
    when p_fn ~* 'agent_brain|dept_plan|exec_agents|reflect|conductor'   then 'agent_reasoning'
    when p_fn ~* 'cos_execute|secretary|chief'                            then 'chief_of_staff_decision'
    when p_fn ~* 'knowledge|kb_|canon_eval|research|exam'                 then 'knowledge_research'
    when p_fn ~* 'extract|parse|ocr'                                      then 'document_extraction'
    when p_fn ~* 'classif|categor|intent|route'                           then 'category_classification'
    when p_fn ~* 'draft|content|blog|marketing|social'                    then 'content_drafting'
    when p_fn ~* 'quote|rfq|supplier|procure'                             then 'procurement_reasoning'
    else 'general_drafting' end);

  v_read  := greatest(coalesce(p_cached_in,0), 0);
  v_write := greatest(coalesce(p_cache_write,0), 0);
  v_plain := greatest(coalesce(p_prompt_tokens,0) - v_read - v_write, 0);

  if not coalesce(p_cached,false) then
    select in_aed_per_mtok, out_aed_per_mtok, cache_read_aed_per_mtok, cache_write_aed_per_mtok
      into v_in, v_out, v_cr, v_cw
      from model_rate where model = p_model;
    if v_in is not null then
      v_cost := round( v_plain/1000000.0 * v_in
                     + v_read /1000000.0 * coalesce(v_cr, v_in * 0.10)
                     + v_write/1000000.0 * coalesce(v_cw, v_in * 1.25)
                     + coalesce(p_output_tokens,0)/1000000.0 * v_out, 6);
    end if;
  end if;

  select deterministic_alternative into v_alt from model_policy where task_class = v_class;
  if v_alt is not null and v_alt <> '' then
    v_cheaper := true; v_reason := 'A deterministic path exists for this task class: ' || v_alt;
  -- THE WASTE DETECTOR NEVER LOOKED AT THE MODEL DOING THE SPENDING (fixed 11 Aug 2026).
  --
  -- The comparator was hardcoded to claude-sonnet-5 as the CHEAP side of the test:
  --     exists (... alt.model = 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5'
  --              where used.model = p_model and alt.in_aed_per_mtok < used.in_aed_per_mtok)
  -- so it could only ever fire for a model more expensive than sonnet-5, and by the input-rate
  -- ladder in model_rate that is exactly one model:
  --     flash-lite 0.92 < qwen 1.18 < haiku 3.67 < gemini-flash 5.51 < SONNET-5 7.35 < opus 18.36
  -- That was a reasonable rule when sonnet-5 was the cheap tier. It is not one now.
  --
  -- Measured over the 7 days to 11 Aug: could_be_cheaper fired on 179 calls - 175 of them on
  -- gemini-3.1-flash-lite (the CHEAPEST model in the fleet, 1.1% of spend, flagged by the
  -- deterministic branch above), 4 on opus, and ZERO on claude-sonnet-5 across 622 calls carrying
  -- 84% of all spend. The one field built to find waste was structurally blind to it.
  --
  -- Now it asks the actual question - is there a materially cheaper model than the one used - and
  -- names the cheapest so the reason is actionable rather than a boolean. The 2x threshold is
  -- deliberate: qwen at 1.18 against flash-lite at 0.92 is a 1.3x difference and flagging it would
  -- be noise, while sonnet-5 against flash-lite is 8x and is the finding.
  elsif not coalesce(p_cached,false) then
    select mr.model, mr.in_aed_per_mtok into v_alt_model, v_alt_rate
      from model_rate mr
     where mr.in_aed_per_mtok is not null
     order by mr.in_aed_per_mtok asc
     limit 1;
    select mr.in_aed_per_mtok into v_used_rate from model_rate mr where mr.model = p_model;
    if v_alt_model is not null and v_used_rate is not null
       and v_alt_rate * 2 <= v_used_rate then
      v_cheaper := true;
      v_reason := v_alt_model || ' costs ' || round(v_used_rate / nullif(v_alt_rate,0), 1)
               || 'x less on input than ' || p_model
               || ' (' || v_alt_rate || ' vs ' || v_used_rate || ' AED/Mtok). '
               || 'Whether it is good enough for this task class is a policy decision, not a fact - '
               || 'this flag is the question, not the answer.';
    end if;
  end if;

  insert into ai_cost_log (fn, dept_key, agent_key, task_class, model_used, model_selected_because,
    tier, prompt_tokens, output_tokens, cached, cache_hit_key, latency_ms, cost_aed,
    could_be_cheaper, cheaper_reason, ok, confidence, cached_in_tokens, cache_write_tokens)
  values (p_fn, p_dept, p_agent, v_class, p_model, p_because, p_tier,
    coalesce(p_prompt_tokens,0), coalesce(p_output_tokens,0), coalesce(p_cached,false),
    p_cache_key, p_latency_ms, v_cost, v_cheaper, v_reason, coalesce(p_ok,true),
    case when p_confidence is null then null
         when p_confidence >= 0 and p_confidence <= 1   then p_confidence
         when p_confidence > 1  and p_confidence <= 100 then round(p_confidence / 100.0, 4)
         else null end,
    v_read, v_write);

  return v_cost;
end
fn_goal_attainment:
with p as (
    select case p_horizon
             when 'monthly'   then to_char(now(),'YYYY-MM')
             when 'quarterly' then to_char(now(),'YYYY')||'-Q'||extract(quarter from now())::int
             else to_char(now(),'YYYY') end as label),
  s as (
    select g.actual_value, g.target_value, coalesce(cg.direction,'at_least') dir
      from goal_period g
      left join company_goals cg on cg.key = g.goal_key
      cross join p
     where g.horizon = p_horizon and g.period_label = p.label and g.target_value is not null)
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'horizon', p_horizon,
    'period', (select label from p),
    'goals_total', count(*),
    'goals_measured', count(*) filter (where actual_value is not null),
    'pct', round(avg(case
        -- NOT least(100, ...): least() ignores nulls, so an unmeasured goal scored 100%.
        when actual_value is null then null
        when dir in ('at_most','down')
          then least(100.0, case when actual_value = 0 then 100.0
                                 else 100.0 * target_value / nullif(actual_value,0) end)
        else least(100.0, 100.0 * actual_value / nullif(target_value,0)) end), 1))
  from s;
fn_runner_silence_watch:
declare r record; v_run bigint; n_alert int := 0; n_watched int := 0; v_email text;
begin
  insert into agent_runs(agent, started_at) values ('runner_silence_watch', clock_timestamp()) returning id into v_run;

  select to_email into v_email from notifications
   where type='founder_brief' and to_email is not null order by created_at desc limit 1;

  -- RE-DERIVE, NEVER SEED. One pass over 30 days of runs gives every runner its own observed
  -- cadence. A runner seen fewer than 5 times has no cadence worth calling regular and is recorded
  -- as on-demand rather than alerted on — which is what stops this becoming the noise generator the
  -- 18 July snapshot would have been if anything had ever read it.
  with runs as (
    select agent, started_at, counts,
           started_at - lag(started_at) over (partition by agent order by started_at) gap
      from agent_runs where started_at > now() - interval '30 days'),
  agg as (
    select agent,
           count(*) as n,
           -- A CADENCE IS NOT A BURST. Measured on the first run: doc_extract, match, quote_compare,
           -- inquiry_intake and stripe_webhook all showed a "median gap" of 0.00-0.08 hours, because
           -- they are EVENT-DRIVEN and fire in clusters when work arrives. Treating a cluster as a
           -- schedule makes every quiet day an alert. A real cadence shows up on separate DAYS, so
           -- that is what is counted.
           count(distinct started_at::date) as active_days,
           -- A RUNNER LOGGED ONLY ON EXCEPTIONS HAS NO CADENCE EITHER. cos_execute writes an
           -- agent_runs row under its own name ONLY when it has a throttled signal to report (a
           -- refused task start); its ordinary hourly work is logged under 'chief_of_staff'. So its
           -- rows stop the moment it stops having a PROBLEM, and the first version of this watch
           -- read that as the runner going silent -- alerting daily on a loop that was working.
           count(*) filter (where coalesce(counts ? 'signal', false)) as signal_rows,
           max(started_at) as last_seen,
           percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by extract(epoch from gap)/3600.0) as median_gap_h
      from runs group by agent)
  insert into agent_expectations (agent, kind, max_silence_hours, on_demand, median_gap_hours,
                                  runs_observed, last_seen, note, updated_at)
  select a.agent,
         case when exists (select 1 from org_agents o where o.agent_key = a.agent) then 'employee' else 'code' end,
         -- Three times its own median, floored at 6 hours and capped at two weeks. Derived from the
         -- runner rather than from its schedule, because the schedule is what fn_agent_silence_watch
         -- already checks and is exactly what stayed green while the work stopped.
         case when a.n >= 5 and a.active_days >= 5 and a.median_gap_h >= 0.5 and a.n > a.signal_rows
              then least(336, greatest(6, ceil(a.median_gap_h * 3)))
              else 999999 end,
         not (a.n >= 5 and a.active_days >= 5 and a.median_gap_h >= 0.5 and a.n > a.signal_rows),
         round(a.median_gap_h::numeric, 2),
         a.n,
         a.last_seen,
         case when a.n >= 5 and a.active_days >= 5 and a.median_gap_h >= 0.5 and a.n > a.signal_rows
              then 'cadence learned from '||a.n||' run(s) across '||a.active_days||' day(s) in 30d, median gap '||round(a.median_gap_h::numeric,2)||'h'
              else 'no steady cadence ('||a.n||' run(s) across '||a.active_days||' day(s), median gap '
                   ||coalesce(round(a.median_gap_h::numeric,2)::text,'n/a')||'h) — event-driven or on-demand, not watched' end,
         now()
    from agg a
  on conflict (agent) do update set
    kind = excluded.kind, max_silence_hours = excluded.max_silence_hours,
    on_demand = excluded.on_demand, median_gap_hours = excluded.median_gap_hours,
    runs_observed = excluded.runs_observed, last_seen = excluded.last_seen,
    note = excluded.note, updated_at = now();

  select count(*) into n_watched from agent_expectations where not on_demand;

  -- EVERY row, not just the watched ones. Scoping this to `not on_demand` left a stale silent=true
  -- on any runner that moved INTO on_demand — measured on the first run: five event-driven runners
  -- kept a silent flag they could no longer clear.
  update agent_expectations e
     set silent = (not e.on_demand
                   and e.last_seen is not null
                   and e.last_seen < now() - (e.max_silence_hours || ' hours')::interval);

  for r in select agent, kind, last_seen, max_silence_hours, median_gap_hours
             from agent_expectations where silent and not on_demand order by agent
  loop
    if not exists (select 1 from founder_alerts
                    where event='runner_silent' and detail like '%"'||r.agent||'"%'
                      and created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') then
      insert into founder_alerts(level, event, detail, channel)
      values (case when r.kind='employee' then 'high' else 'warn' end, 'runner_silent',
        jsonb_build_object('runner', r.agent, 'kind', r.kind,
          'last_run', r.last_seen::text,
          'silent_hours', round(extract(epoch from (now()-r.last_seen))/3600),
          'own_median_gap_hours', r.median_gap_hours,
          'expected_within_hours', r.max_silence_hours)::text, 'email');
      if v_email is not null and r.kind = 'employee' then
        insert into notifications(type,to_email,subject,body,status)
        values ('agent_silence', v_email,
          'Employee has stopped working: '||r.agent,
          'The runner "'||r.agent||'" last did anything at '||coalesce(r.last_seen::text,'unknown')||
          '. Its own observed cadence over the last 30 days is one run every '||
          coalesce(r.median_gap_hours::text,'?')||' hours, so it is now well past due. Its scheduled '||
          'job may still be succeeding — this watch looks at what the runner DID, not at whether its '||
          'schedule fired.','pending');
      end if;
      n_alert := n_alert + 1;
    end if;
  end loop;

  update agent_runs set finished_at=clock_timestamp(), status='ok',
      counts=jsonb_build_object('runners', (select count(*) from agent_expectations),
                                'watched', n_watched, 'silent', (select count(*) from agent_expectations where silent),
                                'alerts', n_alert,
                                'employees', (select count(*) from agent_expectations where kind='employee'))
   where id=v_run;

  return jsonb_build_object('runners',(select count(*) from agent_expectations),
                            'watched',n_watched,'alerts',n_alert);
exception when others then
  update agent_runs set finished_at=clock_timestamp(), status='error', note=left(sqlerrm,500) where id=v_run;
  raise;
end
fn_demo_marker_scan:
declare r record; n bigint;
begin
  for r in
    select c.table_name t, c.column_name k
      from information_schema.columns c
      join information_schema.tables tb
        on tb.table_schema = c.table_schema and tb.table_name = c.table_name
     where c.table_schema = 'public'
       and tb.table_type = 'BASE TABLE'
       and c.data_type in ('text','character varying','character')
     order by 1, 2
  loop
    begin
      execute format(
        'select count(*) from public.%I where %I ~* %L', r.t, r.k,
        'ZZ DEMO|example\.invalid|qd-demo') into n;
    exception when others then
      n := -1;   -- an unreadable column is reported, never silently counted as zero
    end;
    if n <> 0 then rel := r.t; col := r.k; rows := n; return next; end if;
  end loop;
end
fn_employee_kpi_measure:
declare n_ok int := 0; n_bad int := 0;
begin
  create temporary table if not exists _kpi_now on commit drop as
    select kpi_id, agent_key, actual, target, unit, attainment, verdict from fn_kpi_scoreboard();

  update employee_kpi k
     set actual_value = s.actual,
         measured_at  = case when s.actual is null then null else now() end
    from _kpi_now s where s.kpi_id = k.id;

  insert into employee_kpi_history
    (kpi_id, agent_key, actual_value, target_value, unit, attainment, verdict)
  select s.kpi_id, s.agent_key, s.actual, s.target, s.unit, s.attainment, s.verdict
    from _kpi_now s
  on conflict (kpi_id, measured_on) do update
    set actual_value = excluded.actual_value,
        target_value = excluded.target_value,
        unit         = excluded.unit,
        attainment   = excluded.attainment,
        verdict      = excluded.verdict,
        measured_at  = now();

  select count(*) filter (where measured_at is not null),
         count(*) filter (where measured_at is null and coalesce(measure_sql,'') <> '')
    into n_ok, n_bad
    from employee_kpi where active;
  return query select n_ok, n_bad;
end
fn_employee_scorecard:
declare
  v_cap  int := greatest(coalesce(p_max_chars, 1400), 300);
  v_out  text := '';
  v_line text;
begin
  p_agent_key := coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(p_agent_key), p_agent_key);
  if coalesce(btrim(p_agent_key),'') = '' then return null; end if;

  -- YOUR NUMBER. attainment mirrors fn_kpi_scoreboard exactly, including the percent_max
  -- inversion; it is NOT recomputed with a different rule, because two rules that must agree is
  -- how sec() and J() ended up with 8 and 11 variants of the same helper.
  -- An unmeasured KPI says so in words. It must never read as a zero.
  select string_agg(
           '- '||z.kpi||': target '||coalesce(z.target_value::text,'?')||' '||coalesce(z.unit,'')
           ||case
               when z.actual_value is null then ' — NOT MEASURED YET (no number exists; do not assume one)'
               else ' — you are at '||z.actual_value::text
                    ||case when z.target_value is null then ''
                    when z.target_value = 0 then
                      case when z.actual_value <= 0 then ', at the zero-defect target (MET)'
                           else ', against a target of ZERO (MISSED)' end
                           when z.unit = 'percent_max'
                             then ', '||round(least(100.0, 100.0 * z.target_value / nullif(z.actual_value,0)),0)::text||'% of target'
                           else ', '||round(100.0 * z.actual_value / z.target_value,0)::text||'% of target' end
                    ||case
                        when z.target_value is null or z.target_value = 0 then ''
                        when z.unit = 'percent_max' then
                          case when z.actual_value <= z.target_value then ' (MET)' else ' (MISSED)' end
                        else
                          case when z.actual_value >= z.target_value then ' (MET)'
                               when z.actual_value >= 0.9 * z.target_value then ' (NEAR)'
                               else ' (MISSED)' end end
             end
           ||case when z.serves_goal is not null then ' — serves company goal '||z.serves_goal else '' end,
           E'\n' order by z.kpi)
    into v_line
    from (select k.kpi, k.target_value, k.unit, k.actual_value, k.serves_goal
            from employee_kpi k
           where k.agent_key = p_agent_key and k.active
           order by k.kpi limit 8) z;

  if v_line is not null then
    v_out := v_out || E'\n# YOUR NUMBER RIGHT NOW — measured, not asserted\n' || v_line || E'\n';
  end if;

  -- YOUR DEPARTMENT'S OBJECTIVE and the company goal it serves. This is the chain the founder
  -- described, delivered to the one employee that has to act on it.
  select string_agg(
           '- '||d.objective
           ||case when d.target_value is not null then ' (target '||d.target_value::text||' '||coalesce(d.unit,'')||')' else '' end
           ||case when d.actual_value is not null then ', department is at '||d.actual_value::text
                  when d.measure_sql is not null then ', not yet measured'
                  else '' end
           ||case when g.key is not null then E'\n    serves company goal '||g.key||' — "'||g.goal||'"' else '' end,
           E'\n' order by d.sort, d.id)
    into v_line
    from department_objective d
    join org_agents a on a.agent_key = p_agent_key and a.department = d.dept_key
    left join company_goals g on g.key = d.goal_key and g.active
   where d.active
   limit 6;

  if v_line is not null then
    v_out := v_out || E'\n# WHAT YOUR DEPARTMENT IS FOR\n' || v_line || E'\n';
  end if;

  if v_out = '' then return null; end if;
  return left(v_out, v_cap);
end
fn_employee_kpi_trend:
with h as (
    select k.kpi, h.kpi_id, h.actual_value, h.unit, h.verdict, h.measured_on,
           first_value(h.actual_value) over w_asc  as first_v,
           first_value(h.actual_value) over w_desc as latest_v,
           first_value(h.verdict)      over w_desc as latest_verdict,
           row_number()                over w_desc as rn,
           count(*)                    over (partition by h.kpi_id) as n
      from employee_kpi_history h
      join employee_kpi k on k.id = h.kpi_id
     where h.agent_key = coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(p_agent_key), p_agent_key)
       and h.measured_on > (now() at time zone 'utc')::date - p_days
       and h.actual_value is not null
    window w_asc  as (partition by h.kpi_id order by h.measured_on),
           w_desc as (partition by h.kpi_id order by h.measured_on desc)
  )
  select kpi, unit, n,
         first_v, latest_v,
         case when n < 2 or first_v is null or latest_v is null then 'no trend yet'
              when latest_v = first_v then 'flat'
              when (unit = 'percent_max') = (latest_v < first_v) then 'improving'
              else 'worsening' end,
         latest_verdict
    from h where rn = 1
   order by kpi;
fn_cost_per_os:
declare
  v_since timestamptz := now() - make_interval(days => greatest(coalesce(p_days,30), 1));
  v_rows jsonb; v_total numeric; v_calls bigint; v_unattributed bigint;
  v_unpriceable bigint; v_unpriceable_tokens bigint; v_first_unpriceable date; v_last_unpriceable date;
begin
  select coalesce(sum(cost_aed),0), count(*),
         count(*) filter (where dept_key is null),
         count(*) filter (where coalesce(cost_aed,0)=0 and (coalesce(prompt_tokens,0)+coalesce(output_tokens,0))>0 and not coalesce(cached,false)),
         coalesce(sum(coalesce(prompt_tokens,0)+coalesce(output_tokens,0))
                  filter (where coalesce(cost_aed,0)=0 and (coalesce(prompt_tokens,0)+coalesce(output_tokens,0))>0 and not coalesce(cached,false)),0),
         min(occurred_at) filter (where coalesce(cost_aed,0)=0 and (coalesce(prompt_tokens,0)+coalesce(output_tokens,0))>0 and not coalesce(cached,false))::date,
         max(occurred_at) filter (where coalesce(cost_aed,0)=0 and (coalesce(prompt_tokens,0)+coalesce(output_tokens,0))>0 and not coalesce(cached,false))::date
    into v_total, v_calls, v_unattributed, v_unpriceable, v_unpriceable_tokens, v_first_unpriceable, v_last_unpriceable
    from ai_cost_log where occurred_at > v_since;

  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(x order by x->>'cost_aed' desc), '[]'::jsonb) into v_rows from (
    select jsonb_build_object(
             'os_key',       coalesce(d.os_key, '(unattributed)'),
             'departments',  count(distinct l.dept_key),
             'calls',        count(*),
             'tokens',       coalesce(sum(coalesce(l.prompt_tokens,0)+coalesce(l.output_tokens,0)),0),
             'cost_aed',     round(coalesce(sum(l.cost_aed),0), 4),
             'share_pct',    case when v_total > 0
                                  then round(100.0 * coalesce(sum(l.cost_aed),0) / v_total, 1)
                                  else null end,
             'cost_per_call', case when count(*) > 0
                                   then round(coalesce(sum(l.cost_aed),0) / count(*), 5) else null end
           ) x
      from ai_cost_log l
      left join os_department d on d.dept_key = l.dept_key
     where l.occurred_at > v_since
     group by coalesce(d.os_key, '(unattributed)')
  ) s;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'window_days', p_days,
    'since', v_since,
    'total_cost_aed', round(v_total, 4),
    'by_os', v_rows,
    -- THE COVERAGE TRAVELS WITH THE NUMBER. A caller cannot read one without the other.
    'coverage', jsonb_build_object(
      'calls', v_calls,
      'attributed_to_a_department', v_calls - v_unattributed,
      'unattributed', v_unattributed,
      'attributed_pct', case when v_calls > 0
                             then round(100.0 * (v_calls - v_unattributed) / v_calls, 1) else null end,
      'departments_seen', (select count(distinct dept_key) from ai_cost_log where occurred_at > v_since),
      'departments_active', (select count(*) from org_departments where active),
      'unpriceable_calls', v_unpriceable,
      'unpriceable_tokens', v_unpriceable_tokens,
      'unpriceable_window', case when v_unpriceable > 0
        then v_first_unpriceable::text || ' to ' || v_last_unpriceable::text else null end,
      'note', 'Unpriceable = real tokens, not cached, cost_aed 0. Those calls are counted in "calls" and contribute 0 to cost, so total_cost_aed is a FLOOR, not the spend. They are deliberately not repriced: applying today''s model_rate to past usage would report a number that was never charged.')
  );
end

fn_delete_proposer:
declare v_out jsonb := '[]'::jsonb; c record; v_n int; v_id bigint; v_prev record;
  v_specs jsonb := jsonb_build_array(
    jsonb_build_object('category','model_policy_by_identity_target_employee','agent','ai_director','risk','low',
      'title_suffix','imported model-policy rows that name no employee',
      'sql', $s$select count(*) from model_policy_by_identity where scope='target_employee'$s$,
      'why','96 rows scoped target_employee, 0 matching an org_agents.agent_key. DECIDED 11 Aug 2026: KEEP. They are the pack''s TARGET ORG CHART - department, title, manager and authority_tier for 96 roles - not dead routing config. routing_tier superseded their MODEL choice, not their org design. fn_ai_route reads only scope=''current_agent'', so they route nothing.'),
    jsonb_build_object('category','decorative_company_goals','agent','analytics_director','risk','medium',
      'title_suffix','Company goals that cannot be missed and cannot pull anything down',
      'sql', $s$select count(*) from company_goals g where g.active and coalesce(g.measure_sql,'')='' and coalesce(g.no_measure_reason,'')='' and not exists (select 1 from department_objective d where d.goal_key=g.key and d.active)$s$,
      'why','Active, no measure_sql, no department objective, AND no recorded reason why. A goal that cannot be measured cannot be missed. Giving it a measure or a written reason both count; leaving it silent does not.'),
    jsonb_build_object('category','orphan_agent_expectations','agent','it','risk','low',
      'title_suffix','agent_expectations rows watching something that does not exist',
      'sql', $s$select count(*) from agent_expectations e where public.fn_org_agent_resolve(e.agent) is null and coalesce(e.kind,'') <> 'code' and not exists (select 1 from cron.job j where j.jobname ilike '%'||e.agent||'%' or j.command ilike '%'||e.agent||'%')$s$,
      'why','Resolves to no employee through key OR alias, is not a code/job name, and matches no cron job. Each one can raise a silence alarm about a thing that cannot run, which is how an employee gets dispatched to diagnose nothing.'),
    jsonb_build_object('category','unmeasurable_employee_kpis','agent','analytics_director','risk','medium',
      'title_suffix','Employee KPIs with a target and no way to measure it',
      'sql', $s$select count(*) from employee_kpi k where k.active and coalesce(k.measure_sql,'')='' and coalesce(k.no_measure_reason,'')=''$s$,
      'why','An employee is told it is judged on something nobody can score, and nobody has written down why. Most need an instrument or demand that does not exist yet rather than deletion - a recorded reason closes this, a silent row does not.'),
    jsonb_build_object('category','inactive_org_agents','agent','hr_director','risk','low',
      'title_suffix','Employees marked inactive and still on the books',
      'sql', $s$select count(*) from org_agents where not coalesce(active,true)$s$,
      'why','An inactive employee still resolves in manager chains and still appears in joins that do not filter on active. Either reactivate it or remove it deliberately.')
  );
begin
  for c in select * from jsonb_array_elements(v_specs) as t(spec)
  loop
    execute (c.spec->>'sql') into v_n;
    if coalesce(v_n,0) = 0 then continue; end if;

    select id into v_id from public.agent_actions
     where kind = 'delete_proposal' and detail->>'category' = c.spec->>'category'
       and status = 'needs_review' limit 1;
    if v_id is not null then
      update public.agent_actions
         set title = v_n || ' — ' || (c.spec->>'title_suffix'),
             detail = coalesce(detail,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'count', v_n, 'why', c.spec->>'why', 'counted_by', c.spec->>'sql',
               'counted_at', now())
       where id = v_id;
      continue;
    end if;

    -- THE DECISION HOLDS UNTIL THE FACT CHANGES. A category answered 'keep' is not asked again at
    -- the same size or smaller. It IS asked again if the count grows past what was accepted, which
    -- is a different question about a different number.
    select (detail->>'count')::int as n, detail->>'decision' as decision
      into v_prev
      from public.agent_actions
     where kind = 'delete_proposal' and detail->>'category' = c.spec->>'category'
       and detail ? 'decision'
     order by id desc limit 1;
    if found and v_prev.decision in ('keep','keep_with_reason','retire')
       and v_n <= coalesce(v_prev.n, 0) then
      continue;
    end if;

    insert into public.agent_actions (agent, kind, status, risk, title, recommendation, detail)
    values (c.spec->>'agent', 'delete_proposal', 'needs_review', c.spec->>'risk',
            v_n || ' — ' || (c.spec->>'title_suffix'),
            'Decide deliberately: remove, retire (active=false), or keep with a stated reason. Do not close this without one of the three.',
            jsonb_build_object('category', c.spec->>'category', 'count', v_n,
              'why', c.spec->>'why', 'counted_by', c.spec->>'sql', 'counted_at', now(),
              'reopened_over', case when v_prev.n is null then null else v_prev.n end,
              'proposes','review for removal — this routine never deletes anything'));
    v_out := v_out || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('category', c.spec->>'category', 'count', v_n));
  end loop;

  insert into public.agent_runs(agent, status, counts, note, started_at, finished_at)
  values ('delete_proposer','ok', jsonb_build_object('opened', jsonb_array_length(v_out)),
          'delete proposals refreshed; ' || jsonb_array_length(v_out) || ' newly opened', now(), now());
  return v_out;
end
fn_workflow_run_follow_task:
declare v_run uuid;
begin
  if new.status is not distinct from old.status then return new; end if;
  if new.status not in ('done','failed','escalated') then return new; end if;

  for v_run in
    select r.id from public.workflow_run r
     where r.workflow_key = 'employee_task'
       and r.status = 'running'
       and (r.context->>'task_id') = new.id::text
  loop
    update public.workflow_step_run
       set status = 'skipped', finished_at = now(),
           output = coalesce(output, '{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
             'closed_by', 'owning_org_task', 'org_task_id', new.id,
             'org_task_status', new.status,
             'note', 'the owning task was performed and reviewed as one act; this step was never '
                     || 'separately observed, so it is skipped rather than claimed as done')
     where workflow_run_id = v_run and finished_at is null;

    update public.workflow_run
       set status      = case when new.status = 'done' then 'done' else 'failed' end,
           finished_at = now(),
           updated_at  = now(),
           context     = coalesce(context,'{}'::jsonb)
                         || jsonb_build_object('closed_by','owning_org_task',
                                               'org_task_status', new.status),
           error       = case when new.status = 'done' then null
                              else jsonb_build_object('owning_org_task', new.id,
                                                      'org_task_status', new.status) end
     where id = v_run;
  end loop;
  return new;
end
fn_workflow_step_claim:
declare v_out jsonb; v_today int; v_cap int; v_demand_ready int;
begin
  update public.workflow_step_run sr
     set status = 'ready'
   where sr.status = 'running'
     and sr.finished_at is null
     and sr.started_at < now() - interval '15 minutes'
     and not exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                      where x.workflow_step_run_id = sr.id
                        and x.status in ('queued','running','succeeded'));

  select coalesce((value #>> '{}')::int, 6) into v_cap
    from public.decision_policy where key = 'workflow_reflection_steps_per_day';
  v_cap := coalesce(v_cap, 6);

  -- NON-DEMAND ONLY. A supplier registration step worked this morning must not make the company
  -- refuse an inquiry step this afternoon.
  select count(*) into v_today
    from public.workflow_step_run sr
   where sr.output->>'worked_by' = 'workflow_dispatch'
     and sr.finished_at >= date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'utc') at time zone 'utc'
     and not public.fn_task_is_demand(sr.action_class);

  -- Is there revenue-path work waiting that the ceiling must not block? Same predicates as the pick,
  -- so this cannot claim the ceiling is irrelevant for a step the pick would reject anyway.
  select count(*) into v_demand_ready
    from public.workflow_step_run sr
    join public.workflow_run r on r.id = sr.workflow_run_id
   where sr.status = 'ready'
     and sr.finished_at is null
     and r.status = 'running'
     and r.workflow_key <> 'employee_task'
     and coalesce(sr.input->>'gate','') <> 'founder'
     and public.fn_task_is_demand(sr.action_class)
     and public.fn_workflow_actor_resolve(sr.workflow_run_id, sr.actor) is not null
     and not exists (
           select 1 from public.org_action_executor e
            where e.action_class = sr.action_class and e.active and e.kind = 'edge'
              and e.risk_tier = 'low' and e.advisory_safe and e.reversible
              and not e.notifies_human
              and coalesce(e.required_authority,'') <> 'founder');

  if v_today >= v_cap and v_demand_ready = 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object('capped', true, 'worked_today', v_today, 'cap', v_cap,
             'demand_ready', 0,
             'note', 'the daily reflection ceiling is spent and no revenue-path step is waiting; see '
                     || 'scripts/sql/the_dispatchers_ceiling_counted_revenue_work_against_reflection.sql');
  end if;

  with pick as (
    select sr.id
      from public.workflow_step_run sr
      join public.workflow_run r on r.id = sr.workflow_run_id
     where sr.status = 'ready'
       and sr.finished_at is null
       and r.status = 'running'
       and r.workflow_key <> 'employee_task'
       and coalesce(sr.input->>'gate','') <> 'founder'
       -- THE SPLIT. A revenue-path step is always claimable; a reflection step only while the
       -- day's ceiling holds.
       and (public.fn_task_is_demand(sr.action_class) or v_today < v_cap)
       and public.fn_workflow_actor_resolve(sr.workflow_run_id, sr.actor) is not null
       and not exists (
             select 1 from public.org_action_executor e
              where e.action_class = sr.action_class and e.active and e.kind = 'edge'
                and e.risk_tier = 'low' and e.advisory_safe and e.reversible
                and not e.notifies_human
                and coalesce(e.required_authority,'') <> 'founder')
     order by sr.id
     -- the reflection remainder PLUS whatever revenue-path work is waiting, so demand is not
     -- rationed by a counter that no longer counts it. See the overshoot note in the header.
     limit greatest(least(coalesce(p_limit, 5), greatest(v_cap - v_today, 0) + v_demand_ready), 1)
     for update of sr skip locked
  ), claimed as (
    update public.workflow_step_run sr
       set status = 'running', started_at = now()
      from pick
     where sr.id = pick.id
    returning sr.id, sr.workflow_run_id, sr.step_no, sr.actor, sr.action_class, sr.input
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'step_run_id',  c.id,
           'run_id',       c.workflow_run_id,
           'step_no',      c.step_no,
           'employee',     public.fn_workflow_actor_resolve(c.workflow_run_id, c.actor),
           'addressed_as', coalesce(c.input->>'addressed_as', c.actor),
           'action_class', c.action_class,
           'step',         c.input->>'step',
           'gate',         c.input->>'gate',
           'workflow_key', r.workflow_key,
           'workflow',     w.name,
           'context',      r.context,
           -- WHAT THIS RUN HAS ALREADY CONCLUDED. See the header: without this the process does not
           -- accumulate. Skipped steps are excluded on purpose - their note says the work was never
           -- separately observed, and passing that on as a finding would be a fabrication.
           'prior_steps', (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                                    'step_no', p.step_no,
                                    'step',    p.input->>'step',
                                    'by',      coalesce(p.output->>'employee', p.actor),
                                    'outcome', left(coalesce(p.output->>'outcome',
                                                             p.output->>'note', ''), 600))
                                  order by p.step_no), '[]'::jsonb)
                             from (select p2.* from public.workflow_step_run p2
                                    where p2.workflow_run_id = c.workflow_run_id
                                      and p2.step_no < c.step_no
                                      and p2.status = 'done'
                                      and coalesce(p2.output->>'outcome', p2.output->>'note','') <> ''
                                    order by p2.step_no desc
                                    limit 3) p)
         ) order by c.id), '[]'::jsonb)
    into v_out
    from claimed c
    join public.workflow_run r on r.id = c.workflow_run_id
    left join public.workflow w on w.workflow_key = r.workflow_key;

  return v_out;
end

fn_ai_confidence_prior:
-- A CONSTANT IS NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND THIS IS THE GUARD THAT SAYS SO.
  -- The founder's own reading of the two existing emitters: "always emit exactly 1.000, which
  -- carries no information". A model that reports the same number every time would otherwise
  -- downgrade itself to a cheaper tier on the strength of its own unvarying optimism. stddev = 0
  -- over the window means the signal has no content, so it does not route anything. n >= 5 for the
  -- same reason at the other end: one confident answer is an anecdote.
  select case
           when count(*) >= 5 and coalesce(stddev_samp(confidence), 0) > 0
           then jsonb_build_object(
                  'prior', round(percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by confidence)::numeric, 4),
                  'n', count(*),
                  'spread', round(stddev_samp(confidence)::numeric, 4))
           else null
         end
    from public.ai_cost_log
   where agent_key = coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(p_agent_key), p_agent_key)
     and task_class = p_task_class
     and confidence is not null
     and occurred_at > now() - interval '14 days';
fn_task_is_demand:
select coalesce(p_action_class,'') ~*
    -- the revenue path: someone outside the company is on the other end of it
    '(invite|quote|rfq|inquir|lead|customer|supplier|onboard|registration|approv|kyc|collection|payment|refund|dispute|contract|delivery|fulfil)'
fn_cos_work_gate:
declare
  v_budget int;
  v_used   int;
  v_demand int;
  v_reflect int;
  v_classes jsonb;
begin
  select coalesce((value #>> '{}')::int, 6) into v_budget
    from public.decision_policy where key = 'cos_reflection_tasks_per_day';
  v_budget := coalesce(v_budget, 6);

  select count(*) into v_used
    from public.org_tasks k
   where k.last_run_at >= date_trunc('day', (now() at time zone 'utc')) at time zone 'utc'
     and not public.fn_task_is_demand(k.action_class)
     -- NOT `result->>'mode' <> 'executed_by_invoker'`, which is what this said first and it
     -- over-counted by ten on the first run. That mode is written by fn_action_invoke_collect at
     -- COLLECT time, so a task the invoker dispatched at :45 and has not collected yet still reads
     -- mode NULL and was counted as model work. The ten 'Supply gap' knowledge_acquire tasks in
     -- flight this morning are exactly that: kb_deepen at 0.026 AED a call, charged against a
     -- ceiling meant for a 25,000-token one. The invoker ALWAYS leaves an action_execution row and
     -- the cos_execute model path never does, so the row is the reliable discriminator and it is
     -- true from dispatch, not from collection.
     and not exists (
       select 1 from public.action_execution a
        where (a.request->>'org_task_id') = k.id::text
          and a.created_at >= date_trunc('day', (now() at time zone 'utc')) at time zone 'utc');

  select count(*) filter (where not public.fn_task_is_demand(action_class))
    into v_reflect
    from public.org_tasks where status in ('assigned','in_progress');

  -- The concrete classes cos_execute may select on. PostgREST cannot evaluate the regex above, so
  -- the gate resolves it here against the classes that ACTUALLY have open work and hands back a
  -- list. One source of truth, and the edge function carries no copy of the pattern.
  --
  -- AND IT REFUSES ANY CLASS WIRED TO AN UNSAFE EXECUTOR. This gate moves demand work to the FRONT
  -- of cos_execute's queue, and a cost control must never widen a risk. Found on the first run, and
  -- it was not hypothetical: org_tasks 1360 and 1361 - "Start invites: kitchen-and-bathroom-
  -- suppliers", "Start invites: real-estate-agencies" - are action_class='invite', tier='autonomous',
  -- status='assigned', wired to fn_org_exec_invite with risk_tier='high', advisory_safe=false,
  -- reversible=false. They carry the HIGHEST ids in a 385-row FIFO queue, so today they are
  -- unreachable; promoting 'invite' to the head of the queue would have put a high-risk irreversible
  -- supplier mailing first in line, on the exact day the founder wrote "LAST — supplier invites. DO
  -- NOT ENABLE YET" because the bounce rate is at the platform's own 0.08 brake.
  --
  -- A class is eligible only if NO active executor for it is high-risk, irreversible or not
  -- advisory-safe. This is the same triple fn_org_task_execute_sweep already requires before it will
  -- invoke anything; the two paths now agree instead of disagreeing.
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(distinct k.action_class), '[]'::jsonb) into v_classes
    from public.org_tasks k
   where k.status in ('assigned','in_progress')
     and k.action_class is not null
     and public.fn_task_is_demand(k.action_class)
     and not exists (
       select 1 from public.org_action_executor e
        where e.action_class = k.action_class and e.active
          and (e.risk_tier <> 'low' or not e.advisory_safe or not e.reversible));

  -- demand_open counts ELIGIBLE demand only — the same set cos_execute can actually select. Counting
  -- every demand-classed row here would report "2 revenue-path tasks still run uncapped" for two
  -- invite tasks the gate has just refused to hand over, and gated=false would then describe a run
  -- that in fact calls no model. The number and the decision have to come from one set.
  select count(*) into v_demand
    from public.org_tasks
   where status in ('assigned','in_progress')
     and action_class is not null
     and v_classes ? action_class;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'demand_classes',         v_classes,
    'reflection_budget',      v_budget,
    'reflection_used_today',  v_used,
    'reflection_allowed',     v_used < v_budget,
    'demand_open',            v_demand,
    'reflection_open',        v_reflect,
    -- nothing at all to do without a model: the ceiling is spent AND no revenue-path task is waiting
    'gated',                  (v_used >= v_budget and v_demand = 0),
    'reason', case
        when v_used < v_budget then
          'reflection ' || v_used || '/' || v_budget || ' today; working normally'
        when v_demand > 0 then
          'reflection ceiling reached (' || v_used || '/' || v_budget || '); ' || v_demand ||
          ' revenue-path task(s) still run uncapped'
        else
          'reflection ceiling reached (' || v_used || '/' || v_budget || ') and no revenue-path task '
          'is waiting, so no model is called this run'
      end
  );
end
fn_supplier_capability_derive:
declare v_written int := 0; v_skipped_no_trade int := 0; v_candidates int := 0;
begin
  with cand as (
    select l.id,
           public.fn_norm_trades(
             coalesce(l.company_name,'')||' '||coalesce(l.categories,'')||' '||
             coalesce(l.sector,'')||' '||coalesce(l.services,'')||' '||coalesce(l.products,'')) as trades,
           -- ROLES AT INSERT, not by a later sweep. See the header: the sweep is what had to be
           -- repeated, and a row written without a role is a row no supplier can confirm.
           public.fn_lead_role_codes(l.business_role) as roles,
           array_remove(array[nullif(btrim(coalesce(l.emirate,'')),'')]
                        || coalesce(l.service_emirates,'{}'::text[]), null) as emirates,
           (select coalesce(array_agg(distinct btrim(x)) filter (where btrim(x) <> ''), '{}')
              from unnest(string_to_array(regexp_replace(coalesce(l.products,''), '[;|/]', ',', 'g'), ',')) x
             where length(btrim(x)) between 2 and 80) as products_norm,
           (select coalesce(array_agg(distinct btrim(x)) filter (where btrim(x) <> ''), '{}')
              from unnest(string_to_array(regexp_replace(coalesce(l.services,''), '[;|/]', ',', 'g'), ',')) x
             where length(btrim(x)) between 2 and 80) as services_norm
      from public.leads l
     where not (coalesce(l.company_name,'') ilike 'ZZ DEMO%' or coalesce(l.email,'') ilike '%@example.invalid')
       and coalesce(l.banned, false) = false
       and not exists (select 1 from public.supplier_capabilities s where s.supplier_id = l.id)
     order by l.id
     limit p_limit
  ), ins as (
    insert into public.supplier_capabilities as sc (
      supplier_id, trades, roles, coverage_emirates, products_norm, services,
      extracted_at, updated_at, extractor_version, review_status, completeness,
      missing_fields, source_docs)
    select c.id, c.trades, c.roles, c.emirates, c.products_norm[1:40], c.services_norm[1:40],
           now(), now(), 'derived_from_directory_v2', 'derived',
           round(( (array_length(c.trades,1) > 0)::int
                 + (array_length(c.emirates,1) > 0)::int
                 + (array_length(c.products_norm,1) > 0)::int
                 + (array_length(c.services_norm,1) > 0)::int )::numeric / 4, 2),
           array_remove(array[
             case when array_length(c.products_norm,1) is null then 'products' end,
             case when array_length(c.emirates,1)      is null then 'coverage_emirates' end,
             'brands','certifications','team_size','min_project_value','max_project_value'
           ], null),
           jsonb_build_object(
             'derived_from','leads directory (company_name, categories, sector, services, products, emirate, business_role)',
             'method','fn_norm_trades over taxonomy_trade aliases + fn_lead_role_codes - deterministic, no model call',
             'confirmed_by_supplier', false,
             'at', now())
    from cand c
    where array_length(c.trades,1) > 0
    returning 1
  )
  select (select count(*) from ins), (select count(*) from cand),
         (select count(*) from cand where array_length(trades,1) is null)
    into v_written, v_candidates, v_skipped_no_trade;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'candidates', v_candidates,
    'written', v_written,
    'skipped_no_trade', v_skipped_no_trade,
    'total_capability_rows', (select count(*) from public.supplier_capabilities),
    'confirmable', (select count(*) from public.supplier_capabilities
                     where array_length(trades,1) > 0 and array_length(roles,1) > 0),
    'confirmed_rows', (select count(*) from public.supplier_capabilities where confirmed_at is not null),
    'note', 'derived rows are UNCONFIRMED on purpose: fn_match_capability still refuses them until '
            'the supplier confirms their own scope. This gives that conversation something to be about.');
end

fn_org_task_assign:
declare v_assigned int := 0; v_no_capacity int := 0; v_considered int := 0; v_saturated text;
begin
  with open_tasks as (
    select t.id, t.dept_key, t.created_at, t.action_class
      from public.org_tasks t
     where t.assigned_agent is null
       and t.status in ('assigned','in_progress')
     order by t.created_at
     limit greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 200), 1)
  ),
  load as (
    select a.agent_key, a.department, coalesce(a.max_open_tasks, 6) as cap,
           coalesce(r.runtime_mode, 'on_demand_specialist') as runtime_mode,
           (select count(*) from public.org_tasks o
             where o.assigned_agent = a.agent_key and o.status in ('assigned','in_progress')) as open_now,
           case when p.tier = 'probation' then 1 else 0 end as probation_rank
      from public.org_agents a
      left join public.agent_reputation p on p.agent_key = a.agent_key
      left join public.org_role r on r.runtime_agent_key = a.agent_key and r.status = 'active'
     where a.active
       and coalesce(a.available, true)
       and (a.unavailable_until is null or a.unavailable_until < now())
  ),
  ranked as (
    select ot.id as task_id, l.agent_key, l.cap, l.open_now,
           row_number() over (partition by ot.id
                              order by l.probation_rank, l.open_now, l.agent_key) as pick,
           row_number() over (partition by l.agent_key
                              order by ot.created_at, ot.id) as nth_for_agent
      from open_tasks ot
      join load l on l.department = ot.dept_key
      -- AN INDEPENDENT REVIEWER CARRYING THE DEPARTMENT'S ROUTINE QUEUE IS NOT INDEPENDENT OF IT.
      -- Review work still reaches them: the review action classes are the exception, and
      -- fn_pick_reviewer routes review directly rather than through this queue.
     where l.runtime_mode <> 'independent_reviewer'
        or coalesce(ot.action_class,'') in ('review','audit','verify','qa_gate','security_review',
                                            'compliance_check','legal_review','supplier_verify',
                                            'capability_review','self_review')
  ),
  chosen as (
    select task_id, agent_key from ranked
     where pick = 1 and (open_now + nth_for_agent) <= cap
  ),
  done as (
    update public.org_tasks t
       set assigned_agent = c.agent_key, updated_at = now()
      from chosen c
     where t.id = c.task_id and t.assigned_agent is null
    returning t.id
  )
  select (select count(*) from done), (select count(*) from open_tasks)
    into v_assigned, v_considered;

  v_no_capacity := v_considered - v_assigned;

  select string_agg(x.dept_key||' '||x.unowned||'/'||x.capacity, ', ' order by x.unowned desc)
    into v_saturated
    from (select t.dept_key, count(*) as unowned,
                 (select coalesce(sum(coalesce(a.max_open_tasks,6)),0) from public.org_agents a
                   where a.active and coalesce(a.available,true) and a.department = t.dept_key) as capacity
            from public.org_tasks t
           where t.assigned_agent is null and t.status in ('assigned','in_progress')
           group by t.dept_key
          having count(*) > 0
           order by count(*) desc
           limit 6) x;

  insert into public.agent_runs (agent, started_at, finished_at, status, counts, note)
  values ('org_task_assign', now(), now(), 'ok',
          jsonb_build_object('considered', v_considered, 'assigned', v_assigned,
                             'left_unowned', v_no_capacity, 'oversubscribed', coalesce(v_saturated,'none')),
          'Assigned '||v_assigned||' of '||v_considered||' unowned open task(s) to a named employee '
          ||'in the owning department, skipping independent reviewers for non-review work. '
          ||v_no_capacity||' left unowned because no colleague in that department had capacity '
          ||'under max_open_tasks - deliberate: an unowned task is visible, an overloaded one is '
          ||'not. Departments carrying more open work than they staff (unowned/capacity): '
          ||coalesce(v_saturated,'none')||'.');

  return jsonb_build_object('considered', v_considered, 'assigned', v_assigned,
                            'left_unowned', v_no_capacity, 'oversubscribed', coalesce(v_saturated,'none'));
end
fn_rfq_redispatch_sweep:
declare
  r record;
  v_ref text; v_secret text;
  v_sent int := 0; v_eligible int := 0;
begin
  select value into v_secret from app_secrets where key = 'cred_db_internal';
  if v_secret is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('error', 'cred_db_internal missing', 'ran_at', now());
  end if;

  select value into v_ref from app_secrets where key = 'project_ref';
  if v_ref is null then
    select substring(command from 'https://([a-z]+)[.]supabase[.]co') into v_ref
      from cron.job where command like '%supabase.co/functions/v1/%' limit 1;
  end if;
  if v_ref is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('error', 'cannot determine project ref', 'ran_at', now());
  end if;

  select count(*) into v_eligible
    from public.inquiries i
   where i.rfq_ready is true
     and i.status in ('open', 'sent', 'split')
     and (i.routing->>'dispatched_at') is not null
     and (i.routing->>'fanout') is not null and (i.routing->>'fanout')::int = 0
     and i.created_at > now() - interval '90 days'
     and coalesce((i.routing->>'redispatch_count')::int, 0) < 30
     and coalesce((i.routing->>'redispatch_last')::timestamptz, 'epoch'::timestamptz)
           < now() - interval '6 hours';

  for r in
    select i.id
      from public.inquiries i
     where i.rfq_ready is true
       and i.status in ('open', 'sent', 'split')
       and (i.routing->>'dispatched_at') is not null
       and (i.routing->>'fanout') is not null and (i.routing->>'fanout')::int = 0
       and i.created_at > now() - interval '90 days'
       and coalesce((i.routing->>'redispatch_count')::int, 0) < 30
       and coalesce((i.routing->>'redispatch_last')::timestamptz, 'epoch'::timestamptz)
             < now() - interval '6 hours'
     order by i.created_at
     limit greatest(p_limit, 0)
  loop
    -- Stamped BEFORE the call, so a request that never comes back still consumes its attempt and
    -- the backoff holds. dispatched_at is left alone: it records a real historical event and the
    -- fixed guard no longer treats a zero-fanout run as a dispatch.
    update public.inquiries
       set routing = coalesce(routing, '{}'::jsonb)
                   || jsonb_build_object(
                        'redispatch_last', now(),
                        'redispatch_count', coalesce((routing->>'redispatch_count')::int, 0) + 1)
     where id = r.id;

    perform net.http_post(
      url     := 'https://' || v_ref || '.supabase.co/functions/v1/dispatch_inquiry',
      headers := jsonb_build_object('Content-Type', 'application/json'),
      body    := jsonb_build_object('__secret', v_secret, 'inquiry_id', r.id));

    v_sent := v_sent + 1;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ran_at', now(), 'eligible', v_eligible, 'retried', v_sent, 'limit', p_limit,
    'note', case when v_eligible = 0
                 then 'No RFQ is waiting on supply. Nothing to retry.'
                 else v_sent || ' of ' || v_eligible || ' RFQs that reached zero suppliers were '
                      || 'offered to the matcher again; supply may have arrived since they were created.'
            end);
end
fn_capability_enrich_sweep:
declare
  r record;
  v_ref text; v_secret text;
  v_sent int := 0; v_eligible int := 0;
begin
  select value into v_secret from app_secrets where key = 'cred_db_internal';
  if v_secret is null then

  select count(*) into v_eligible

     and coalesce((l.enrich_retry->>'last')::timestamptz, 'epoch'::timestamptz) < now() - interval '12 hours';

  for r in
    select l.id
      from public.leads l
     where l.approval_status = 'approved'
       and l.capability_enriched_at is null
       and l.claimed_by is not null
       and l.claimed_by not ilike '%@example.%'

     order by l.id
     limit greatest(p_limit, 0)
  loop
    -- Stamped BEFORE the call so a request that never returns still consumes its attempt and the
    -- backoff holds. capability_enriched_at is left for enrich_capability to set: this routine
    -- records that it ASKED, never that the work was done.
    update public.leads
       set enrich_retry = coalesce(enrich_retry, '{}'::jsonb)
                        || jsonb_build_object(
                             'last', now(),
                             'count', coalesce((enrich_retry->>'count')::int, 0) + 1)
     where id = r.id;

    perform net.http_post(
      url     := 'https://' || v_ref || '.supabase.co/functions/v1/enrich_capability',
      headers := jsonb_build_object('Content-Type', 'application/json'),
      body    := jsonb_build_object('__secret', v_secret, 'lead_id', r.id));

    v_sent := v_sent + 1;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'ran_at', now(), 'eligible', v_eligible, 'retried', v_sent, 'limit', p_limit,
    'note', case when v_eligible = 0
                 then 'Every claimed, approved supplier has a capability record. Nothing to retry.'
                 else v_sent || ' approved supplier(s) had no capability record and were re-sent to '
                      || 'enrich_capability; without one they are invisible to the matcher and to every RFQ.'
            end);
end
