fn_wa_context:
declare v_e164 text; v_email text; v_lead record; v_cust record;
begin
  -- ONE IDENTIFIER, TWO SHAPES. wa_from arrives as 'whatsapp:+9715...'; a browser session arrives
  -- as an email address. An '@' is the discriminator: nothing that is a phone number contains one,
  -- and an address stripped of non-digits is meaningless, which is how a mis-shaped identifier used
  -- to fall through to "known: false" instead of an answer.
  v_email := nullif(lower(btrim(coalesce(p_phone, ''))), '');
  if v_email is not null and position('@' in v_email) = 0 then v_email := null; end if;
  v_e164 := regexp_replace(coalesce(p_phone, ''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g');
  if v_e164 = '' and v_email is null then return jsonb_build_object('scope','none'); end if;

  -- ---------------------------------------------------------------- FOUNDER: the company itself
  if p_audience = 'founder' then
    return jsonb_build_object(
      'scope','company',
      'suppliers', jsonb_build_object(
        'leads_total',      (select count(*) from leads),
        'claimed',          (select count(*) from leads where coalesce(claimed,false)),
        'claimed_real',     (select count(*) from leads where coalesce(claimed,false)
                              and not (coalesce(company_name,'') ilike 'ZZ DEMO%' or coalesce(email,'') ilike '%@example.invalid')),
        'approved',         (select count(*) from leads where approval_status = 'approved'),
        'licence_verified', (select count(*) from leads where coalesce(verified,false)),
        'with_email',       (select count(*) from leads where coalesce(btrim(email),'') <> '')),
      'invites', jsonb_build_object(
        'enabled',      (select value from app_secrets where key='invite_enabled'),
        'daily_cap',    (select value from app_secrets where key='invite_daily_cap'),
        'sent_today',   (select count(*) from leads where invited_at >= date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'utc')),
        'sent_7d',      (select count(*) from leads where invited_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
        'bounced_7d',   (select count(*) from leads where invite_status='bounced' and invited_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
        'uncontacted',  (select count(*) from leads where invited_at is null and coalesce(btrim(email),'') <> '')),
      'demand', jsonb_build_object(
        'customers',        (select count(*) from customers),
        'inquiries_total',  (select count(*) from inquiries),
        'inquiries_7d',     (select count(*) from inquiries where created_at > now() - interval '7 days'),
        'quotes_total',     (select count(*) from quotes),
        'quotes_7d',        (select count(*) from quotes where created_at > now() - interval '7 days')),
      'money', jsonb_build_object(
        'transactions',      (select count(*) from transactions),
        'revealed',          (select count(*) from transactions where revealed_at is not null),
        'ai_spend_today_aed',(select round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed),0)::numeric,2) from ai_cost_log where occurred_at >= current_date),
        'ai_spend_month_aed',(select round(coalesce(sum(cost_aed),0)::numeric,2) from ai_cost_log where occurred_at >= date_trunc('month', now()))),
      'health', jsonb_build_object(
        'agent_runs_failed_24h', (select count(*) from agent_runs where status in ('error','failed') and started_at > now() - interval '24 hours'),
        'actions_pending',       (select count(*) from agent_actions where status in ('pending','needs_review')),
        'escalations_open',      (select count(*) from agent_actions where coalesce(escalated,false) and status in ('pending','needs_review'))),
      -- THE PART THAT IS HIS. Named so the model cannot read it as more company telemetry: these
      -- are items no agent is allowed to settle, and they are waiting for him specifically.
      'your_decision_queue', public.fn_founder_queue(12));
  end if;

  -- ---------------------------------------------------------------- SUPPLIER: only their own row
  if p_audience = 'supplier' then
    select * into v_lead from leads l
     where (v_e164 <> '' and (regexp_replace(coalesce(l.phone_e164, l.phone, ''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') = v_e164
                           or regexp_replace(coalesce(l.whatsapp,''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') = v_e164))
        or (v_email is not null and (lower(coalesce(l.claimed_by,'')) = v_email or lower(coalesce(l.email,'')) = v_email))
     order by coalesce(l.claimed,false) desc, l.id limit 1;
    if not found then return jsonb_build_object('scope','supplier','known', false); end if;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'scope','supplier', 'known', true,
      'company', v_lead.company_name,
      'account', jsonb_build_object('email', v_lead.claimed_by, 'phone', coalesce(v_lead.phone_e164, v_lead.phone)),
      'profile', jsonb_build_object(
        'claimed',          coalesce(v_lead.claimed,false),
        'approval_status',  coalesce(v_lead.approval_status,'not submitted'),
        'verified',         coalesce(v_lead.verified,false),
        'email_verified',   coalesce(v_lead.owner_email_verified,false),
        'phone_verified',   coalesce(v_lead.owner_phone_verified,false),
        'trade_licence_no', v_lead.trade_license_no,
        'licence_authority',v_lead.license_authority,
        'licence_expiry',   v_lead.license_expiry,
        'licence_on_file',  (v_lead.license_doc_path is not null),
        'blocked_because',  v_lead.licence_gate_reason),
      'work', jsonb_build_object(
        'inquiries_received',  (select count(*) from inquiry_matches m where m.supplier_id = v_lead.id),
        'inquiries_quoted',    (select count(distinct q.inquiry_id) from quotes q where q.supplier_id = v_lead.id),
        'inquiries_missed',    (select count(*) from inquiry_matches m where m.supplier_id = v_lead.id
                                  and not exists (select 1 from quotes q where q.inquiry_id = m.inquiry_id and q.supplier_id = v_lead.id)),
        'quotes_submitted',    (select count(*) from quotes q where q.supplier_id = v_lead.id),
        'last_quote',          (select jsonb_build_object('amount_aed', q.quote_amount, 'status', q.status, 'when', q.created_at)
                                  from quotes q where q.supplier_id = v_lead.id order by q.created_at desc limit 1),
        'jobs_won',            (select count(*) from quotes q where q.supplier_id = v_lead.id and q.status = 'accepted')));
  end if;

  -- ---------------------------------------------------------------- CUSTOMER: only their own rows
  if p_audience = 'customer' then
    select * into v_cust from customers c
     where (v_e164 <> '' and regexp_replace(coalesce(c.phone,''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') = v_e164)
        or (v_email is not null and lower(coalesce(c.email,'')) = v_email)
     limit 1;
    if not found then return jsonb_build_object('scope','customer','known', false); end if;

    return jsonb_build_object(
      'scope','customer', 'known', true,
      'name', v_cust.full_name,
      -- WHAT WE HOLD FOR THEM. "what is my email registered" was one of the four questions the
      -- assistant could not answer, and the answer was one column away the whole time.
      'account', jsonb_build_object(
        'email', v_cust.email, 'phone', v_cust.phone,
        'language', v_cust.locale, 'industry', v_cust.industry,
        'customer_since', v_cust.created_at),
      'profile', jsonb_build_object(
        'phone_verified', coalesce(v_cust.phone_verified,false),
        'email_verified', coalesce(v_cust.email_verified,false),
        'terms_signed',   (v_cust.signed_terms_url is not null),
        -- create_inquiry's own gate, stated as the fact it is, so the assistant answers "can I post
        -- a request" with the truth rather than an encouragement.
        'can_post_request', (coalesce(v_cust.phone_verified,false) and coalesce(v_cust.email_verified,false)
                             and v_cust.signed_terms_url is not null)),
      'inquiries', coalesce((
        select jsonb_agg(x order by x->>'created_at' desc) from (
          select jsonb_build_object(
            'id', i.id, 'category', i.category, 'emirate', i.emirate, 'status', i.status,
            'created_at', i.created_at,
            'suppliers_received', (select count(*) from inquiry_matches m where m.inquiry_id = i.id),
            'quotes_received',    (select count(*) from quotes q where q.inquiry_id = i.id and q.status='submitted'),
            -- PRE-REVEAL: a band and a count, never the individual quotes and never a supplier name.
            'revealed', exists (select 1 from transactions t where t.inquiry_id = i.id and t.revealed_at is not null),
            'price_band', case
              when exists (select 1 from transactions t where t.inquiry_id = i.id and t.revealed_at is not null)
                then (select jsonb_build_object('low', min(q.quote_amount), 'high', max(q.quote_amount), 'average', round(avg(q.quote_amount)::numeric,0))
                        from quotes q where q.inquiry_id = i.id and q.status='submitted')
              else (select case when count(*) = 0 then null
                                else jsonb_build_object('average_rounded_to_nearest_1000',
                                        round(avg(q.quote_amount)::numeric / 1000) * 1000, 'note',
                                        'rounded band only - the exact quotes and the supplier names unlock when you reveal')
                           end from quotes q where q.inquiry_id = i.id and q.status='submitted') end) as x
          from inquiries i where i.customer_id = v_cust.id order by i.created_at desc limit 10) z), '[]'::jsonb));
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('scope','unknown');
end

fn_os_ai_quality:
with nights as (
  select at, row_number() over (order by at desc) rn
  from (select distinct at from public.ai_quality_snapshots) d
),
latest_at as (select at from nights where rn = 1),
-- one row per agent for the most recent night, whichever era wrote it
latest as (
  select s.agent,
         round(sum(s.override_pct * greatest(s.actions_30d,1))::numeric
               / nullif(sum(greatest(s.actions_30d,1)),0), 1) as override_pct,
         sum(s.actions_30d)::int as actions_30d
  from public.ai_quality_snapshots s
  where s.at = (select at from latest_at)
  group by s.agent
),
-- the trailing picture, excluding the night we are reporting on
prev as (
  select s.agent,
         round(sum(s.override_pct * greatest(s.actions_30d,1))::numeric
               / nullif(sum(greatest(s.actions_30d,1)),0), 1) as avg_prev,
         count(distinct s.at) as nights
  from public.ai_quality_snapshots s
  where s.at < (select at from latest_at)
  group by s.agent
)
select jsonb_build_object(
  'as_of', (select at from latest_at),
  'nights_held', (select count(*) from nights),
  'agents', (select count(*) from latest),
  -- the one headline, weighted the same way as every row under it
  'override_pct_overall', (select round(sum(override_pct * greatest(actions_30d,1))::numeric
                                        / nullif(sum(greatest(actions_30d,1)),0), 1) from latest),
  'actions_30d_total', (select coalesce(sum(actions_30d),0) from latest),
  'meaning', 'override_pct is the share of that agent''s proposed actions in the last 30 days that a human rejected, dismissed, declined or overrode. Higher is worse.',
  'rows', coalesce((
    select jsonb_agg(r order by r->>'sort_key')
    from (
      select jsonb_build_object(
               'agent', l.agent,
               'override_pct', l.override_pct,
               'actions_30d', l.actions_30d,
               'avg_prev', p.avg_prev,
               'nights_of_history', coalesce(p.nights, 0),
               -- stated only when there IS a history to compare against, so a first-night agent
               -- reads as 'new' rather than as 'no change'
               'delta', case when p.avg_prev is null then null
                             else round(l.override_pct - p.avg_prev, 1) end,
               'sort_key', lpad((1000 - least(999, l.actions_30d))::text, 4, '0') || l.agent
             ) as r
      from latest l left join prev p on p.agent = l.agent
    ) x), '[]'::jsonb)
);
fn_customer_decision_support:
declare
  -- A median over fewer than this many quotes is an anecdote wearing a statistic's clothes.
  MIN_PRICE_N constant int := 5;
  v_recommend jsonb;
  v_chase     jsonb;
  v_market    jsonb;
begin
  if p_customer is null then return jsonb_build_object('error','no_customer'); end if;

  -- ── 1. WHICH QUOTE, AND WHY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- lead_time is free text ('3 weeks', '10-14 days', 'ASAP'). The first integer is taken and
  -- scaled by the unit word; anything that yields no integer is UNKNOWN and never claimed as fast.
  -- A quote with no parseable lead time cannot win the speed comparison, which is the honest
  -- outcome: we would be guessing on the customer's behalf.
  with q as (
    select i.id inq, i.summary, i.category, q.id qid, q.supplier_id,
           coalesce(q.customer_price, q.quote_amount) price,
           q.lead_time,
           case
             when q.lead_time ~ '\d' then
               (regexp_match(q.lead_time, '(\d+)'))[1]::int
               * case when q.lead_time ~* 'week' then 7 when q.lead_time ~* 'month' then 30 else 1 end
             else null
           end days
    from inquiries i
    join quotes q on q.inquiry_id = i.id
    where i.customer_id = p_customer
      and coalesce(q.status,'') not in ('withdrawn','expired','rejected')
      and coalesce(q.customer_price, q.quote_amount) is not null
  ),
  agg as (
    select inq, min(summary) summary, min(category) category, count(*) n,
           min(price) lo, max(price) hi,
           (array_agg(qid order by price asc))[1]                       cheapest_id,
           (array_agg(price order by price asc))[1]                     cheapest_price,
           (array_agg(price order by price asc))[2]                     next_price,
           (array_agg(qid  order by days asc) filter (where days is not null))[1] fastest_id,
           (array_agg(days order by days asc) filter (where days is not null))[1] fastest_days,
           (array_agg(days order by price asc))[1]                      cheapest_days,
           count(*) filter (where days is not null)                     n_with_days
    from q group by inq
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'inquiry_id', inq, 'summary', summary, 'category', category, 'quotes', n,
           'cheapest_quote_id', cheapest_id, 'cheapest_price', cheapest_price,
           'saving_vs_next', case when next_price is not null then next_price - cheapest_price end,
           'fastest_quote_id', fastest_id, 'fastest_days', fastest_days,
           'same_quote_wins', (fastest_id is not null and fastest_id = cheapest_id),
           -- Only a real trade-off gets a trade-off sentence. Null here means either one quote
           -- won both ways, or too few lead times were stated to compare speed at all.
           'days_sooner', case when fastest_id is distinct from cheapest_id and fastest_days is not null
                                 and cheapest_days is not null then cheapest_days - fastest_days end,
           'spread', hi - lo,
           'lead_times_stated', n_with_days
         ) order by n desc), '[]'::jsonb)
    into v_recommend from agg where n >= 2;

  -- ── 2. WHAT A JOB LIKE THIS NORMALLY COSTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- Answered per category the customer actually uses, or - for a customer with no requests yet -
  -- left empty rather than filled with the platform average of nothing.
  -- fn_norm_trades is resolved ONCE PER CATEGORY here, not inside the correlated subqueries below.
  -- Called per row it is re-evaluated against all 15,306 supplier_capabilities rows twice over and
  -- the whole function times out - measured, it did.
  with cats as (
    select distinct i.category, i.emirate, public.fn_norm_trades(i.category) norm from inquiries i
    where i.customer_id = p_customer and i.category is not null
  ),
  m as (
    select c.category, c.emirate,
           s.n price_n, s.median, s.p25, s.p75,
           -- THROUGH THE LEXICON, NOT THE RAW CATEGORY. A probe with category 'marble' counted 0
           -- suppliers against 15,306 capability rows, because no supplier lists a trade called
           -- "marble" - fn_norm_trades('marble') is {flooring}, and that is the vocabulary the
           -- capability rows are written in. Comparing the customer's word directly against the
           -- supplier's word is the same defect that left discover() returning nothing while
           -- route_inquiry worked: one path got the lexicon and its sibling did not.
           (select count(*) from supplier_capabilities sc
             where (sc.trades && c.norm or sc.services && c.norm)
               and (c.emirate is null or sc.coverage_emirates && array[c.emirate])) suppliers_covering,
           (select count(*) from supplier_capabilities sc
             where (sc.trades && c.norm or sc.services && c.norm)
               and (c.emirate is null or sc.coverage_emirates && array[c.emirate])
               and sc.review_status = 'confirmed')                                  suppliers_confirmed,
           (select round(avg(extract(epoch from (q.created_at - i2.created_at))/86400)::numeric, 1)
              from inquiries i2 join quotes q on q.inquiry_id = i2.id
             where i2.category = c.category)                                        avg_days_to_quote
    from cats c left join category_price_stats s on s.category = c.category
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'category', category, 'emirate', emirate,
           -- The price block is present ONLY when it rests on enough quotes to mean something.
           -- Absent is a statement; a median over two quotes is a different and false one.
           'price_known', (coalesce(price_n,0) >= MIN_PRICE_N),
           'price_n', coalesce(price_n,0),
           'median', case when coalesce(price_n,0) >= MIN_PRICE_N then median end,
           'p25',    case when coalesce(price_n,0) >= MIN_PRICE_N then p25 end,
           'p75',    case when coalesce(price_n,0) >= MIN_PRICE_N then p75 end,
           'suppliers_covering', suppliers_covering,
           'suppliers_confirmed', suppliers_confirmed,
           'avg_days_to_quote', avg_days_to_quote
         )), '[]'::jsonb)
    into v_market from m;

  -- ── 3. A REQUEST HAS GONE QUIET ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  -- One state per open request, each with the action that actually moves it. The thresholds are
  -- deliberately generous: telling somebody their request is stalled on day one is noise, and a
  -- portal that cries stalled is one a customer stops reading.
  with open_i as (
    select i.id, i.summary, i.category, i.created_at,
           extract(epoch from (now() - i.created_at))/86400 age_days,
           (select count(*) from inquiry_matches m where m.inquiry_id = i.id) invited,
           (select count(*) from quotes q where q.inquiry_id = i.id
              and coalesce(q.status,'') not in ('withdrawn','expired','rejected')) quotes
    from inquiries i
    where i.customer_id = p_customer
      and coalesce(i.status,'open') not in ('closed','cancelled','completed','archived')
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'inquiry_id', id, 'summary', summary, 'category', category,
           'age_days', round(age_days::numeric,1), 'invited', invited, 'quotes', quotes,
           -- QUOTE-BEARING STATES ARE TESTED FIRST. Written the other way round, a request that had
           -- collected two quotes but no inquiry_matches row reported 'not_yet_sent' - the portal
           -- telling a customer we had not reached any supplier while two of their quotes sat on
           -- the screen. A quote is proof of delivery; the absence of a match row is only proof
           -- that one path recorded it. Caught by an aborted-transaction probe that seeded exactly
           -- that shape; an empty result would have proved nothing.
           'state', case
             when quotes >= 2 and age_days >= 7              then 'undecided'
             when quotes  = 1 and age_days >= 5              then 'only_one'
             when quotes  = 0 and invited = 0 and age_days >= 1 then 'not_yet_sent'
             when quotes  = 0 and age_days >= 3              then 'no_replies'
             else 'healthy' end
         ) order by age_days desc), '[]'::jsonb)
    into v_chase
    from open_i
   where case
           when quotes >= 2 and age_days >= 7 then true
           when quotes  = 1 and age_days >= 5 then true
           when quotes  = 0 and invited = 0 and age_days >= 1 then true
           when quotes  = 0 and age_days >= 3 then true
           else false end;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'recommend', v_recommend,
    'market',    v_market,
    'chase',     v_chase,
    'min_price_n', MIN_PRICE_N,
    'as_of', now()
  );
end
fn_action_invoke_rpc:
declare r record; v_ran int := 0; v_refused int := 0; v_skipped int := 0; v_failed int := 0;
        v_key text; v_res jsonb; v_missing boolean; v_required int;
begin
  for r in
    select a.id, a.action_class, a.request, a.idempotency_key, a.attempts,
           e.target, e.active, e.risk_tier, e.advisory_safe, e.reversible,
           e.required_authority, e.compensation_action_class, e.idempotency_strategy,
           e.notifies_human, e.unattended_ok
      from public.action_execution a
      join public.org_action_executor e on e.action_class = a.action_class
     where a.status = 'queued' and e.kind = 'rpc'
     order by a.created_at
     limit greatest(coalesce(p_limit, 5), 1)
  loop
    -- THE SAME REFUSALS AS THE EDGE PATH, in the same order and for the same reasons. A SQL
    -- function is not safer than an HTTP call because it is closer to the data; if anything it is
    -- nearer the money. notifies_human is still checked before the risk tier: a message that
    -- should not have been sent cannot be un-sent by a low risk score.
    if not r.active
       or coalesce(r.required_authority,'') = 'founder'
       or (not r.reversible and r.compensation_action_class is null)
       or (coalesce(r.notifies_human,false) and not coalesce(r.unattended_ok,false))
       or not (r.risk_tier = 'low' and r.advisory_safe and r.reversible) then
      update public.action_execution
         set response = coalesce(response,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'invoker','refused','at',now(),'kind','rpc',
               'reason', case
                 when not r.active then 'executor row is inactive'
                 when coalesce(r.required_authority,'') = 'founder' then 'reserved to the founder'
                 when (not r.reversible and r.compensation_action_class is null)
                   then 'not reversible and declares no compensation_action_class'
                 when (coalesce(r.notifies_human,false) and not coalesce(r.unattended_ok,false))
                   then 'notifies_human is true and unattended_ok has not been set for this class'
                 else format('risk gate: tier=%s advisory_safe=%s reversible=%s - the invoker runs low/advisory_safe/reversible only',
                             r.risk_tier, r.advisory_safe, r.reversible) end)
       where id = r.id;
      v_refused := v_refused + 1;
      continue;
    end if;

    -- CAN THIS TARGET ACTUALLY BE CALLED? Asked of pg_proc, not assumed from the table. A missing
    -- function and a function needing arguments we do not have are different failures and are
    -- reported as different reasons.
    select (p.oid is null), coalesce(p.pronargs - p.pronargdefaults, -1)
      into v_missing, v_required
      from (select 1) _
      left join pg_proc p on p.proname = r.target and p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace;

    if v_missing then
      update public.action_execution
         set status = 'failed', finished_at = now(), attempts = coalesce(attempts,0) + 1,
             response = coalesce(response,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'invoker','failed','at',now(),'kind','rpc',
               'error', format('executor target public.%s() does not exist', r.target))
       where id = r.id;
      v_failed := v_failed + 1;
      continue;
    end if;

    if v_required > 0 then
      update public.action_execution
         set status = 'failed', finished_at = now(), attempts = coalesce(attempts,0) + 1,
             response = coalesce(response,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'invoker','failed','at',now(),'kind','rpc',
               'error', format('public.%s() requires %s argument(s) with no default, and a workflow step carries none to give it. Supply them through org_action_executor.params, or give the function defaults - do not let the invoker invent them.',
                               r.target, v_required))
       where id = r.id;
      v_failed := v_failed + 1;
      continue;
    end if;

    v_key := coalesce(nullif(btrim(r.idempotency_key),''),
                      r.action_class || ':' || md5(coalesce(r.request::text,'')));
    if r.idempotency_strategy is distinct from 'none_read_only'
       and exists (select 1 from public.action_execution x
                    where x.id <> r.id and x.status = 'succeeded'
                      and x.idempotency_key = v_key
                      and x.finished_at > now() - interval '24 hours') then
      update public.action_execution
         set status = 'succeeded', finished_at = now(),
             response = coalesce(response,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'invoker','deduplicated','at',now(),'kind','rpc','idempotency_key',v_key)
       where id = r.id;
      v_skipped := v_skipped + 1;
      continue;
    end if;

    -- One form for every return shape. A set-returning function yields its rows; a scalar
    -- function in FROM yields exactly one. Wrapped per row so one failing target cannot roll back
    -- the others in this sweep.
    begin
      execute format('select coalesce(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(t)), ''[]''::jsonb) from public.%I() t', r.target)
        into v_res;
      update public.action_execution
         set status = 'succeeded', finished_at = now(), attempts = coalesce(attempts,0) + 1,
             executor = r.target, idempotency_key = v_key,
             started_at = coalesce(started_at, now()),
             response = coalesce(response,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'invoker','succeeded','at',now(),'kind','rpc','result', v_res)
       where id = r.id;
      v_ran := v_ran + 1;
    exception when others then
      update public.action_execution
         set status = 'failed', finished_at = now(), attempts = coalesce(attempts,0) + 1,
             executor = r.target,
             response = coalesce(response,'{}'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_object(
               'invoker','failed','at',now(),'kind','rpc',
               'error', replace(coalesce(sqlerrm,'unknown'), '''', ''))
       where id = r.id;
      v_failed := v_failed + 1;
    end;
  end loop;

  return jsonb_build_object('ran', v_ran, 'refused', v_refused, 'deduplicated', v_skipped,
                            'failed', v_failed, 'ran_at', now());
end
fn_company_map:
with cap as (select greatest(1, least(coalesce(p_per_class, 40), 200)) n),
  ranked as (
    select g.kind, g.ref_id, g.label, g.props,
           row_number() over (partition by g.kind order by g.label, g.ref_id) rn
      from graph_nodes g
  ),
  kept as (select * from ranked, cap where ranked.rn <= cap.n),
  totals as (select kind, count(*) total from graph_nodes group by kind)
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'rebuilt_at', (select max(updated_at) from graph_nodes),
    'node_total', (select count(*) from graph_nodes),
    'edge_total', (select count(*) from graph_edges),
    'per_class_cap', (select n from cap),
    'classes', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
               'kind', t.kind, 'total', t.total,
               'shown', (select count(*) from kept k where k.kind = t.kind))
             order by t.total desc)
        from totals t), '[]'::jsonb),
    'nodes', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
               'kind', k.kind, 'id', k.ref_id, 'label', k.label, 'props', k.props)
             order by k.kind, k.label)
        from kept k), '[]'::jsonb),
    'edges', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(distinct jsonb_build_object(

        from graph_edges e
       where exists (select 1 from kept a where a.kind = e.src_kind and a.ref_id = e.src_ref)
         and exists (select 1 from kept b where b.kind = e.dst_kind and b.ref_id = e.dst_ref)),
      '[]'::jsonb)
  );

fn_founder_habits_learn:
declare
  EVIDENCE_FLOOR constant int := 3;
  v_founder text;
  n_rows int := 0;
  n_owners int := 0;
begin
  -- EVERY OWNER IDENTITY, NOT A CHOSEN ONE. The first version picked `order by email limit 1` and
  -- landed on ahmadalzain1993@admin.quotesdone.com, which has decided nothing — all twelve founder
  -- decisions are attributed to management@quotesdone.com. It learned 2 habits from the wrong
  -- person and would have gone on doing so silently. Picking an identity alphabetically is picking
  -- it arbitrarily; the table is keyed (founder, habit_key) precisely so both can be held.
  select count(*) into n_owners from public.user_roles where role = 'owner';
  if n_owners = 0 then
    return jsonb_build_object('ok', false, 'reason', 'no owner identity in user_roles');
  end if;

  for v_founder in select lower(email) from public.user_roles where role = 'owner' order by email loop

  -- ── HABIT 1: what he does with each kind of thing that reaches him ────────────────────────────
  insert into public.founder_habit (founder, habit_key, habit_kind, observed_value, observed_text,
                                    sample_n, confident, evidence, first_seen, last_seen, computed_at)
  select v_founder,
         'disposition:' || a.kind,
         'disposition',
         round(100.0 * count(*) filter (where a.status = 'approved')
               / nullif(count(*), 0), 1),
         case
           when count(*) filter (where a.status = 'rejected') = count(*)
             then 'Rejects every ' || a.kind || ' that reaches him (' || count(*) || ' of ' || count(*)
                  || '). The queue is spending his attention on work he does not want.'
           when count(*) filter (where a.status in ('approved','done')) = count(*)
             then 'Approves every ' || a.kind || ' that reaches him (' || count(*) || ' of ' || count(*)
                  || '). A candidate for higher autonomy.'
           else 'Approves ' || count(*) filter (where a.status in ('approved','done')) || ' of '
                || count(*) || ' ' || a.kind || '.'
         end,
         count(*)::int,
         count(*) >= EVIDENCE_FLOOR,
         jsonb_build_object('kind', a.kind,
           'approved', count(*) filter (where a.status in ('approved','done')),
           'rejected', count(*) filter (where a.status = 'rejected'),
           'total', count(*), 'evidence_floor', EVIDENCE_FLOOR),
         min(a.created_at), max(a.decided_at), now()
    from public.agent_actions a
   where lower(coalesce(a.decided_by,'')) = v_founder
     and a.decided_at is not null
   group by a.kind
  on conflict (founder, habit_key) do update set
    observed_value = excluded.observed_value, observed_text = excluded.observed_text,
    sample_n = excluded.sample_n, confident = excluded.confident, evidence = excluded.evidence,
    first_seen = excluded.first_seen, last_seen = excluded.last_seen, computed_at = now();
  get diagnostics n_rows = row_count;

  -- ── HABIT 2: how long he takes, per kind. The latency IS the preference ──────────────────────
  -- He answers what he approves in a fraction of the time he leaves a rejection sitting, so "how
  -- long has this been waiting" is a prediction about the answer, not just a backlog number.
  insert into public.founder_habit (founder, habit_key, habit_kind, observed_value, observed_text,
                                    sample_n, confident, evidence, first_seen, last_seen, computed_at)
  select v_founder,
         'latency:' || a.kind,
         'latency',
         round(avg(extract(epoch from (a.decided_at - a.created_at)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1),
         'Takes a mean of '
           || round(avg(extract(epoch from (a.decided_at - a.created_at)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1)
           || ' hour(s) to answer a ' || a.kind || ', over ' || count(*) || ' decision(s).',
         count(*)::int,
         count(*) >= EVIDENCE_FLOOR,
         jsonb_build_object('kind', a.kind, 'decisions', count(*),
           'min_hours', round(min(extract(epoch from (a.decided_at - a.created_at)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1),
           'max_hours', round(max(extract(epoch from (a.decided_at - a.created_at)) / 3600.0)::numeric, 1),
           'evidence_floor', EVIDENCE_FLOOR),
         min(a.created_at), max(a.decided_at), now()
    from public.agent_actions a
   where lower(coalesce(a.decided_by,'')) = v_founder
     and a.decided_at is not null and a.created_at is not null
   group by a.kind
  on conflict (founder, habit_key) do update set
    observed_value = excluded.observed_value, observed_text = excluded.observed_text,
    sample_n = excluded.sample_n, confident = excluded.confident, evidence = excluded.evidence,
    first_seen = excluded.first_seen, last_seen = excluded.last_seen, computed_at = now();

  end loop;

  select count(*) into n_rows from public.founder_habit;

  insert into public.agent_runs (agent, started_at, finished_at, status, counts, note)
  values ('founder_habits', now(), now(), 'ok',
          jsonb_build_object('habits', n_rows, 'owners', n_owners,
            'confident', (select count(*) from public.founder_habit where confident)),
          'Learned ' || n_rows || ' habit(s) across ' || n_owners || ' owner identit(ies) from the '
          || 'founder''s own decisions, of which '
          || (select count(*) from public.founder_habit where confident)
          || ' clear the ' || EVIDENCE_FLOOR || '-observation floor. The rest are recorded as '
          || 'observations and are NOT presented as preferences.');

  return jsonb_build_object('ok', true, 'owners', n_owners, 'habits', n_rows,
    'confident', (select count(*) from public.founder_habit where confident),
    'evidence_floor', EVIDENCE_FLOOR);
end

    'learned_at',       (select max(computed_at) from founder_habit),
    -- The note is part of the payload rather than the screen, so a caller that renders the rows

    'note', 'A habit below the evidence floor is an observation, not a preference. sample_n travels with every row.',

fn_context_slice:
with scoped as (
    select record_id, title, content, version, source_freshness, effective_date, review_after,
           layer, record_type, authority_tier, tsv
      from ops_knowledge
     where runtime_eligible
       and supersession_state = 'current'
       and layer = p_layer
       and (
         (p_layer = 'company_core'        and scope_type = 'company')
      -- THE MERGE ARM. A department that absorbed another owns its predecessor's knowledge; the
      -- 5,775 rows tagged with the 22 absorbed keys are not rewritten, they are scoped in.
      or (p_layer = 'department_shared'   and dept_key = any(public.fn_dept_scope(p_dept)))
      or (p_layer = 'role_specific'       and role_key = any(coalesce(p_role_ids, '{}')))
      or (p_layer = 'category_specialist' and category_key = p_category)
       )
  ), matched as (
    -- THE FILTER THAT WAS DEAD. No `or true`: when a query is supplied it now decides membership.
    select *, ts_rank(tsv, p_q) as rank, 'query'::text as match
      from scoped
     where p_q is not null and tsv @@ p_q
  ), fallback as (
    -- Only consulted when topical retrieval under-delivers. Highest authority first, and every row
    -- carries match='fallback' so the caller can tell the difference.
    select *, 0::real as rank, 'fallback'::text as match
      from scoped
     where p_q is null or (select count(*) from matched) < 3
  ), unioned as (
    select * from matched
    union all
    select * from fallback f where not exists (select 1 from matched m where m.record_id = f.record_id)
  ), deduped as (
    -- Duplicate suppression: the same record can be reachable by more than one scope arm, and the
    -- same TITLE often repeats across package generations. Keep the freshest of each title.
    select distinct on (coalesce(nullif(title,''), record_id))
           record_id, title, content, version, source_freshness, effective_date, review_after,
           layer, record_type, authority_tier, rank, match
      from unioned
     order by coalesce(nullif(title,''), record_id),
              (match = 'query') desc, rank desc,
              coalesce(effective_date, '1900-01-01'::date) desc, record_id
  ), ranked as (
    select *,
           -- freshness is carried, not judged here: review_after in the past is stale and the
           -- caller must be able to see that rather than infer it.
           (review_after is not null and review_after < current_date) as stale,
           sum(least(length(content), 1800)) over (
             order by (match = 'query') desc, rank desc, record_id
             rows between unbounded preceding and current row) as running
      from deduped
  )
  select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
           'record_id', record_id, 'title', title, 'layer', layer, 'record_type', record_type,
           'version', version, 'source_freshness', source_freshness,
           'review_after', review_after, 'stale', stale,
           'authority_tier', authority_tier, 'match', match,
           'content', left(content, 1800))
         order by (match = 'query') desc, rank desc, record_id), '[]'::jsonb)
    from ranked
   where running <= greatest(p_budget, 1800);
fn_agent_context_v3:
declare
  v_agent      record;
  v_identity   jsonb;
  v_pkg_dept   text;
  v_role_ids   text[];
  v_out        jsonb;
  v_ids        text[] := '{}';
  v_used       integer := 0;
  v_budget     integer := greatest(coalesce(p_budget_chars, 24000), 2000);
  v_q          tsquery;
  v_scope      text[];
  v_role       record;
begin
  -- RESOLVE BEFORE CONTEXT ASSEMBLY (14 Aug 2026).
  --
  -- This lookup was `where a.agent_key = p_agent_key` against org_agents, so it only ever answered
  -- to a runtime agent_key. Measured: fn_agent_context_v3('chief_of_staff') returned
  -- {"error":"unknown agent"} - and chief_of_staff is not a stale string, it is brief's own
  -- role_id in org_role. fn_org_agent_resolve('chief_of_staff') has always returned 'brief'.
  --
  -- This is the hottest path in the company: agent_brain, action_worker, dept_plan, agent_act and
  -- exec_agents all assemble context through here. An employee addressed by its canonical role id,
  -- a merged-away key, a packaged role id or a job title got no context at all - not a failure,
  -- an empty prompt - while the resolver that answers all four sat one call away.
  --
  -- Section 2 of the closure brief requires identity to be resolved BEFORE context assembly. This
  -- is that line. coalesce keeps an unknown key unknown, so the refusal below still fires.
  p_agent_key := coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(p_agent_key), p_agent_key);

  select a.agent_key, a.department, a.role, a.title, a.manager_key, a.seniority,
         a.responsibilities, a.max_open_tasks, a.active, d.name dept_name, d.charter, d.north_star
    into v_agent
    from org_agents a
    left join org_departments d on d.dept_key = a.department
   where a.agent_key = p_agent_key;

  if v_agent.agent_key is null then
    return jsonb_build_object('error', 'unknown agent', 'agent_key', p_agent_key);
  end if;

  v_scope := public.fn_dept_scope(v_agent.department);

  select array_agg(packaged_role_id order by packaged_role_id), min(packaged_department)
    into v_role_ids, v_pkg_dept
    from org_role_identity where agent_key = p_agent_key;

  -- The canonical role. Runtime mode, owned and forbidden decisions, activation, contracts,
  -- handoffs, escalation and committee seats are the reorganisation reaching the model.
  select r.role_id, r.display_name, r.runtime_mode, r.authority_level, r.owned_decisions,
         r.forbidden_decisions, r.activation_conditions, r.output_contracts, r.handoff_targets,
         r.escalation_targets, r.manager_role_id, r.budget_limit, r.evaluation_suite,
         (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('committee', c.committee_key, 'seat', c.seat)
                                    order by c.committee_key), '[]'::jsonb)
            from org_role_committee c where c.role_id = r.role_id) as committees
    into v_role
    from org_role r where r.runtime_agent_key = p_agent_key and r.status = 'active';

  -- 1. IDENTITY — who the agent is, who it reports to, what it may decide.
  v_identity := jsonb_build_object(
    'agent_key', v_agent.agent_key,
    'title', coalesce(v_agent.title, v_agent.role),
    'department', v_agent.department,
    'department_name', v_agent.dept_name,
    'department_charter', v_agent.charter,
    'department_north_star', v_agent.north_star,
    'department_knowledge_scope', to_jsonb(v_scope),
    'manager', v_agent.manager_key,
    'seniority', v_agent.seniority,
    'responsibilities', v_agent.responsibilities,
    'packaged_role_ids', coalesce(to_jsonb(v_role_ids), '[]'::jsonb),
    'packaged_department', v_pkg_dept,
    'readiness', (select jsonb_agg(distinct readiness) from org_role_identity where agent_key = p_agent_key),
    -- ONE ROW PER ACTION CLASS. Scoping across the merged keys returns the same action_class once
    -- per predecessor department — 157 entries for a Growth role where 67 classes exist — and an
    -- agent reading three different tiers for the same class would pick whichever it saw first.
    -- Most restrictive wins: advisory < gated < supervised < autonomous.
    'authority', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('action_class', action_class, 'max_tier', max_tier,
                                          'threshold_aed', threshold_aed) order by action_class)
        from (select distinct on (action_class) action_class, max_tier, threshold_aed
                from org_authority where dept_key = any(v_scope)
               order by action_class,
                        case max_tier when 'advisory' then 1 when 'gated' then 2
                                      when 'supervised' then 3 else 4 end,
                        threshold_aed nulls first) a), '[]'::jsonb),
    'max_open_tasks', v_agent.max_open_tasks)
    || case when v_role.role_id is null then '{}'::jsonb else jsonb_build_object(
         'role_id', v_role.role_id,
         'role_display_name', v_role.display_name,
         'runtime_mode', v_role.runtime_mode,
         'authority_level', v_role.authority_level,
         'owned_decisions', to_jsonb(v_role.owned_decisions),
         'forbidden_decisions', to_jsonb(v_role.forbidden_decisions),
         'activation_conditions', v_role.activation_conditions,
         'output_contracts', to_jsonb(v_role.output_contracts),
         'handoff_targets', to_jsonb(v_role.handoff_targets),
         'escalation_targets', to_jsonb(v_role.escalation_targets),
         'manager_role_id', v_role.manager_role_id,
         'budget_limit_aed', v_role.budget_limit,
         'evaluation_suite', v_role.evaluation_suite,
         'committees', v_role.committees) end;

  if p_task_text is not null and length(p_task_text) > 1 then
    v_q := public.fn_task_tsquery(p_task_text);
  end if;

  -- 2. DETERMINISTIC RULES — structured, complete, never similarity-ranked.
  with rules as (
    select record_id, layer, record_type, title, structured_data, authority_tier, risk_level,
           version, source_freshness, effective_date, review_after
      from ops_knowledge
     where runtime_eligible
       and supersession_state = 'current'
       and layer in ('authority','kpi','decision_playbook','policy')
       and (
         (scope_type = 'company')
         or (scope_type = 'department' and dept_key = any(v_scope))
         or (role_key = any(coalesce(v_role_ids, '{}')))
         or (p_category_key is not null and category_key = p_category_key)
       )
     order by case layer when 'authority' then 0 when 'policy' then 1 when 'decision_playbook' then 2 else 3 end,
              record_id
     limit 60
  )
  select jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(r)), array_agg(r.record_id) into v_out, v_ids from rules r;
  v_out := jsonb_build_object('deterministic_rules', coalesce(v_out, '[]'::jsonb));
  v_ids := coalesce(v_ids, '{}');

  -- 3. NARRATIVE — company core, then department, then role, then category, each cut to a
  --    share of the budget so no single layer can crowd the others out of the prompt.
  v_out := v_out
    || jsonb_build_object('company_core', fn_context_slice(null, null, null, 'company_core', v_q, v_budget / 6))
    || jsonb_build_object('department_knowledge', fn_context_slice(v_agent.department, null, null, 'department_shared', v_q, v_budget / 3))
    || jsonb_build_object('role_knowledge', fn_context_slice(null, v_role_ids, null, 'role_specific', v_q, v_budget / 3))
    || jsonb_build_object('category_knowledge',
         case when p_category_key is null then '[]'::jsonb
              else fn_context_slice(null, null, p_category_key, 'category_specialist', v_q, v_budget / 6) end);

  -- 4. VALIDATED EXPERIENCE — only lessons a manager or evaluator has validated. A proposed
  --    lesson is deliberately invisible here; that is the whole point of the two states.
  v_out := v_out || jsonb_build_object('validated_experience', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('id', id, 'topic', topic, 'content', left(content, 1200),
                                          'confidence', confidence, 'valid_until', valid_until))
        from (select * from agent_knowledge
               where agent_key = p_agent_key
                 and layer = 'experience'
                 and validation_status = 'validated'
                 and (valid_until is null or valid_until >= current_date)
               order by coalesce(confidence, 0) desc, updated_at desc nulls last
               limit 8) e), '[]'::jsonb));

  -- 5. LIVE DATA BINDINGS — what the agent must fetch rather than remember. The binding is
  --    knowledge; the value is not, and is never cached here.
  v_out := v_out || jsonb_build_object('live_data_required', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('record_id', record_id, 'title', title,
                                          'binding', structured_data))
        from ops_knowledge
       where record_type = 'live_data_binding' and runtime_eligible
         and supersession_state = 'current'
         and (scope_type = 'company' or dept_key = any(v_scope))
       limit 12), '[]'::jsonb));

  -- 6. TOOLS the agent is actually allowed to execute.
  v_out := v_out || jsonb_build_object('tools', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('action_class', action_class, 'kind', kind,
                                          'risk_tier', risk_tier, 'reversible', reversible,
                                          'required_authority', required_authority,
                                          'notifies_human', notifies_human))
        from org_action_executor
       where active and (department = any(v_scope) or target = p_agent_key)
       limit 30), '[]'::jsonb));

  -- collect every knowledge id the assembly actually used
  select v_ids || coalesce(array_agg(x), '{}') into v_ids
    from (select jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(v_out->'company_core','[]'::jsonb) ||
                                      coalesce(v_out->'department_knowledge','[]'::jsonb) ||
                                      coalesce(v_out->'role_knowledge','[]'::jsonb) ||
                                      coalesce(v_out->'category_knowledge','[]'::jsonb)) ->> 'record_id' x) s;

  return jsonb_build_object(
    'identity', v_identity,
    'task_class', p_task_class,
    'category_key', p_category_key,
    'company_objective', coalesce((
      select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('key', key, 'goal', goal, 'metric', metric,
                                          'target', target_value, 'unit', unit, 'period', period,
                                          'owner_dept', owner_dept, 'horizon', horizon))
        from (select * from company_goals
               where active
               order by (owner_dept is not distinct from v_agent.department) desc,
                        (category = 'Financial') desc, sort
               limit 8) g), '[]'::jsonb),
    'budget_chars', v_budget,
    'knowledge_ids', to_jsonb(v_ids),
    'knowledge_count', coalesce(array_length(v_ids, 1), 0),
    'assembled_at', now()
  ) || v_out;
end
fn_context_retrieval_prune:
with d as (delete from agent_context_retrieval where created_at < now() - interval '7 days' returning 1)
  select count(*)::int from d;
fn_agent_action_trace:
begin
  -- Delegates to the shared builder so the UPDATE path and the INSERT path cannot produce
  -- different trace shapes. fn_agent_action_trace_row resolves role, department and manager from
  -- the roster and pulls the knowledge actually retrieved near the decision.
  perform public.fn_agent_action_trace_row(new);
  return new;
end
fn_agent_autonomy_blocked:
with me as (select coalesce(public.fn_org_agent_resolve(p_agent_key), p_agent_key) as k)
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'agent_key', (select k from me),
    'asked_as', p_agent_key,
    'blocked', exists (select 1 from agent_remediation
                        where agent_key = (select k from me) and blocks_autonomy and status <> 'passed'),
    'open_remediations', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
        'id', id, 'failure_class', failure_class, 'competency', competency, 'status', status))
      from agent_remediation where agent_key = (select k from me) and status <> 'passed'), '[]'::jsonb),
    'readiness', coalesce((select jsonb_agg(distinct readiness) from org_role_identity
                            where agent_key = (select k from me)), '[]'::jsonb));
fn_role_readiness_recompute:
declare v_counts jsonb;
begin
  with fact as (
    select
      i.agent_key, i.packaged_role_id, a.active, a.department,
      exists (select 1 from ops_knowledge k
               where k.role_key = i.packaged_role_id and k.runtime_eligible
                 and k.supersession_state = 'current')                         as has_knowledge,
      exists (select 1 from org_departments d
               where d.lead_agent = i.agent_key or d.brain_agent = i.agent_key) as is_named_runner,
      exists (select 1 from agent_runs r where r.agent = i.agent_key)           as has_run,
      exists (select 1 from org_action_executor e
               where e.active and (e.department = a.department or e.target = i.agent_key)) as has_tools,
      exists (select 1 from ops_knowledge k
               where k.record_type = 'live_data_binding'
                 and (k.scope_type = 'company' or k.dept_key = a.department))   as has_live_data,
      exists (select 1 from agent_context_retrieval c where c.agent_key = i.agent_key)
        or exists (select 1 from agent_actions x where x.agent = i.agent_key)   as traceable,
      exists (select 1 from agent_remediation m
               where m.agent_key = i.agent_key and m.status = 'passed')         as trained,
      exists (select 1 from agent_remediation m
               where m.agent_key = i.agent_key and m.blocks_autonomy and m.status <> 'passed') as blocked,
      exists (select 1 from org_action_executor e
               where e.active and e.department = a.department
                 and (e.risk_tier in ('high','medium') or e.notifies_human))    as consequential,
      -- an isolation call outranks every rung below it
      (select d.resolution from role_isolation_decision d
        where d.agent_key = i.agent_key and d.packaged_role_id = i.packaged_role_id)
                                                                               as isolation_resolution
    from org_role_identity i
    join org_agents a on a.agent_key = i.agent_key
  ), rung as (
    select agent_key, packaged_role_id,
      case
        when isolation_resolution = 'block'                then 'blocked'
        when isolation_resolution = 'restrict_to_advisory' then 'restricted_to_advisory'
        when not active                       then 'blocked'
        when blocked                          then 'restricted_to_advisory'
        when not has_knowledge                then 'blocked'
        when trained and not blocked          then 'independent_certification_pending'
        when consequential and not trained    then 'restricted_to_advisory'
        when traceable and has_live_data and has_tools then 'decision_trace_connected'
        when has_live_data and has_tools      then 'live_data_connected'
        when has_tools                        then 'tools_connected'
        when is_named_runner or has_run       then 'runtime_mapped'
        else 'knowledge_imported'
      end as readiness
    from fact
  )
  update org_role_identity i set readiness = r.readiness, updated_at = now()
    from rung r
   where i.agent_key = r.agent_key and i.packaged_role_id = r.packaged_role_id
     and i.readiness is distinct from r.readiness;

  select jsonb_object_agg(readiness, n) into v_counts
    from (select readiness, count(*) n from org_role_identity group by 1) s;

  -- The one status a builder session may never assign.
  if exists (select 1 from org_role_identity where readiness = 'certified_for_defined_role_scope') then
    raise exception 'certified_for_defined_role_scope was assigned without an independent evaluator';
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('recomputed_at', now(), 'counts', v_counts,
    'ceiling', 'independent_certification_pending');
end
fn_blueprint_regressions:
with runs as (
    select distinct run_id, run_at from os_blueprint_result
     where spec_file = p_spec and ref = p_ref order by run_at desc limit 2
  ), newest as (select * from os_blueprint_result where run_id = (select run_id from runs order by run_at desc limit 1)),
     prev   as (select * from os_blueprint_result where run_id = (select run_id from runs order by run_at asc  limit 1))
  select n.check_id, n.name, p.ok, n.ok,
         case when p.ok and not n.ok then 'REGRESSED'
              when not p.ok and n.ok then 'FIXED'
              else 'unchanged' end,
         n.evidence
    from newest n
    join prev p using (check_id)
   where (select count(*) from runs) = 2
     and p.ok is distinct from n.ok
   order by 5, 1;
fn_blueprint_result_prune:
with d as (delete from os_blueprint_result where run_at < now() - interval '90 days' returning 1)
  select count(*)::int from d;
trg_org_role_touch: begin new.updated_at := now(); return new; end
fn_org_role_resolve:
select coalesce(
    (select r.role_id from public.org_role r where r.role_id = p_any and r.status = 'active'),
    (select a.role_id from public.org_role_alias a
        join public.org_role r on r.role_id = a.role_id and r.status = 'active'
       where a.alias = p_any),
    (select r.role_id from public.org_role r
       where r.runtime_agent_key = p_any and r.status = 'active' limit 1),
    -- last arm: whatever org_agents' own alias table already knew, mapped forward
    (select r.role_id from public.org_agent_alias g
        join public.org_role r on r.runtime_agent_key = g.agent_key and r.status = 'active'
       where g.alias = p_any limit 1)
  );

   where not exists (select 1 from public.fn_org_role_deferred() d
                      where d.rule = v.rule and d.role_id = v.role_id);

fn_overlay_for_category:

    'overlay_role_id', 'category_overlay_'||c.category_key,
    'owner_agent', c.owner_agent,
    'invoked_by_role', 'inquiry_router',
    'readiness', c.readiness,
    'exists', (select count(*) > 0 from public.org_role r
                where r.role_id = 'category_overlay_'||c.category_key and r.status='active'))
    from public.org_category_identity c where c.category_key = p_category_key;
fn_objective_cascade:
with company as (
    select count(*) filter (where active) as goals,
           count(*) filter (where active and coalesce(measure_sql,'') <> '') as measurable,
           max(target_value) filter (where active and category = 'Financial') as top_target
      from public.company_goals),
  dept as (
    select count(*) filter (where active) as objectives,
           count(*) filter (where active and coalesce(goal_key,'') <> '') as linked_to_goal
      from public.department_objective),
  role_kpi as (
    select count(*) filter (where k.active) as kpis,
           count(*) filter (where k.active and (coalesce(k.serves_goal,'') <> '' or k.serves_objective is not null)) as linked,
           count(*) filter (where k.active and k.measured_at is not null) as measured
      from public.employee_kpi k
      join public.org_role r on r.runtime_agent_key = k.agent_key and r.status = 'active'),
  work as (
    select count(*) filter (where status in ('assigned','in_progress')) as open,
           count(*) filter (where status in ('assigned','in_progress') and assigned_agent is not null) as owned
      from public.org_tasks)
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'revenue_objective_aed', (select top_target from company),
    'company_goals', (select goals from company),
    'company_goals_measurable', (select measurable from company),
    'department_objectives', (select objectives from dept),
    'department_objectives_linked_to_a_company_goal', (select linked_to_goal from dept),
    'role_kpis', (select kpis from role_kpi),
    'role_kpis_linked_upward', (select linked from role_kpi),
    'role_kpis_with_a_measured_actual', (select measured from role_kpi),
    'open_work', (select open from work),
    'open_work_with_one_accountable_owner', (select owned from work),
    'unlinked_department_objectives', (select objectives - linked_to_goal from dept),
    'unlinked_role_kpis', (select kpis - linked from role_kpi),
    'note', 'links are written only where a department owns exactly one active goal or objective; '
            ||'the remainder are reported unlinked rather than guessed');
fn_knowledge_gap:
with layers as (
    select k as layer, p_ctx->k as rows
      from unnest(array['company_core','department_knowledge','role_knowledge','category_knowledge']) k
     where jsonb_typeof(p_ctx->k) = 'array'
  ), per as (
    select l.layer,
           jsonb_array_length(l.rows)                                                          as n,
           (select count(*) from jsonb_array_elements(l.rows) e where e->>'match' = 'query')    as matched,
           (select count(*) from jsonb_array_elements(l.rows) e where (e->>'stale')::boolean)   as stale
      from layers l
  )
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'layers', coalesce(jsonb_object_agg(layer, jsonb_build_object('records', n, 'matched_query', matched, 'stale', stale)), '{}'::jsonb),
    'total_records',  coalesce(sum(n),0),
    'total_matched',  coalesce(sum(matched),0),
    'total_stale',    coalesce(sum(stale),0),
    -- The one boolean the runtime acts on.
    'has_gap',        coalesce(sum(matched),0) = 0,
    'gap_layers',     coalesce((select jsonb_agg(layer order by layer) from per where n > 0 and matched = 0), '[]'::jsonb),
    'instruction',    case when coalesce(sum(matched),0) = 0
                        then 'NO retrieved knowledge matched this task. You are working from general departmental material only. Say so explicitly, and request, research or escalate rather than answering as if you had specific guidance.'
                        else null end)
  from per;
fn_write_decision_trace:
declare
  v_id       uuid;
  v_agent    text := nullif(p->>'agent_key','');
  v_role     text;
  v_dept     text;
  v_mgr      text;
  v_dobj     text;
  v_corr     uuid := coalesce(nullif(p->>'correlation_id','')::uuid, gen_random_uuid());
begin
  if v_agent is null then
    raise exception 'fn_write_decision_trace: agent_key is required. A trace that cannot name who decided is not evidence.';
  end if;

  -- Identity is resolved SERVER-SIDE from the roster. A model cannot label its own trace with
  -- someone else's role, which is the whole point of separating role_id from agent_key.
  select a.department, a.manager_key, d.north_star
    into v_dept, v_mgr, v_dobj
    from org_agents a left join org_departments d on d.dept_key = a.department
   where a.agent_key = v_agent;

  v_role := coalesce(nullif(p->>'role_id',''),
                     (select i.packaged_role_id from org_role_identity i
                       where i.agent_key = v_agent order by i.packaged_role_id limit 1));

  insert into decision_trace (
    correlation_id, entity_type, entity_id, decision_type, proposed_by, decided_by,
    policy_keys, knowledge_refs, evidence_refs, alternatives, assumptions, risk,
    confidence, authority_result, decision, outcome_status,
    task_id, agent_key, role_id, department_id, manager_id, task_class,
    company_objective, department_objective, relevant_kpi,
    knowledge_versions, source_freshness, tools_requested, tools_executed, tool_result_refs,
    uncertainty, escalation_decision, proposed_action, expected_outcome, review_date,
    model, provider, input_tokens, output_tokens, estimated_cost_aed, final_status
  ) values (
    v_corr,
    coalesce(nullif(p->>'entity_type',''),'agent_task'),
    nullif(p->>'entity_id',''),
    coalesce(nullif(p->>'decision_type',''),'agent_decision'),
    v_agent,
    coalesce(nullif(p->>'decided_by',''), v_agent),
    coalesce((select array_agg(x) from jsonb_array_elements_text(coalesce(p->'policy_keys','[]'::jsonb)) x), '{}'),
    coalesce(p->'knowledge_refs','[]'::jsonb),
    coalesce(p->'evidence_refs','[]'::jsonb),
    coalesce(p->'alternatives','[]'::jsonb),
    coalesce(p->'assumptions','[]'::jsonb),
    coalesce(p->'risk','{}'::jsonb),
    nullif(p->>'confidence','')::numeric,
    coalesce(p->'authority_result','{}'::jsonb),
    coalesce(p->'decision','{}'::jsonb),
    coalesce(nullif(p->>'outcome_status',''),'pending'),
    nullif(p->>'task_id',''), v_agent, v_role, v_dept, v_mgr, nullif(p->>'task_class',''),
    -- The canonical company objective, read from the row that owns it rather than restated here:
    -- company_goals.revenue_annual = "Reach AED 1,000,000 annual revenue", target 1000000 AED.
    coalesce(nullif(p->>'company_objective',''),
             (select g.goal || ' (' || g.target_value::text || ' ' || coalesce(g.unit,'') || ')'
                from company_goals g where g.key = 'revenue_annual' and g.active limit 1)),
    coalesce(nullif(p->>'department_objective',''), v_dobj),
    nullif(p->>'relevant_kpi',''),
    coalesce(p->'knowledge_versions','{}'::jsonb),
    coalesce(p->'source_freshness','{}'::jsonb),
    coalesce((select array_agg(x) from jsonb_array_elements_text(coalesce(p->'tools_requested','[]'::jsonb)) x), '{}'),
    coalesce((select array_agg(x) from jsonb_array_elements_text(coalesce(p->'tools_executed','[]'::jsonb)) x), '{}'),
    coalesce(p->'tool_result_refs','[]'::jsonb),
    nullif(p->>'uncertainty',''), nullif(p->>'escalation_decision',''),
    nullif(p->>'proposed_action',''), nullif(p->>'expected_outcome',''),
    nullif(p->>'review_date','')::date,
    nullif(p->>'model',''), nullif(p->>'provider',''),
    nullif(p->>'input_tokens','')::integer, nullif(p->>'output_tokens','')::integer,
    nullif(p->>'estimated_cost_aed','')::numeric, nullif(p->>'final_status','')
  ) returning id into v_id;

  return v_id;
end
fn_agent_action_trace_row:
declare v_ids text[]; v_id uuid;
begin
  -- knowledge actually retrieved by this agent near the decision, from the recording table
  select coalesce(array_agg(distinct k), '{}') into v_ids
    from agent_context_retrieval r, unnest(r.knowledge_ids) k
   where r.agent_key = a.agent
     and r.created_at between a.decided_at - interval '30 minutes' and a.decided_at + interval '1 minute';

  select public.fn_write_decision_trace(jsonb_build_object(
    'agent_key',       a.agent,
    'entity_type',     coalesce(a.target_table,'agent_action'),
    'entity_id',       coalesce(a.target_id::text, a.id::text),
    'decision_type',   a.kind,
    'decided_by',      coalesce(a.decided_by, a.agent),
    'task_id',         a.id::text,
    'confidence',      a.confidence::text,
    'risk',            jsonb_build_object('tier', a.risk, 'escalated', a.escalated),
    'evidence_refs',   coalesce(a.evidence, '[]'::jsonb),
    'alternatives',    coalesce(a.alternatives, '[]'::jsonb),
    'assumptions',     coalesce(a.assumptions, '[]'::jsonb),
    'knowledge_refs',  to_jsonb(v_ids),
    'proposed_action', a.recommendation,
    'expected_outcome',a.expected_impact,
    'escalation_decision', case when a.escalated then 'escalated' else 'within_authority' end,
    'outcome_status',  case when a.status in ('done','approved') then 'accepted'
                            when a.status in ('rejected','dismissed') then 'rejected'
                            else 'pending' end,
    'final_status',    a.status
  )) into v_id;
  return v_id;
end
fn_decision_trace_immutable:
begin
  if old.sealed_at is not null then
    -- Only the outcome may be graded after sealing. Everything the decision was BASED on is frozen.
    if (new.decision        is distinct from old.decision)
    or (new.evidence_refs   is distinct from old.evidence_refs)
    or (new.knowledge_refs  is distinct from old.knowledge_refs)
    or (new.tool_result_refs is distinct from old.tool_result_refs)
    or (new.confidence      is distinct from old.confidence)
    or (new.authority_result is distinct from old.authority_result)
    or (new.agent_key       is distinct from old.agent_key)
    or (new.role_id         is distinct from old.role_id)
    or (new.proposed_action is distinct from old.proposed_action) then
      raise exception 'decision_trace % is sealed. Evidence, confidence, authority and identity cannot be edited after the fact; grade the outcome instead.', old.id;
    end if;
  end if;
  return new;
end
fn_seal_decision_trace: update decision_trace set sealed_at = now() where id = p_id and sealed_at is null returning true;
fn_management_decision_review:
with t as (
    select *,
           case when jsonb_typeof(knowledge_refs)='array' then jsonb_array_length(knowledge_refs) else 0 end as kn,
           case when jsonb_typeof(evidence_refs) ='array' then jsonb_array_length(evidence_refs)  else 0 end as ev
      from decision_trace
     where (p_department is null or department_id = p_department)
       and created_at > now() - make_interval(days => greatest(p_days,1))
  )
  select t.id, t.created_at, t.agent_key, t.role_id, t.department_id, t.manager_id,
         t.decision_type, t.proposed_action, t.confidence, t.escalation_decision,
         t.tools_requested, t.tools_executed, t.kn, t.ev,
         t.review_date, t.outcome_status, t.final_status, t.sealed_at is not null,
         nullif(concat_ws('; ',
           case when t.role_id is null            then 'no canonical role' end,
           case when t.ev = 0                     then 'no evidence' end,
           case when t.confidence is null         then 'no confidence' end,
           case when t.escalation_decision is null then 'no authority decision' end,
           case when t.review_date is null        then 'no review date' end,
           case when t.final_status is null       then 'no output status' end), '')
  from t order by t.created_at desc limit greatest(p_limit,1);
fn_archetype_tier:
select case p_archetype
           when 'director' then 1
           when 'analyst-controller' then 2
           when 'reviewer-auditor' then 2
           when 'operations-specialist' then 3
           else 9 end;
fn_role_identity_isolation_guard:
declare v_other text;
begin
  select string_agg(o.packaged_role_id || ' (' || o.archetype || ')', ', '
                    order by o.packaged_role_id)
    into v_other
    from public.org_role_identity o
   where o.agent_key = new.agent_key
     and o.packaged_department = new.packaged_department
     and o.packaged_role_id <> new.packaged_role_id
     and ( (    new.archetype = 'reviewer-auditor'
            and o.archetype in ('director','operations-specialist','analyst-controller'))
        or (    o.archetype = 'reviewer-auditor'
            and new.archetype in ('director','operations-specialist','analyst-controller')) );

  if v_other is null then
    return new;
  end if;

  -- The conflict may exist, but only as a decision somebody signed for — and signed for THIS
  -- archetype.  Matching on (agent_key, packaged_role_id) alone was tried and probed: it let
  -- payments-and-revenue-operations-analyst-controller be redefined to reviewer-auditor on the
  -- strength of a decision that had been recorded about the analyst-controller identity.  A
  -- decision about one identity is not consent for a different one.
  if exists (select 1 from public.role_isolation_decision d
              where d.agent_key = new.agent_key
                and d.packaged_role_id = new.packaged_role_id
                and d.archetype = new.archetype) then
    return new;
  end if;

  raise exception
    'agent % would be both producer and independent reviewer of % (this row: % as %; also holds: %)',
    new.agent_key, new.packaged_department, new.packaged_role_id, new.archetype, v_other
    using errcode = '23514',
          hint = 'record the call in role_isolation_decision first: '
                 'isolate | split | restrict_to_advisory | block';
end

select jsonb_build_object(
