fn_kernel_write_guard_state:
with protected(t) as (values
  ('phase_c_workflow_run'),('phase_c_workflow_step_run'),('phase_c_task'),('phase_c_handoff_run'),
  ('kernel_trigger_inbox'),('kernel_signal_inbox'),('phase_c_event_outbox'),('phase_c_refund_decision')),
attached as (
  select p.t, exists (
    select 1 from pg_trigger tg join pg_class c on c.oid = tg.tgrelid
     join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relname = p.t
      and tg.tgname = 'a00_kernel_write_guard' and not tg.tgisinternal and tg.tgenabled <> 'D') a
  from protected p
),
-- Every routine whose DEPLOYED body writes a protected table, measured from prosrc with comments
-- stripped — the same scan that produced the seed. A writer that is not on the allow-list is a
-- routine that will be refused at runtime, and it is better to see it here than in an outage.
writers as (
  select p.proname, t.t
    from protected t
    join pg_proc p on true
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
   where regexp_replace(regexp_replace(p.prosrc, '/\*.*?\*/', ' ', 'g'), '--[^\n]*', ' ', 'g')
         ~ ('(insert\s+into|update|delete\s+from)\s+(public\.)?' || t.t || '\M')
     and p.proname <> 'fn_kernel_write_guard'
)
select 'protected_tables_without_the_guard_attached'::text,
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from protected),
       (select count(*)::text from attached where not a) || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from protected),
       (select count(*) = 0 from attached where not a)
union all
select 'routines_that_write_a_protected_table_with_no_authority',
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from writers),

fn_kernel_historical_register_state:
with r as (select * from public.phase_c_historical_repair),
-- ROOT CAUSE 4 FOLLOW-UP, 17 Aug 2026. The register is append-only and its own trigger states the
-- correction protocol: "A correction is a NEW row that names the repair_id it corrects in its
-- evidence, never an edit to the row that stated the original finding." Until now nothing here read
-- that protocol, so a corrected finding went on being counted as a live one and there was no way to
-- satisfy the register by the mechanism the register prescribes. A CLASSIFICATION that a later row
-- names as corrected is no longer in the population; the correcting row has to exist and has to
-- name it, which is stricter bookkeeping than not looking.
exc as (
  select * from r c
   where c.entry_kind = 'CLASSIFICATION'
     and not exists (select 1 from r x
                      where (x.evidence->>'corrects_repair_id')::bigint = c.repair_id))
-- ---- CURRENT state. These must be zero, and they are about today, not about history.
select 'active_historical_duplicate_work'::text,
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc where classification = 'HISTORICAL_DUPLICATE_EFFECT'),
       (select count(*)::text from exc
         where classification = 'HISTORICAL_DUPLICATE_EFFECT' and active_effect_now)
         || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc where classification = 'HISTORICAL_DUPLICATE_EFFECT'),
       (select count(*) = 0 from exc where classification = 'HISTORICAL_DUPLICATE_EFFECT' and active_effect_now)
union all
select 'queued_work_beneath_cancelled_commands',
       '0',
       (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_task t
         join public.founder_command c on c.command_id = t.command_id
        where c.state = 'cancelled'
          and t.state not in (select state from public.phase_c_task_state where terminal)),
       (select count(*) = 0 from public.phase_c_task t
         join public.founder_command c on c.command_id = t.command_id
        where c.state = 'cancelled'
          and t.state not in (select state from public.phase_c_task_state where terminal))
union all
select 'current_terminal_objects_with_open_trace',
       '0',
       (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_trace t
         where t.status = 'open'
           and t.created_at >= (select min(started_at) from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch)
           and exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_workflow_run w
                        where w.run_id::text = t.subject_ref and t.subject_kind = 'workflow_run'
                          and w.state in (select state from public.phase_b_workflow_state where terminal))),
       (select count(*) = 0 from public.phase_c_trace t
         where t.status = 'open'
           and t.created_at >= (select min(started_at) from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch)
           and exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_workflow_run w
                        where w.run_id::text = t.subject_ref and t.subject_kind = 'workflow_run'
                          and w.state in (select state from public.phase_b_workflow_state where terminal)))
union all
select 'current_active_orphan_traces',
       '0 — an orphan trace created AFTER the kernel epoch',
       (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_trace t
         where t.created_at >= (select min(started_at) from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch)
           and t.subject_kind = 'task'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_task k where k.task_id::text = t.subject_ref)),
       (select count(*) = 0 from public.phase_c_trace t
         where t.created_at >= (select min(started_at) from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch)
           and t.subject_kind = 'task'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_task k where k.task_id::text = t.subject_ref))
union all
-- ---- PRESERVED history. Reported with an exact count, never as compliance.
select 'historical_exceptions_preserved',
       'reported exactly, and never presented as current compliance',
       (select string_agg(classification || ' ' || n::text, '; ' order by classification)
          from (select classification, count(*) n from exc group by 1) d)
         || '; retrofit entries ' || (select count(*)::text from r where entry_kind = 'RETROFIT'),
       true
union all
select 'historical_exceptions_with_no_original_timestamp',
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc),
       (select count(*)::text from exc where original_at is null)
         || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc),
       (select count(*) = 0 from exc where original_at is null)
union all
select 'historical_exceptions_with_no_reason_they_cannot_be_reconstructed',
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc),
       (select count(*)::text from exc where coalesce(btrim(cannot_reconstruct),'') = '')
         || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc),
       (select count(*) = 0 from exc where coalesce(btrim(cannot_reconstruct),'') = '')
union all
select 'historical_exceptions_dated_after_the_kernel_cutover',
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc where original_at is not null),
       (select count(*)::text from exc where original_at is not null and original_at >= kernel_cutover_at)
         || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from exc where original_at is not null),
       -- A "historical" exception that happened after the kernel took over is not historical. It
       -- is a live defect wearing the wrong label, and that is worth failing on.
       (select count(*) = 0 from exc where original_at is not null and original_at >= kernel_cutover_at)
union all
select 'register_is_append_only',
       'a trigger refusing UPDATE and DELETE',
       (select case when count(*) = 1 then 'present' else 'MISSING' end
          from pg_trigger tg join pg_class c on c.oid = tg.tgrelid
         where c.relname = 'phase_c_historical_repair'
           and tg.tgname = 'a00_phase_c_historical_repair_append_only'
           and not tg.tgisinternal and tg.tgenabled <> 'D'),
       (select count(*) = 1 from pg_trigger tg join pg_class c on c.oid = tg.tgrelid
         where c.relname = 'phase_c_historical_repair'
           and tg.tgname = 'a00_phase_c_historical_repair_append_only'
           and not tg.tgisinternal and tg.tgenabled <> 'D');

fn_kernel_cutover_measure:
with
body as (
  select p.oid, p.proname,
         regexp_replace(regexp_replace(p.prosrc, '/\*.*?\*/', ' ', 'g'), '--[^\n]*', ' ', 'g') src
    from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
   where n.nspname = 'public'
),
-- A routine that reaches the kernel by ANY of the three doors the specification allows.
kernel_caller as (
  select b.proname from body b
   where b.src ~ '\yfn_kernel_trigger_submit\s*\('
      or b.src ~ '\yfn_kernel_signal_submit\s*\('
      or b.src ~ '\yfn_kernel_source_emit\s*\('
),
protected(t) as (values
  ('phase_c_workflow_run'),('phase_c_workflow_step_run'),('phase_c_task'),('phase_c_handoff_run'),
  ('kernel_trigger_inbox'),('kernel_signal_inbox'),('phase_c_event_outbox'),('phase_c_refund_decision')),
-- A routine that writes business work DIRECTLY. Anything on the kernel's own allow-list is
-- excluded: fn_kernel_step_complete writes those tables because it is the kernel.
direct_writer as (
  select distinct b.proname from body b join protected pr
      on b.src ~ ('(insert\s+into|update|delete\s+from)\s+(public\.)?' || pr.t || '\M')
   where not exists (select 1 from public.kernel_write_authority a where a.routine_name = b.proname)
),
-- The trigger a source names as discharging it, resolved to the routine it actually fires.
named as (
  select c.source_component_id, c.source_class, c.current_activation, c.status,
         c.disposition_evidence, c.target_step_or_signal, c.idempotency_key, c.trace_policy,
         split_part(c.disposition_evidence, ':', 1) as ev_kind,
         split_part(c.disposition_evidence, ':', 2) as ev_ref,
         case split_part(c.disposition_evidence, ':', 1)
           when 'routine' then split_part(c.disposition_evidence, ':', 2)
           when 'trigger' then (select p.proname from pg_trigger tg join pg_proc p on p.oid = tg.tgfoid
                                 where tg.tgname = split_part(c.disposition_evidence, ':', 2)
                                   and not tg.tgisinternal limit 1)
         end as ev_routine
    from public.phase_c_source_cutover c
),
judged as (
  select n.*,
         case
           when n.current_activation = 'DISABLED'
             or n.source_class = 'D RETIRE_OR_HISTORICAL'
             or n.ev_kind = 'retired'                      then 'RETIRED_OR_INACTIVE'
           when n.ev_kind in ('read_only','inactive') and n.source_class = 'C READ_ONLY_MONITOR'
                                                            then 'READ_ONLY'
           -- ROOT CAUSE 3. CUT_OVER used to mean ONLY "the named routine calls a function whose
           -- name contains kernel". That is the caller knocking. Ten ACTIVE sources were reported
           -- CUT_OVER while fn_kernel_signal_submit refused every submission they made, because
           -- their signal type was registered inactive. CUT_OVER now requires all seven:
           --   (a) the source is active                       — the outer case already established
           --   (b) the canonical adapter is deployed          — ev_routine resolves to a real routine
           --   (c) the routine reaches a kernel door          — kernel_caller
           --   (d) for a workflow SIGNAL, the type is ACTIVE and registered
           --   (e) the handler exists                         — a disposition the service implements
           --   (f) the handler accepts at least one valid state — a non-terminal workflow state exists
           --   (g) idempotency and trace policy are recorded on the source row
           when n.ev_kind in ('routine','trigger') and n.ev_routine is not null
                and exists (select 1 from kernel_caller k where k.proname = n.ev_routine)
                and (n.source_class not like 'B %' or exists (
                      select 1 from public.kernel_signal_type t
                       where t.signal_type = n.target_step_or_signal
                         and t.activation_state = 'active'
                         and t.disposition in ('ATTACH_ONLY','COMPLETE_STEP','REVIEW_VERDICT','CANCEL')))
                and exists (select 1 from public.phase_b_workflow_state ws where not ws.terminal)
                and coalesce(btrim(n.idempotency_key),'') <> ''
                and coalesce(btrim(n.trace_policy),'') <> ''
                                                            then 'CUT_OVER'
           else 'BYPASSING'
         end as verdict
    from named n
)
select 'total_sources'::text, 'reported, not asserted'::text,
       (select count(*)::text from judged), true
union all
select 'active_sources', 'reported',
       (select count(*)::text from judged where current_activation = 'ACTIVE'), true
union all
select 'inactive_sources', 'reported',
       (select count(*)::text from judged where current_activation = 'DISABLED'), true
union all
select 'class_split', 'reported',
       (select string_agg(source_class || ' ' || n::text, '; ' order by source_class)
          from (select source_class, count(*) n from judged group by 1) d), true
union all
select 'verdict_split', 'reported',
       (select string_agg(verdict || ' ' || n::text, '; ' order by verdict)
          from (select verdict, count(*) n from judged group by 1) d), true
union all
-- THE line. No expected numerator: it counts what it finds.
select 'active_sources_bypassing_the_kernel', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from judged where verdict = 'BYPASSING' and current_activation = 'ACTIVE')
         || coalesce(' [' || (select string_agg(source_component_id, ', ')
              from judged where verdict = 'BYPASSING' and current_activation = 'ACTIVE') || ']', ''),
       (select count(*) = 0 from judged where verdict = 'BYPASSING' and current_activation = 'ACTIVE')
union all
select 'active_sources_with_no_disposition_evidence', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from judged
         where current_activation = 'ACTIVE' and coalesce(btrim(disposition_evidence),'') = '')
         || coalesce(' [' || (select string_agg(source_component_id, ', ') from judged
              where current_activation = 'ACTIVE' and coalesce(btrim(disposition_evidence),'') = '') || ']', ''),
       (select count(*) = 0 from judged
         where current_activation = 'ACTIVE' and coalesce(btrim(disposition_evidence),'') = '')
union all
-- A claim that names a trigger which does not exist, or exists and does not call the kernel.
select 'coverage_claims_with_nothing_behind_them', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from judged
         where ev_kind in ('routine','trigger')
           and (ev_routine is null
                or not exists (select 1 from kernel_caller k where k.proname = ev_routine)))
         || coalesce(' [' || (select string_agg(source_component_id || ' -> ' || disposition_evidence, ', ')
              from judged where ev_kind in ('routine','trigger')
                and (ev_routine is null
                     or not exists (select 1 from kernel_caller k where k.proname = ev_routine))) || ']', ''),
       (select count(*) = 0 from judged
         where ev_kind in ('routine','trigger')
           and (ev_routine is null
                or not exists (select 1 from kernel_caller k where k.proname = ev_routine)))
union all
-- ROOT CAUSE 3. The line that would have caught it. An ACTIVE source whose signal type does not
-- accept submissions is not cut over, however its adapter is written.
select 'active_sources_targeting_an_inactive_signal_type', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from judged j
         where j.current_activation = 'ACTIVE' and j.source_class like 'B %'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.kernel_signal_type t
                            where t.signal_type = j.target_step_or_signal
                              and t.activation_state = 'active'))
         || coalesce(' [' || (select string_agg(j.source_component_id || ' -> ' || j.target_step_or_signal, ', ')
              from judged j where j.current_activation = 'ACTIVE' and j.source_class like 'B %'
                and not exists (select 1 from public.kernel_signal_type t
                                 where t.signal_type = j.target_step_or_signal
                                   and t.activation_state = 'active')) || ']', ''),
       (select count(*) = 0 from judged j
         where j.current_activation = 'ACTIVE' and j.source_class like 'B %'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.kernel_signal_type t
                            where t.signal_type = j.target_step_or_signal
                              and t.activation_state = 'active'))

union all
-- An active signal type with no handler the service implements is a door with nothing behind it.
select 'active_signal_types_without_a_handler', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from public.kernel_signal_type t
         where t.activation_state = 'active'
           and t.disposition not in ('ATTACH_ONLY','COMPLETE_STEP','REVIEW_VERDICT','CANCEL')),
       (select count(*) = 0 from public.kernel_signal_type t
         where t.activation_state = 'active'
           and t.disposition not in ('ATTACH_ONLY','COMPLETE_STEP','REVIEW_VERDICT','CANCEL'))

union all
-- Reported for the record: how many verdicts rest on nothing but source-text caller detection.
select 'cutover_rows_resting_only_on_source_text_caller_detection', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from judged j
         where j.verdict = 'CUT_OVER' and j.source_class like 'B %'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.kernel_signal_type t
                            where t.signal_type = j.target_step_or_signal
                              and t.activation_state = 'active')),
       (select count(*) = 0 from judged j
         where j.verdict = 'CUT_OVER' and j.source_class like 'B %'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.kernel_signal_type t
                            where t.signal_type = j.target_step_or_signal
                              and t.activation_state = 'active'))

union all
-- An ACTIVE source whose own routine writes a protected table directly. The kernel's own writers
-- are excluded by kernel_write_authority, so this is a genuine bypass and not the kernel itself.
select 'active_sources_writing_business_work_directly', '0',
       (select count(*)::text from judged j
         where j.current_activation = 'ACTIVE'
           and exists (select 1 from direct_writer w
                        where w.proname = (select p.proname from pg_trigger tg
                                             join pg_proc p on p.oid = tg.tgfoid
                                            where tg.tgname = split_part(j.source_component_id, ':', 3)
                                              and not tg.tgisinternal limit 1))),
       (select count(*) = 0 from judged j
         where j.current_activation = 'ACTIVE'
           and exists (select 1 from direct_writer w
                        where w.proname = (select p.proname from pg_trigger tg
                                             join pg_proc p on p.oid = tg.tgfoid
                                            where tg.tgname = split_part(j.source_component_id, ':', 3)
                                              and not tg.tgisinternal limit 1)));
fn_kernel_retired_grant_state:
with g as (
  select r.path_name, r.disposition,
         coalesce((select string_agg(rp.grantee || ':' || rp.privilege_type, ', ')
                     from information_schema.routine_privileges rp
                    where rp.routine_schema = 'public' and rp.routine_name = r.path_name
                      and rp.grantee in ('anon','authenticated','service_role','PUBLIC')), '') ordinary
    from public.kernel_retired_path r
)
select 'retired_paths_executable_by_an_ordinary_role'::text,
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from g),
       (select count(*)::text from g where ordinary <> '') || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from g)
         || coalesce(' [' || (select string_agg(path_name || ' -> ' || ordinary, '; ')
              from g where ordinary <> '') || ']', ''),
       (select count(*) = 0 from g where ordinary <> '')
union all
select 'retired_paths_with_a_recorded_final_state',
       (select count(*)::text from g) || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from g),
       (select string_agg(disposition || ' ' || n::text, '; ' order by disposition)
          from (select disposition, count(*) n from g group by 1) d),
       (select count(*) = 0 from g where coalesce(btrim(disposition),'') = '')
union all
-- A compatibility wrapper must reach the kernel and nothing else. Measured from the deployed body,

select 'compatibility_wrappers_not_calling_the_kernel',
       '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from g where disposition = 'COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER_TO_KERNEL'),
       (select count(*)::text from g
         join pg_proc p on p.proname = g.path_name
         join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
        where g.disposition = 'COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER_TO_KERNEL'
          and regexp_replace(regexp_replace(p.prosrc,'/\*.*?\*/',' ','g'),'--[^\n]*',' ','g')
              !~ '\yfn_kernel_')
         || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from g where disposition = 'COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER_TO_KERNEL'),
       (select count(*) = 0 from g
         join pg_proc p on p.proname = g.path_name
         join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
        where g.disposition = 'COMPATIBILITY_WRAPPER_TO_KERNEL'

              !~ '\yfn_kernel_');

fn_kernel_system_execution_begin:
declare v_comp public.phase_c_component%rowtype; v_trace bigint;
begin
  select * into v_comp from public.phase_c_component where component_id = p_input->>'component_id';
  if not found then
    raise exception 'fn_kernel_system_execution_begin: component % is not registered', p_input->>'component_id'
      using errcode = '23503';
  end if;
  if coalesce(btrim(p_input->>'correlation_id'),'') = ''
     or coalesce(btrim(p_input->>'causation_id'),'') = '' then
    raise exception 'fn_kernel_system_execution_begin: correlation_id and causation_id are required '
      'at BEGIN. An execution that cannot be joined to what caused it is not traceable afterwards '
      'by adding the ids later.' using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  v_trace := public.fn_phase_c_trace_write('TRACE-SYSTEM-EXECUTION', jsonb_build_object(
    'subject_kind',     'system_execution',
    'subject_ref',      v_comp.component_id,
    'component_id',     v_comp.component_id,
    'system_actor_id',  coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'system_actor',''), v_comp.canonical_system_actor),
    'actor_role_id',    coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'accountable_role_id',''), v_comp.accountable_role_id),
    'manager_role_id',  coalesce((select manager_role_id from public.org_role
                                   where role_id = coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'accountable_role_id',''),
                                                            v_comp.accountable_role_id)), ''),
    'authority_result', coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'authority_result',''), 'pending_at_begin'),
    'state_before',     coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'state_before',''), 'not_started'),
    'state_after',      'in_flight',
    'input_hash',       coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'input_hash',''),
                                 case when p_input ? 'input' then md5(p_input->>'input')
                                      else 'no_input_recorded' end),
    'output_hash',      'not_finished',
    'evidence_refs',    jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
                          'lifecycle', 'begin',
                          'correlation_id', p_input->>'correlation_id',
                          'causation_id',   p_input->>'causation_id',
                          'trigger_source', coalesce(p_input->>'trigger_source','(unstated)'),
                          'started_at', coalesce(nullif(p_input->>'started_at','')::timestamptz, now()))),
    'status',           'open'));
  return v_trace;
end
fn_kernel_system_execution_fail:
select public.fn_kernel_system_execution_close(p_trace, p_input || jsonb_build_object(
    'result', 'failed',
    'failure', coalesce(nullif(btrim(p_input->>'failure'),''),
                        coalesce(p_input->>'sqlstate','') || ' ' || coalesce(p_input->>'message','(no message)')),
    'retry_eligible', coalesce(p_input->>'retry_eligible','false')::boolean));
fn_kernel_intake_execution:
declare v_trace bigint; v_result text;
begin
  v_result := case
    when coalesce(p_trace_input->>'state_after','') in ('refused','rejected') then 'refused'
    when coalesce(p_trace_input->>'state_after','') = 'deferred' then 'no_op'
    else 'succeeded' end;

  v_trace := public.fn_kernel_system_execution_begin(jsonb_build_object(
    'component_id',    p_component,
    'correlation_id',  coalesce(nullif(p_trace_input->>'correlation_id',''), 'intake:' || p_component),
    'causation_id',    coalesce(nullif(p_trace_input->>'causation_id',''), 'intake:' || p_component),
    'authority_result', p_trace_input->>'authority_result',
    'state_before',    p_trace_input->>'state_before',
    'input_hash',      p_trace_input->>'input_hash',
    'trigger_source',  coalesce(nullif(p_trace_input->>'trigger_source',''),
                                'kernel door ' || p_component)));

  -- Everything the door said about its own subject is preserved on the trace rather than dropped:
  -- the run, the step run, the task and the door's original subject_ref stay readable.
  update public.phase_c_trace set
    run_id       = coalesce(nullif(p_trace_input->>'run_id','')::bigint, run_id),
    parent_trace_id = coalesce(
      nullif(p_trace_input->>'parent_trace_id','')::bigint,
      (select r.trace_id from public.phase_c_workflow_run r
        where r.run_id = nullif(p_trace_input->>'run_id','')::bigint),
      parent_trace_id),
    step_run_id  = coalesce(nullif(p_trace_input->>'step_run_id','')::bigint, step_run_id),
    task_id      = coalesce(nullif(p_trace_input->>'task_id','')::bigint, task_id),
    evidence_refs = coalesce(evidence_refs,'[]'::jsonb) || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
      'door_subject_kind', p_trace_input->>'subject_kind',
      'door_subject_ref',  p_trace_input->>'subject_ref',
      'door_evidence',     p_trace_input->'evidence_refs'))
  where trace_id = v_trace;

  return public.fn_kernel_system_execution_close(v_trace, jsonb_build_object(
    'result',      v_result,
    'state_after', p_trace_input->>'state_after',
    'output_hash', p_trace_input->>'output_hash',
    'failure',     case when v_result = 'failed' then p_trace_input->>'failure' end));
end
fn_refund_founder_decision_only:
begin

    using errcode = '42501',
          hint = 'Every refund needs the founder, at any amount — his instruction, 17 Aug 2026. '
              || 'A refund reaches ''approved'' only through fn_refund_decide, and only with a '
              || 'decided_by that is an active row in public.phase_c_founder_identity. '
              || 'Before this guard, fn_refund_request auto-approved anything inside the promised '
              || 'window and under org_authority(customer_success, refund_within_window) — AED '
              || '2,000 — writing decided_by = ''policy:auto_window'' and setting '

fn_phase_c_event_runtime_observation:

           else                                                         'NEVER_OBSERVED'

fn_phase_c_event_truth_state:
select 'stored_structural_status_disagrees_with_derived'::text,
         '0'::text,
         (select count(*)::text from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state where structural_status_disagrees)
           || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_event_binding),
         (select count(*) from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state where structural_status_disagrees) = 0
  union all
  select 'registry_only_event_presented_as_runtime_observed'::text,
         '0 — structurally impossible: runtime observation is derived, not stored'::text,
         '0 of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_event_binding),
         true
  union all
  select 'structurally_connected'::text,
         'reported, never read as a runtime claim'::text,
         (select count(*)::text from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state
           where structural_status_derived = 'CONNECTED')
           || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_event_binding),
         true
  union all
  select 'runtime_observed_at_least_once'::text,
         'reported; it rises as the runtime is released'::text,
         (select count(*)::text from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state
           where runtime_observation <> 'NEVER_OBSERVED')
           || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_event_binding),
         true
  union all
  -- The one that would have caught the original defect if it had existed: an event the registry
  -- calls deferred, which is nevertheless running.
  --
  -- SCOPED TO THE CURRENT REGIME, AND THE HISTORY IS REPORTED ON ITS OWN LINE BELOW. On its first
  -- run this check fired at 1 of 60: EV-W06-COMPLETED, emitted and delivered once at
  -- 2026-08-16 23:15:23 — three minutes BEFORE the kernel epoch at 23:18:23. A pre-cutover emission
  -- by the runtime the kernel replaced is not a live contradiction, and counting it would hold this
  -- check red forever over a row nothing can now produce. Splitting the population by the epoch is
  -- the same discipline fn_kernel_system_trace_state already applies to cron executions.
  --
  -- last_seen, not first_seen: a binding that emitted before the cutover AND after it is a live
  -- contradiction and must still fail.
  select 'deferred_binding_that_is_actually_running'::text,
         '0 since the kernel epoch'::text,
         (select count(*)::text from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state s
           where s.structural_status_derived = 'DEFERRED_RUNTIME_IMPLEMENTATION'
             and s.last_seen >= (select started_at from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch
                                  where epoch_id = 'S3_SYSTEM_EXECUTION_TRACING'))
           || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_event_binding
                          where connection_status = 'DEFERRED_RUNTIME_IMPLEMENTATION'),
         (select count(*) from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state s
           where s.structural_status_derived = 'DEFERRED_RUNTIME_IMPLEMENTATION'
             and s.last_seen >= (select started_at from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch
                                  where epoch_id = 'S3_SYSTEM_EXECUTION_TRACING')) = 0
  union all
  select 'deferred_binding_that_ran_before_the_kernel_epoch'::text,
         'informational — historical, produced by the runtime the kernel replaced'::text,
         (select count(*)::text from public.v_phase_c_event_binding_state s
           where s.structural_status_derived = 'DEFERRED_RUNTIME_IMPLEMENTATION'
             and s.runtime_observation <> 'NEVER_OBSERVED'
             and s.last_seen < (select started_at from public.phase_c_kernel_epoch
                                 where epoch_id = 'S3_SYSTEM_EXECUTION_TRACING'))
           || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_event_binding
                          where connection_status = 'DEFERRED_RUNTIME_IMPLEMENTATION'),
         true;

fn_kernel_truncate_protection_state:
with enforcing as (
    select distinct c.relname as tbl
      from pg_trigger   tg
      join pg_class     c  on c.oid = tg.tgrelid
      join pg_namespace ns on ns.oid = c.relnamespace
      join pg_proc      p  on p.oid = tg.tgfoid
     where ns.nspname = 'public'
       and not tg.tgisinternal
       and (tg.tgtype & 32) = 0
       and p.prokind = 'f'
       and pg_get_functiondef(p.oid) ilike '%raise exception%'
  ),
  guarded as (
    select distinct c.relname as tbl
      from pg_trigger   tg
      join pg_class     c  on c.oid = tg.tgrelid
      join pg_namespace ns on ns.oid = c.relnamespace
     where ns.nspname = 'public'
       and not tg.tgisinternal
       and (tg.tgtype & 32) <> 0
  ),
  m as (
    select e.tbl,
           (e.tbl in (select tbl from guarded)) as has_guard,
           (   has_table_privilege('service_role',  format('public.%I', e.tbl), 'TRUNCATE')
            or has_table_privilege('authenticated', format('public.%I', e.tbl), 'TRUNCATE')
            or has_table_privilege('anon',          format('public.%I', e.tbl), 'TRUNCATE')
           ) as grants_truncate
      from enforcing e
  )
  select 'enforcing_tables_without_a_truncate_guard',
         '0',
         count(*) filter (where not has_guard)::text || ' of ' || count(*)::text,
         count(*) filter (where not has_guard) = 0
    from m
  union all
  select 'enforcing_tables_still_granting_truncate',
         '0',
         count(*) filter (where grants_truncate)::text || ' of ' || count(*)::text,
         count(*) filter (where grants_truncate) = 0
    from m
  union all
  -- Informational, and it is the number that made the defect invisible: how many tables the old
  -- typed list covered. Kept so a reader can see the population this check watches is derived.
  select 'raw_enforcing_tables_watched',
         'informational',
         count(*)::text || ' of ' || count(*)::text,
         true
    from m;
fn_phase_c_freeze_drift:
with live as (
    select f.subject, f.object_identity, f.digest as frozen,
           case
             when f.object_kind = 'routine' then (
               select encode(sha256(convert_to(pg_get_functiondef(p.oid),'UTF8')),'hex')
                 from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid=p.pronamespace
                where n.nspname='public'
                  and p.proname || '(' || pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid) || ')'
                      = f.object_identity)
             when f.object_kind = 'table' and f.object_identity = 'public.phase_c_component' then (
               select encode(sha256(convert_to(string_agg(
                 c.component_id || '|' || coalesce(c.component_type,'') || '|' || coalesce(c.workflow_id,'')
                   || '|' || coalesce(c.step_id,'') || '|' || coalesce(c.accountable_role_id,'')
                   || '|' || coalesce(c.canonical_system_actor,'') || '|' || coalesce(c.authority_class,'')
                   || '|' || coalesce(c.trace_policy_id,'') || '|' || coalesce(c.activation_state,'')
                   || '|' || coalesce(c.classification,'') || '|' || coalesce(c.mutates_state::text,''),
                 chr(10) order by c.component_id),'UTF8')),'hex')
                 from public.phase_c_component c)
             else f.digest   -- repository_file subjects are checked in CI, not here; never silently green
           end as now_digest
      from public.phase_c_frozen_subject f
  ), judged as (
    -- D49. A live digest is undrifted when it matches the frozen baseline, OR when a recorded
    -- amendment carries BOTH the frozen baseline as its prior digest AND this body as its new one.
    -- An unrecorded edit is drift. An edit on top of an amendment is drift, because its prior digest
    -- no longer matches. Overwriting phase_c_frozen_subject.digest would have made both invisible.
    --
    -- E13 required the amendment to name a Phase C change request. E23 makes that reference a
    -- foreign key to public.phase_c_change_request, so an amendment can no longer point at a
    -- document nobody wrote.
    select l.*,
           exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment a
                    where a.object_identity = l.object_identity
                      and a.prior_digest = l.frozen
                      and a.new_digest   = l.now_digest
                      and coalesce(btrim(a.change_request_ref),'') <> '') as amended
      from live l
  )
  select 'frozen_subjects_drifted', '0',
         count(*) filter (where now_digest is distinct from frozen and not amended)::text
           || ' of ' || count(*)::text,
         count(*) filter (where now_digest is distinct from frozen and not amended) = 0
    from judged
  union all
  select 'frozen_subjects_whose_object_no_longer_exists', '0',
         count(*) filter (where now_digest is null)::text || ' of ' || count(*)::text,
         count(*) filter (where now_digest is null) = 0
    from judged
  union all
  select 'frozen_subjects_changed_under_a_recorded_amendment', 'informational',
         count(*) filter (where amended)::text || ' of ' || count(*)::text, true
    from judged
  union all
  -- E23 REPLACES frozen_subjects_changed_with_no_change_request, WHICH COULD NOT FIRE.
  -- That row tested btrim(change_request_ref) = '' on a column that is NOT NULL and shape-checked,
  -- so it read 0 of 25 whatever anyone did. The R3 acceptance named it, correctly, as a green tick
  -- measuring nothing. What is checkable is whether the MECHANISM is still in place, and this row
  -- goes red the moment any of the three constraints is dropped.
  select 'change_request_reference_is_enforced', '3',
         -- The three are counted into ONE number. An earlier draft printed the two constraints as
         -- "2 of 3" and reported the NOT NULL separately, which read as a failing check sitting
         -- next to a green tick — the precise confusion this row exists to end.
         ((select count(*) from pg_constraint
            where conrelid = 'public.phase_c_freeze_amendment'::regclass
              and conname in ('phase_c_freeze_amendment_change_request_ref_shape',
                              'phase_c_freeze_amendment_change_request_fk'))
          + (select count(*) from information_schema.columns
              where table_schema='public' and table_name='phase_c_freeze_amendment'
                and column_name='change_request_ref' and is_nullable='NO'))::text
         || ' of 3 (shape check, foreign key to phase_c_change_request, NOT NULL)',
         (select count(*) from pg_constraint
           where conrelid = 'public.phase_c_freeze_amendment'::regclass
             and conname in ('phase_c_freeze_amendment_change_request_ref_shape',
                             'phase_c_freeze_amendment_change_request_fk')) = 2
         and (select count(*) from information_schema.columns
               where table_schema='public' and table_name='phase_c_freeze_amendment'
                 and column_name='change_request_ref' and is_nullable='NO') = 1
  union all
  select 'amendments_whose_change_request_is_unregistered', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment a
           where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_change_request cr
                              where cr.change_request_ref = a.change_request_ref))
         || ' of ' || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment a
                      where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_change_request cr
                                         where cr.change_request_ref = a.change_request_ref))
  union all
  -- E34. THIS ROW'S ok WAS THE LITERAL true, AND IT READ 4 of 4.
  --
  -- Its own comment was candid - "Reported, never used. A change request that has been WRITTEN is
  -- not one that has been APPROVED" - and the consequence stood anyway: four amendments to frozen
  -- Phase C kernel contracts are live in production, unapproved, under a fully green board. The
  -- independent acceptance named it as the same species this estate keeps finding, a board row
  -- whose ok is a constant, and scored it LOW because it was disclosed. Disclosed in a comment is
  -- not disclosed on the board.
  --
  -- It is now a REAL RED, and it goes green the moment the founder signs. That is the right colour
  -- because the condition is genuinely unmet: an amendment to a frozen contract is not complete
  -- until the person who froze it has approved the change. Nothing here can clear it and nothing
  -- here should be able to - approved_by and approved_at are constrained to move as a pair, and a
  -- builder writing his own name into them would be the whole defect this row exists to surface.
  --
  -- 'expected' is now 0 rather than the word 'informational', so a reader comparing expected with
  -- actual sees the gap instead of a label that excuses it.
  -- E38. THIS ASKED `approved_by is null`, WHICH IS A QUESTION ABOUT A STORED STRING.
  -- An acceptance auditor added itself to public.phase_c_founder_identity as an email identity
  -- (service_role held INSERT), approved all four amendments with it, and DELETED the row again --
  -- leaving four approvals naming a string that resolves to nobody, and this row green. E38 revoked
  -- those write grants; this half asks the question fresh instead of trusting what was stored, so
  -- deleting the approver re-reddens the board in the same statement. It is also the backstop for
  -- an owner disabling the trigger: a guard can be turned off, a derivation cannot.
  select 'amendments_awaiting_founder_approval', '0',
         (select count(*) from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment a
           where a.approved_by is null
              or not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_founder_identity fi
                              where fi.active
                                and lower(btrim(fi.identity)) = lower(btrim(a.approved_by))))::text
           || ' of ' || (select count(*) from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment)::text
           || ' await the founder (change requests named: '
           || (select coalesce(string_agg(distinct change_request_ref, ', '),'(none)')
                 from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment)
           -- E36. THIS SAID "Only he can clear this row." and nothing enforced it: approved_by was
           -- free text, and the acceptance auditor cleared all four with 'zz-r5-audit-not-the-founder'
           -- in one statement, turning the whole freeze board green. The trigger
           -- a10_freeze_amendment_approver_is_the_founder now refuses any approver that does not
           -- resolve to an ACTIVE row in public.phase_c_founder_identity. The row names the register
           -- rather than a person, because the register is what the database can check.
           || '). Cleared only while approved_by RESOLVES to one of the '
           || (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_founder_identity where active)
           || ' active identities in public.phase_c_founder_identity -- asked here on every read, and enforced at write time by a10_freeze_amendment_approver_is_the_founder.',
         (select count(*) from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment a
           where a.approved_by is null
              or not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_founder_identity fi
                              where fi.active
                                and lower(btrim(fi.identity)) = lower(btrim(a.approved_by)))) = 0
  union all
  -- F31. HOW THE APPROVAL WAS GIVEN, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS WHETHER THERE IS ONE.
  --
  -- The row above asks whether approved_by resolves to an active founder identity. It cannot tell
  -- an approval the founder placed through a verified Supabase Auth session from one a migration
  -- wrote on the strength of an instruction he sent in a message. Both leave the same string in the
  -- same column. F23 wrote the second kind for PCCR-003 and said so in its own header; nothing on
  -- any board repeated it, so a reader saw "approved by the founder" and had no way to learn which.
  --
  -- This row is red while any approval rests on WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION. It is a disclosure, not an
  -- accusation: the instruction is real, quoted verbatim in the change request, and the design it
  -- approves is strictly harder to pass than the one it replaced. What is missing is his signature
  -- through the door F20 built and F21 granted, and that is his to give, not this repository's.
  select 'amendments_approved_on_written_instruction_only', '0',
         (select count(*) from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment
           where approval_basis = 'WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION')::text
         || ' of ' || (select count(*) from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment)::text
         || ' (change requests: '
         || (select coalesce(string_agg(distinct change_request_ref, ', '),'(none)')
               from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment where approval_basis = 'WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION')
         || '). An approval recorded from a written instruction is not a founder session. Cleared '
         || 'only by re-approval through a verified auth subject, which no migration can perform.',
         (select count(*) from public.phase_c_freeze_amendment
           where approval_basis = 'WRITTEN_INSTRUCTION') = 0
  union all
  select 'raw_frozen_subjects', 'informational',
         count(*)::text || ' of ' || count(*)::text, true
    from judged;
fn_phase_c_founder_approval_immutable:
begin
  -- E40. This message was hard-coded to `public.phase_c_founder_approval` while the trigger sits on
  -- phase_c_frozen_subject as well, so a person hitting it was told the wrong table -- and then
  -- advised to "record a NEW row", which until this file was the one door standing open on that
  -- register. It names what it is actually protecting now.
  raise exception '% is append-only and its rows are permanent: % is refused. A founder approval and the frozen subjects it covers are the record that everything else is measured against, so they are never edited or deleted -- record a new row through a migration applied as the owner. (phase_c_approval_immutable)',
    TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP
    using errcode = '23514';
end
fn_phase_d_handler_execute:
declare
  v_review jsonb;   -- F34: the recorded canonical internal review for this step run
  b   public.phase_d_handler_binding%rowtype;
  s   public.phase_b_workflow_step%rowtype;
  sr  public.phase_c_workflow_step_run%rowtype;
  ec  public.phase_d_step_effect%rowtype;
  v_step_run bigint := nullif(p_input->>'step_run_id','')::bigint;
  v_actor    text   := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'actor_role_id','')),'');
  v_idem     text   := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'idempotency_key','')),'');
  v_inputs   jsonb  := coalesce(p_input->'inputs','{}'::jsonb);
  v_ctx      text   := lower(coalesce(nullif(btrim(p_input->>'execution_context'),''),'production'));
  v_ok       boolean; v_reason text; v_missing text[];
  v_rule     record; v_rule_ok boolean; v_rule_type text; v_rule_reason text;
  v_applies  boolean; v_why text; v_enforced boolean; v_refusal text; v_state text;
  v_ev_absent boolean := false;   -- E19
  v_refused  jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
  v_skipped  jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
  v_gate     record; v_gstate text; v_gpassed boolean; v_gtype text;
  v_greason  text; v_grefusal text; v_gapplies boolean; v_gwhy text;
  v_gates    jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
  v_gblocked jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
  v_evaluated jsonb := '[]'::jsonb;
  v_output   jsonb;
  v_assert   jsonb;
  v_result   jsonb;
  v_effect   jsonb;
  v_cap      jsonb;   -- F05: the accepted capability result for this step run, or null
  v_cap_req  jsonb;   -- F05: the capability request this handler opened
begin
  -- ---- 0. the call itself ------------------------------------------------------------------
  if v_step_run is null or v_actor is null or v_idem is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step_run_id, actor_role_id and idempotency_key are all required (got %, %, %) (pd_input_schema_invalid)',
      coalesce(v_step_run::text,'(null)'), coalesce(v_actor,'(null)'), coalesce(v_idem,'(null)')
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;
  if v_ctx not in ('production','test') then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: execution_context must be production or test, got %',
      v_ctx using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  select * into sr from public.phase_c_workflow_step_run where step_run_id = v_step_run;
  if not found then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: no step run % (pd_step_state_invalid)', v_step_run
      using errcode = '23503';
  end if;

  -- ---- 0b. THE BRANCH PROBE'S HOLD --------------------------------------------------------
  -- Section 1 of the founder's ruling asks for BRANCH coverage of all 257 frozen steps. The frozen
  -- model is a linear chain: next_step_if_pass names the next step (or WORKFLOW_COMPLETE), and
  -- next_step_if_fail names one of three symbolic outcomes and never a step. So a step's fail edge
  -- is exercised by an ACTOR reporting failure on it, which requires the step to be OPEN.
  --
  -- MEASURED 23 Aug 2026: 249 of 257 steps are completed by this handler in the same statement the
  -- kernel opens them, so they are never open and no actor can ever take them. W18 is the extreme
  -- case -- all seven steps EXECUTED unaided, the run reaching completed inside
  -- fn_kernel_workflow_start, nothing left to fail or cancel. A handler that succeeds is the
  -- system working; it also means the fail edge of the frozen model is unreachable through the
  -- actor door, and an unexercised branch cannot be reported as covered.
  --
  -- This is the hold, and every part of it is deliberately narrow:
  --   * it acts only inside an open Phase D fixture context, which fn_phase_d_test_context_open
  --     grants for one operation inside one transaction that ends in raise exception;
  --   * it names ONE step, set by the caller at transaction level, and never a workflow or a class;
  --   * it refuses with its own code, pd_handler_held_for_branch_probe, which appears in
  --     phase_d_dispatch.refusal_code -- so no reader, and no deliverable, can mistake a held step
  --     for a handler that could not do its work;
  --   * it changes nothing else. The kernel then does exactly what it does for any refused
  --     dispatch: the step stays open and owned.
  --
  -- What the fail-branch case then proves is the KERNEL's edge for that step -- outcome fail moves
  -- the step to failed and the run to the step's declared failure_workflow_state, with no partial
  -- effect and no residue -- and NOT that the handler could have failed. Those are different
  -- claims and the coverage matrix records which one it has, per step.
  if nullif(btrim(coalesce(current_setting('app.phase_d_hold_step', true), '')), '') = sr.step_id
     and public.fn_phase_d_fixture_context() is not null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % is held open by an audited Phase D branch probe; the handler declined so an actor can take the step (pd_handler_held_for_branch_probe)',
      sr.step_id using errcode = '23505';
  end if;

  select * into b from public.phase_d_handler_binding where step_id = sr.step_id;
  if not found then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % has no Phase D handler binding — fail closed. Every one of the 257 frozen steps must carry exactly one. (pd_input_schema_invalid)',
      sr.step_id using errcode = '23503';
  end if;
  select * into s from public.phase_b_workflow_step where step_id = sr.step_id;

  select * into ec from public.phase_d_step_effect where step_id = sr.step_id;
  if not found then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % has no declared effect contract. A handler with no declared effect is the schema-only handler this phase exists to remove. (pd_effect_undeclared)',
      sr.step_id using errcode = '23503';
  end if;

  -- ---- 1. TYPED INPUT ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  select valid, reason, missing into v_ok, v_reason, v_missing
    from public.fn_phase_d_schema_validate(b.input_schema_id, v_inputs);
  if not v_ok then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % input rejected: % (pd_input_schema_invalid)',
      sr.step_id, v_reason using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  -- ---- 2. RULES IN SCOPE -------------------------------------------------------------------
  -- SCOPE IS NOT APPLICABILITY. The frozen registry scopes rules by WORKFLOW, so BR-002 is in
  -- scope for all 257 steps while only 28 of them name an independent reviewer. Asking
  -- fn_kernel_reviewer_independent about a NULL reviewer returns false, which refused an intake
  -- step for a creator/reviewer collision that could not exist. fn_phase_d_rule_applies decides
  -- both, and records the reason either way.
  --
  -- Refusals are collected rather than short-circuited: a caller told only the first thing wrong
  -- fixes one thing and comes back.
  for v_rule in select unnest(b.rule_ids) rid loop
    select applies, why into v_applies, v_why
      from public.fn_phase_d_rule_applies(v_rule.rid, sr.step_id);
    if not coalesce(v_applies,false) then
      v_skipped := v_skipped || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
        'rule_id', v_rule.rid, 'applies', false, 'why', v_why));
      continue;
    end if;

    select state, ok, rule_type, enforced, reason, refusal_code, coalesce(evidence_absent,false)
      into v_state, v_rule_ok, v_rule_type, v_enforced, v_rule_reason, v_refusal, v_ev_absent
      from public.fn_phase_d_rule_check(v_rule.rid,
        jsonb_build_object(
          'accountable_role_id', sr.accountable_role_id,
          'reviewer_role_id',    nullif(b.independent_reviewer_role_id,''),
          'actor_role_id',       v_actor,
          'step_id',             sr.step_id,
          'workflow_id',         b.workflow_id,
          'run_id',              sr.run_id,
          'founder_gate',        b.founder_gate,
          'execution_context',   v_ctx)
        || coalesce(p_input->'context','{}'::jsonb));

    v_evaluated := v_evaluated || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
      'rule_id', v_rule.rid, 'state', v_state, 'rule_type', v_rule_type, 'ok', v_rule_ok,
      'enforced', v_enforced, 'reason', v_rule_reason));

    if v_rule_type = 'hard' and v_state in ('ENFORCED_FAIL','NOT_IMPLEMENTED') then
      v_refused := v_refused || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
        'rule_id', v_rule.rid, 'state', v_state, 'rule_type', v_rule_type,
        'refusal_code', v_refusal, 'reason', v_rule_reason,
        'evidence_absent', v_ev_absent));
    end if;
  end loop;
  if jsonb_array_length(v_refused) > 0 then
    -- E19. TWO DIFFERENT EVENTS DESERVE TWO DIFFERENT NAMES. If EVERY refusal on this step is an
    -- absence of evidence, the code says so and fn_phase_d_dispatch_step records
    -- REFUSED_EVIDENCE_ABSENT. If even one rule read its evidence and judged it against policy, the
    -- whole refusal is pd_rule_refused: a genuine violation is not diluted by the absences beside
    -- it. Both refuse, and neither is a pass.
    if not exists (select 1 from jsonb_array_elements(v_refused) x
                    where not coalesce((x->>'evidence_absent')::boolean, false)) then
      raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % refused by % hard business rule(s), every one of them for evidence the call did not name rather than for a policy the call broke: % (pd_evidence_absent)',
        sr.step_id, jsonb_array_length(v_refused), v_refused::text using errcode = '23514';
    end if;
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % refused by % hard business rule(s): % (pd_rule_refused)',
      sr.step_id, jsonb_array_length(v_refused), v_refused::text using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  -- ---- 2b. GATES IN SCOPE, EACH AGAINST ITS OWN DECLARED EVIDENCE --------------------------
  for v_gate in select unnest(b.gate_ids) gid loop
    select ga.applies, ga.why into v_gapplies, v_gwhy
      from public.fn_phase_d_gate_applies(v_gate.gid, sr.step_id) ga;
    if not coalesce(v_gapplies,false) then
      v_gates := v_gates || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
        'gate_id', v_gate.gid, 'state', 'NOT_APPLICABLE', 'why', v_gwhy));
      continue;
    end if;
    select ge.state, ge.passed, ge.gate_type, ge.reason, ge.refusal_code, coalesce(ge.evidence_absent,false)
      into v_gstate, v_gpassed, v_gtype, v_greason, v_grefusal, v_ev_absent
      from public.fn_phase_d_gate_evaluate(v_gate.gid,
        jsonb_build_object('step_id', sr.step_id, 'run_id', sr.run_id,
                           'step_run_id', v_step_run,
                           'step_run_id', v_step_run,
                           'actor_role_id', v_actor,
                           'reviewer_role_id', nullif(b.independent_reviewer_role_id,''))
        || coalesce(p_input->'gate_evidence','{}'::jsonb)) ge;

    v_gates := v_gates || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
      'gate_id', v_gate.gid, 'state', v_gstate, 'gate_type', v_gtype,
      'passed', v_gpassed, 'reason', v_greason));

    if v_gtype = 'hard' and v_gstate in ('BLOCKED','NOT_IMPLEMENTED') then
      v_gblocked := v_gblocked || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
        'gate_id', v_gate.gid, 'state', v_gstate,
        'refusal_code', v_grefusal, 'reason', v_greason,
        'evidence_absent', v_ev_absent));
    end if;
  end loop;
  if jsonb_array_length(v_gblocked) > 0 then
    if not exists (select 1 from jsonb_array_elements(v_gblocked) x
                    where not coalesce((x->>'evidence_absent')::boolean, false)) then
      raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % blocked by % hard gate(s), every one of them for evidence the call did not name rather than for a condition the gate judged and rejected: % (pd_evidence_absent)',
        sr.step_id, jsonb_array_length(v_gblocked), v_gblocked::text using errcode = '23514';
    end if;
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % refused by % hard gate(s): % (pd_gate_refused)',
      sr.step_id, jsonb_array_length(v_gblocked), v_gblocked::text using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  -- ---- 3. CAPABILITY BOUNDARY, FAIL CLOSED, AND NO LONGER A MODE STRING --------------------
  -- F05. This read `if b.capability_dependency <> 'NONE' and v_ctx <> 'test'`, so the literal
  -- 'test' arriving in one field turned twenty-one fail-closed business boundaries off at once.
  -- The founder prohibited exactly that shape on 21 Aug 2026. The mode is no longer consulted:
  -- the handler asks whether an ACCEPTED capability result exists for this step run, and the only
  -- way one exists is through fn_phase_d_capability_result_accept, which validates it against the
  -- step's own output contract and which refuses a fixture result outright unless a Phase D
  -- fixture context verifies (F01).
  --
  -- In production there is no fixture context and no provider, so there is no result, so this
  -- raises -- the same refusal, at the same point, for a reason that is now a read rather than a
  -- comparison against a caller-supplied string.
  if b.capability_dependency <> 'NONE' then
    -- The request is opened first and in every context: it is the row a Phase E provider answers,
    -- and a step that never asked cannot be said to have been refused.
    v_cap_req := public.fn_phase_d_capability_request_open(jsonb_build_object(
      'step_run_id', v_step_run, 'requested_by', v_actor));
    v_cap := public.fn_phase_d_capability_answer(v_step_run);
    if v_cap is null then
      raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % depends on capability % (matched on the frozen required_action at: %) and capability request % carries no accepted result. Paid inference is held until Phase E; a Phase D fixture result must be submitted through fn_phase_d_capability_result_accept, which requires a verified Phase D fixture context. Refusing rather than completing a business step from nothing. (pd_capability_unavailable)',
        sr.step_id, b.capability_dependency, coalesce(nullif(b.capability_evidence,''),'(none)'),
        coalesce(v_cap_req->>'request_id','(none)')
        using errcode = '23514';
    end if;
  end if;

  -- ---- 4. PROVIDER BOUNDARY, FAIL CLOSED ---------------------------------------------------
  -- Same correction, same reason. A provider dependency is refused whatever the execution context
  -- says, because the hold is on the provider and not on the caller's description of itself.
  if b.provider_dependency <> 'NONE' then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % depends on external provider % which is disabled for the whole of Phase D. No execution context lifts this. (pd_provider_disabled)',
      sr.step_id, b.provider_dependency using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  -- ---- 4b. H01. THE VERDICT THE KERNEL WILL DEMAND, ASKED FOR HERE FIRST ----------------------
  -- fn_kernel_step_complete 3g refuses a pass on a step whose frozen row names an independent
  -- reviewer unless an approved, independent verdict from that role is sealed on the task. The
  -- handler used to discover that only after producing its effect, and the refusal came out of the
  -- kernel as k3_reviewer_verdict_missing. The same predicate is asked here, before anything is
  -- built, and the refusal is the one the driver answers through fn_kernel_review_decide. Nothing
  -- about the kernel check changes; it still decides at 3g.
  if coalesce(btrim(s.independent_reviewer_role_id),'') <> ''
     and not exists (
       select 1
         from public.phase_c_task t
         join public.phase_c_trace tr on tr.task_id = t.task_id
        where t.run_id = sr.run_id and t.step_id = sr.step_id
          and tr.trace_policy_id = 'TRACE-ROLE-ACTION'
          and tr.evidence_refs @> '[{"review_decision":"approved"}]'::jsonb
          and public.fn_kernel_reviewer_independent(sr.accountable_role_id, tr.reviewer_role_id)
          and (select role_id from public.fn_phase_c_resolve_actor(tr.reviewer_role_id))
              = (select role_id from public.fn_phase_c_resolve_actor(s.independent_reviewer_role_id)))
  then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % names % as its independent reviewer and no approved, independent verdict from that role has been recorded on its task. fn_kernel_review_decide seals the verdict and stamps the reviewer; until it has run the kernel will refuse the completion, so the handler refuses here first. (pd_review_not_recorded)',
      sr.step_id, s.independent_reviewer_role_id using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  -- ---- 5. THE FAMILY HANDLER ---------------------------------------------------------------
  -- F34. The recorded canonical review for this step run, read once.
  v_review := public.fn_phase_d_recorded_review(v_step_run);

  v_assert := (
    select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
             'criterion', btrim(c), 'satisfied_by',
             'named inputs [' || array_to_string(
               (select array_agg(k order by k) from jsonb_object_keys(v_inputs) k), ', ') || ']')
             order by ord), '[]'::jsonb)
      from unnest(string_to_array(coalesce(s.acceptance_criteria,''), ';')) with ordinality u(c, ord)
     where btrim(c) <> '');

  v_output := jsonb_build_object(
    'status', 'completed',
    'output', format('%s — %s', s.step_name, coalesce(s.required_output,'output produced')),
    'acceptance_assertions', case when jsonb_array_length(v_assert) = 0
                                  then jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
                                         'criterion', coalesce(s.acceptance_criteria,'(none declared)'),
                                         'satisfied_by','named inputs'))
                                  else v_assert end,
    'evidence_refs', jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
       'step_id', sr.step_id, 'step_run_id', v_step_run, 'run_id', sr.run_id,
       'handler_id', b.handler_id, 'handler_version', b.handler_version,
       'input_schema_id', b.input_schema_id, 'output_schema_id', b.output_schema_id,
       'inputs_named', v_inputs, 'execution_context', v_ctx)))
    || case when v_cap is null then '{}'::jsonb
            else jsonb_build_object('capability_result', jsonb_build_object(
              'request_id',    v_cap->'request_id',
              'result_id',     v_cap->'result_id',
              'provider_mode', v_cap->>'provider_mode',
              'fixture_id',    v_cap->>'fixture_id',
              'fixture_version', v_cap->'fixture_version',
              'fixture_hash',  v_cap->>'fixture_hash',
              'payload_digest',v_cap->>'payload_digest',
              'evidence',      v_cap->>'evidence')) end
    || case b.handler_class
         when 'INTAKE_HANDLER' then jsonb_build_object(
           'source_ref', coalesce(p_input->>'source_ref', 'step_run:' || v_step_run),
           'captured_verbatim', v_inputs)
         when 'ANALYSIS_HANDLER' then jsonb_build_object(
           'method', 'deterministic reconciliation of the named inputs against the frozen step contract',
           'inputs_used', v_inputs,
           'findings', jsonb_build_array(coalesce(s.required_action,'')),
           'assumptions', jsonb_build_array(
             'only the inputs named in this call were used; no external source was consulted'))
         when 'EXECUTION_HANDLER' then jsonb_build_object(
           'state_change', coalesce(s.required_output,''),
           'target_object', coalesce(ec.effect_object_id,
             (select primary_object from public.phase_b_workflow w
               where w.workflow_id = b.workflow_id), b.workflow_id),
           'authorization_ref', format('accountable owner %s on step %s',
                                       sr.accountable_role_id, sr.step_id))
         -- F34. A REVIEW READ OFF THE CALLER'S OWN STRING.
         -- Both keys came from p_input, so the kernel dispatch -- which passes neither -- produced
         -- an output naming no reviewer, and BR-002 then refused the step for "names (none) as
         -- reviewer". That refusal was true and it was about this harness, not about the business.
         -- The founder's section 4 names CANONICAL_INTERNAL_REVIEW as an allowed execution input
         -- when it travels through its real interface, and that interface is fn_kernel_review_decide:
         -- it checks independence itself, seals a TRACE-ROLE-ACTION carrying the decision, and
         -- stamps phase_c_task.reviewer_role_id. Both values are therefore READ FROM THOSE ROWS.
         -- A caller can no longer assert either one.
         when 'REVIEW_HANDLER' then jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
           'verdict', v_review->'verdict',
           'reviewer_role_id', v_review->'reviewer_role_id'))
         when 'DECISION_HANDLER' then jsonb_build_object(
           'decision', coalesce(s.required_output,''),
           'rationale', coalesce(s.acceptance_criteria,''),
           'authority_ref', format('founder_gate=%s; accountable owner %s',
                                   b.founder_gate, sr.accountable_role_id))
         when 'HANDOFF_HANDLER' then jsonb_build_object(
           'packet', v_inputs,
           'receiving_role_id', coalesce((select h.receiving_role_id from public.phase_b_handoff h
                                           where h.from_step_id = sr.step_id limit 1),
                                         sr.accountable_role_id),
           'acceptance_criteria', coalesce(s.acceptance_criteria,''))
         -- F34. THE FOUR VALUES CAME FROM p_input, AND NOTHING PASSES p_input HERE.
         -- E32 stopped the harness supplying handler inputs, correctly, and the kernel dispatch
         -- passes no measurement keys, so denominator, numerator, formula and window were null on
         -- every call, jsonb_strip_nulls removed them, and the step's own output contract refused
         -- the output the handler had just built. They now come from the committed catalogue
         -- through fn_phase_d_fixture_output, which returns NULL when no row exists -- so a step
         -- with no committed measurement is still refused by its contract, and the denominator-of-0
         -- guard below is untouched.
         when 'MEASUREMENT_HANDLER' then jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
           'metric', coalesce(public.fn_phase_d_fixture_output(sr.step_id,'metric'),
                              to_jsonb(nullif(btrim(coalesce(s.required_output,'')),''))),
           'denominator', public.fn_phase_d_fixture_output(sr.step_id,'denominator'),
           'numerator', public.fn_phase_d_fixture_output(sr.step_id,'numerator'),
           'formula', public.fn_phase_d_fixture_output(sr.step_id,'formula'),
           'window', public.fn_phase_d_fixture_output(sr.step_id,'window')))
         when 'CLOSURE_HANDLER' then jsonb_build_object(
           'blockers_resolved', jsonb_build_array(
             'the frozen fn_kernel_step_complete measures the four mandatory closure blocker '
             || 'classes itself and raises k3_closure_blocked if any is open'),
           'closure_evidence', coalesce(s.closure_criteria,''))
         else '{}'::jsonb end;

  -- ---- 5a. TWO REFUSALS THE SCHEMA ALONE CANNOT MAKE ---------------------------------------
  -- F34. TWO REFUSALS THAT WORE ONE NAME. "no review has been recorded for this step" and "the
  -- recorded review names the creator" are different facts with different remedies, and both came
  -- out as pd_rule_refused/BR-002. The first is now its own code, so a driver can answer it by
  -- recording the review through the kernel's own door and asking for the step again.
  if b.handler_class = 'REVIEW_HANDLER'
     and coalesce(btrim(coalesce(v_output->>'reviewer_role_id','')),'') = '' then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % is a review step and no internal review has been recorded for it. fn_kernel_review_decide seals the verdict and stamps the reviewer on the task; until it has run there is no reviewer to name and no verdict to carry. (pd_review_not_recorded)',
      sr.step_id using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  if b.handler_class = 'REVIEW_HANDLER'
     and not public.fn_kernel_reviewer_independent(
               sr.accountable_role_id, v_output->>'reviewer_role_id') then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % is accountable to % and the review names % as reviewer; those resolve to the same effective identity. A creator cannot be the sole independent reviewer of the same output (BR-002). (pd_rule_refused)',
      sr.step_id, sr.accountable_role_id, coalesce(v_output->>'reviewer_role_id','(none)')
      using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  if b.handler_class = 'MEASUREMENT_HANDLER'
     and jsonb_typeof(v_output->'denominator') = 'number'
     and (v_output->>'denominator')::numeric = 0 then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % reported a denominator of 0. A ratio over nothing is not a measurement, and reporting it as one is how an unmeasured goal scores as perfect. (pd_output_schema_invalid)',
      sr.step_id using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  -- ---- 6. TYPED OUTPUT ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  select valid, reason, missing into v_ok, v_reason, v_missing
    from public.fn_phase_d_schema_validate(b.output_schema_id, v_output);
  if not v_ok then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_handler_execute: step % produced an output its own contract rejects: % (pd_output_schema_invalid)',
      sr.step_id, v_reason using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  -- ---- 6b. THE BUSINESS EFFECT -------------------------------------------------------------
  -- D7. Until this line existed, 257 of 257 handlers produced a typed output the kernel accepted
  -- and no business effect whatsoever, and fn_phase_d_handler_state() said so in red.
  --
  -- The effect payload comes from the CALLER, merged over the step's own facts. Nothing about the
  -- business record is invented here: a step that needs a business_key and an owner_ref and is
  -- given neither refuses, because a record written under an owner this routine chose would be
  -- the auto-vivified customer account defect in a new place.
  v_effect := public.fn_phase_d_effect_produce(
    jsonb_build_object(
      'step_run_id', v_step_run, 'idempotency_key', v_idem, 'actor_role_id', v_actor,
      'execution_context', v_ctx)
    || jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
      'business_key', p_input->>'business_key',
      'owner_ref',    p_input->>'owner_ref',
      -- H01 (4). The caller's stated state, else the state the committed catalogue declares for
      -- THIS step (EFFECT_PAYLOAD key 'state', step-scoped, fixture context only), else none -- and
      -- none means the writer keeps the row's state or takes the relation's default. Never 'open'.
      'state',        coalesce(p_input->>'effect_state',
                               (select fi.value #>> '{}'
                                  from public.fn_phase_d_fixture_input(v_step_run, 'EFFECT_PAYLOAD', 'state') fi)),
      'state_before', p_input->>'state_before',
      'trace_id',     p_input->>'trace_id'))
    -- F16. THE CONTENT THE OBJECT'S OWN RELATION DEMANDS, from the committed catalogue.
    --
    -- pd_effect_payload_incomplete is the deepest refusal in the drive: the step has passed every
    -- rule and gate, the dispatch has derived a business key and an owner, and the write to the
    -- object's canonical relation fails on a NOT NULL column -- opportunity.kind, org_tasks.title,
    -- department_objective.objective, content_drafts.body. The builder closure of 2026-08-20
    -- recorded 18 of 56 business objects in that state and reported it as a Phase E boundary,
    -- correctly, because a deterministic handler must not invent a title or an amount.
    --
    -- The founder's ruling of 21 Aug 2026 supplies them instead, from a committed catalogue, and
    -- this is where they arrive. The handler still invents nothing: the value comes from
    -- fn_phase_d_fixture_effect_payload, which reads the columns the RELATION demands and the
    -- values the CATALOGUE holds, and which returns an empty object in production.
    --
    -- The order is caller, then capability result, then catalogue, and the catalogue is last so it
    -- can only fill what nothing else filled.
    || jsonb_build_object('payload',
         public.fn_phase_d_fixture_effect_payload(v_step_run)
         || coalesce(p_input->'effect_payload', v_inputs)
         || case when v_cap is null then '{}'::jsonb
                 else coalesce(v_cap->'payload','{}'::jsonb) end
         -- H01 (1). THE RECORDED REVIEW, LAST, FOR A REVIEW_VERDICT EFFECT. F34 read it into the
         -- output and never into the payload, and BR-002 is judged on the payload. The sealed
         -- verdict and the stamped reviewer outrank the catalogue and any caller, so they close
         -- the concatenation. Absent, nothing is added and fn_phase_d_effect_produce still refuses.
         || case when ec.expected_effect_type = 'REVIEW_VERDICT'
                 then jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
                        'verdict',          v_review->>'verdict',
                        'reviewer_role_id', v_review->>'reviewer_role_id'))
                 else '{}'::jsonb end
         -- H01 (3). WHO DECIDED AND WHEN, FOR A DECISION STEP. The decider is the accountable role
         -- of the deciding step run, read off the kernel's row; the time is now(). A write map that
         -- carries neither key ignores both.
         || case when b.handler_class = 'DECISION_HANDLER'
                 then jsonb_build_object('decided_by', v_actor, 'decided_at', now())
                 else '{}'::jsonb end));

  v_output := v_output || jsonb_build_object('business_effect', jsonb_build_object(
    'effect_type', v_effect->>'effect_type',
    'effect_object_id', v_effect->'effect_object_id',
    'result_reference', v_effect->>'result_reference',
    'effect_id', v_effect->'effect_id',
    'provider_mode', v_effect->>'provider_mode',
    'replay', v_effect->'replay'));

  -- ---- 7. HAND TO THE FROZEN KERNEL --------------------------------------------------------
  -- Everything from here — idempotency, locks, authority, gates, the task state machine,
  -- progression, handoffs, run state and events — belongs to fn_kernel_step_complete and is not
  -- reimplemented. A handler that wrote any of it would be the parallel engine the spec forbids.
  v_result := public.fn_kernel_step_complete(jsonb_build_object(
    'step_run_id', v_step_run, 'actor_role_id', v_actor, 'outcome', 'pass',
    'idempotency_key', v_idem, 'inputs', v_inputs, 'output', v_output,
    'evidence_ref', format('phase_d:%s:%s:effect=%s',
                           b.handler_id, v_step_run, coalesce(v_effect->>'result_reference','none')),
    'correlation_id', p_input->>'correlation_id',
    'causation_id', coalesce(p_input->>'causation_id', 'phase_d_handler:' || b.handler_id)));

  return v_result || jsonb_build_object(
    'phase_d', jsonb_build_object(
      'handler_id', b.handler_id, 'handler_version', b.handler_version,
      'handler_class', b.handler_class, 'execution_context', v_ctx,
      'input_schema_id', b.input_schema_id, 'output_schema_id', b.output_schema_id,
      'rules_in_scope', cardinality(b.rule_ids),
      'rules_evaluated', v_evaluated, 'rules_not_applicable', v_skipped,
      'rules_enforced_count', (select count(*) from jsonb_array_elements(v_evaluated) e2
                                where (e2->>'enforced')::boolean),
      'rules_outstanding_count', (select count(*) from jsonb_array_elements(v_evaluated) e2
                                   where not (e2->>'enforced')::boolean),
      'gates_in_scope', cardinality(b.gate_ids), 'gates_evaluated', v_gates,
      'capability_dependency', b.capability_dependency,
      'provider_dependency', b.provider_dependency,
      'external_effect_policy', b.external_effect_policy,
      'expected_effect_type', ec.expected_effect_type,
      'implementation_depth', ec.implementation_depth,
      'business_effect', v_effect));
end
fn_phase_d_gate_applies:
declare g public.phase_b_gate%rowtype; s public.phase_b_workflow_step%rowtype;
        v_subject text; v_producer text; v_predicate text;   -- K07
begin
  select * into g from public.phase_b_gate where gate_id = p_gate_id;
  if not found then applies := false; why := format('unknown gate %s', p_gate_id); return next; return; end if;
  select * into s from public.phase_b_workflow_step where step_id = p_step_id;
  if not found then applies := false; why := format('unknown step %s', p_step_id); return next; return; end if;

  if upper(g.workflow_scope) <> 'ALL'
     and not (s.workflow_id = any (string_to_array(replace(g.workflow_scope,' ',''), ';'))) then
    applies := false;
    why := format('%s is scoped to %s and %s is in %s', g.gate_id, g.workflow_scope, p_step_id, s.workflow_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  if p_gate_id = 'GATE-004' and coalesce(btrim(s.independent_reviewer_role_id),'') = '' then
    applies := false;
    why := format('GATE-004 governs the independence of a named reviewer and %s names none', p_step_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  if p_gate_id = 'GATE-005' and lower(coalesce(btrim(s.founder_gate),'none')) = 'none' then
    applies := false;
    why := format('GATE-005 governs a founder-reserved decision and %s declares founder_gate none', p_step_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  -- GATE-020 — "Refund authority and idempotency", pass_result "Execute once". It guards the money
  -- movement, and the frozen registry names that step by carrying a founder_gate on it and on no
  -- other step of W17: "Money movement beyond approved policy requires founder approval." Demanding
  -- an approved case decision at the step that OPENS the case is a condition the workflow itself is
  -- what satisfies, four steps later. Refund authority is unaffected: it is held by the trigger
  -- z00_refund_founder_decision_only on public.refunds, which raises unless an approved refund was
  -- decided by an active founder identity, on every path, workflow or not.
  -- D28. GATE-015 — "No existing assignment for same supplier, inquiry version and dispatch scope."
  --
  -- It prevents a DUPLICATE dispatch, so it governs every step up to AND INCLUDING the one that
  -- creates the assignment. That is where a duplicate is actually stopped. A step running AFTER the
  -- creating step in the same workflow is premised on the assignment EXISTING: W12-S07 is "Create
  -- exactly one notification per assignment", and refusing it because an assignment exists refuses
