  -- the workflow for having done its own job one step earlier.
  --
  -- THIS IS NOT THE WHOLE-WORKFLOW EXEMPTION THAT WAS TRIED AS D17 AND DISCARDED. GATE-015 is
  -- scoped to W12 alone, so exempting W12 would leave it governing nothing — the session brief says
  -- exactly that and it is right. This exempts only the steps that come after the assignment has
  -- been legitimately created, and the gate still governs W12-S01 through S06, the creating step
  -- included. Its purpose survives intact.
  --
  -- THE PRODUCING STEP IS DERIVED, NEVER NAMED HERE. The object the gate measures is resolved by
  -- matching the gate contract's own evidence_source against the canonical relation of the object,
  -- and the producing step is then read from phase_d_step_effect. Renaming a step or moving the
  -- effect moves this with it.
  --
  -- The same shape as the GATE-020 refinement immediately below, which the estate already accepted:
  -- a condition that the workflow itself is what satisfies, demanded before the workflow satisfies it.
  if p_gate_id = 'GATE-015'
     and exists (
       select 1
         from public.phase_d_step_effect e
         join public.phase_d_business_object_binding bb on bb.object_id = e.effect_object_id
         join public.phase_d_gate_contract gc on gc.gate_id = p_gate_id
        where e.workflow_id = s.workflow_id
          and e.step_id < p_step_id
          and bb.canonical_relation is not null
          and gc.evidence_source ilike '%' || bb.canonical_relation || '%')
  then
    applies := false;
    why := format('GATE-015 stops a DUPLICATE dispatch, so it governs up to and including the step that creates the assignment; %s runs after it and is premised on the assignment existing', p_step_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  if p_gate_id = 'GATE-020' and lower(coalesce(btrim(s.founder_gate),'none')) = 'none' then
    applies := false;
    why := format('GATE-020 guards the execution of an approved financial action; %s declares founder_gate none and is not the money-movement step', p_step_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  if p_gate_id = 'GATE-007'
     and not exists (select 1 from public.phase_b_handoff h where h.from_step_id = p_step_id) then
    applies := false;
    why := format('GATE-007 governs a handoff packet and %s opens no handoff', p_step_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  if p_gate_id = 'GATE-008' and not coalesce(s.is_closure_step, false) then
    applies := false;
    why := format('GATE-008 is a closure gate and %s is not the closure step', p_step_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  -- G03. A GATE THAT DEMANDS A REVIEWER'S VERDICT AT A STEP THAT RUNS BEFORE ANY REVIEW.
  --
  -- Measured, on the three gates whose evidence_keys name reviewer_role_id:
  --
  --   GATE-021 "Marketing artifact approval", pass_result "Publish approved revision.", scope W03;W20
  --            refused W03-S01 "Set acquisition objective" and W20-S01 "Define content objective
  --            and hypothesis" for want of the reviewer of a final asset the workflow has not yet
  --            produced. W03 first reviews at S06; W20 at S04.
  --   GATE-026 "Knowledge validation", pass_result "Publish runtime-eligible version.", scope W26
  --            refused W26-S01 "Open knowledge gap or change", an INTAKE step. W26 first reviews
  --            at S05.
  --
  -- Both are the shape this function already refines twice. GATE-020 was narrowed because it
  -- demanded an approved case decision at the step that OPENS the case; GATE-015 because it
  -- refused a workflow for having done its own job one step earlier. This is the same sentence:
  -- a condition that the workflow itself is what satisfies, demanded before the workflow
  -- satisfies it.
  --
  -- NOTHING IS WEAKENED. The gate still applies from the workflow's first review step to its last
  -- step, which is where the artifact exists, where the review happens, and where publication is
  -- decided -- W03-S06..S09, W20-S04..S09, W26-S05..S09. A step at or after that point with no
  -- recorded reviewer still refuses.
  --
  -- NO GATE AND NO STEP IS NAMED. The condition is derived: the gate's own evidence_keys carry
  -- reviewer_role_id, and the frozen registry says which of this workflow's steps are reviews.
  -- A workflow with no review step at all is untouched -- there is no point before which to be
  -- early -- and GATE-004 keeps its own, narrower, earlier exemption.
  if exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_gate_contract gc
              where gc.gate_id = p_gate_id
                and 'reviewer_role_id' = any(gc.evidence_keys))
     and p_step_id < (select min(rs.step_id) from public.phase_b_workflow_step rs
                       where rs.workflow_id = s.workflow_id and rs.step_type = 'review')
  then
    applies := false;
    why := format('%s requires an independent reviewer''s verdict and %s runs before %s, the first review step of %s; the review this gate reads is produced by the workflow itself, later',
                  p_gate_id, p_step_id,
                  (select min(rs.step_id) from public.phase_b_workflow_step rs
                    where rs.workflow_id = s.workflow_id and rs.step_type = 'review'),
                  s.workflow_id);
    return next; return;
  end if;

  -- K07. THE GENERAL RULE THE FOUR NARROWINGS ABOVE ARE INSTANCES OF: a gate does not govern a
  -- step that runs BEFORE the step which produces the gate's own subject. GATE-013 asked W08-S01 --
  -- the first step of the workflow whose purpose is to build the supplier-safe package -- to
  -- already name that package.
  --
  -- IT IS A BEFORE-RULE, NOT A WHOLE-WORKFLOW EXEMPTION. The gate still applies at the producing
  -- step and at every step after it, so a gate scoped to one workflow still governs it. Nothing is
  -- named here: the subject is the gate contract's own evidence key matched against
  -- public.phase_d_fixture_stage.contributes_ref -- the same derivation fn_phase_d_rule_applies
  -- uses -- and the producing step is read from public.phase_d_step_effect.
  select st.object_id, gc.predicate_kind into v_subject, v_predicate
    from public.phase_d_gate_contract gc
    join public.phase_d_fixture_stage st on st.contributes_ref = any(gc.evidence_keys)
   where gc.gate_id = p_gate_id
   limit 1;
  if v_subject is not null then
    select min(x.step_id) into v_producer
      from public.phase_d_step_effect x
     where x.workflow_id = s.workflow_id and x.effect_object_id = v_subject;
    if v_producer is not null
       and (p_step_id < v_producer
            -- AT the producing step too, but only where the gate's test is the PRESENCE of the
            -- subject's identity. A MEASURED gate is untouched: GATE-015 exists to judge the
            -- creating step, and exempting it there would leave it governing nothing.
            or (p_step_id = v_producer and v_predicate = 'EVIDENCE_REQUIRED')) then
      applies := false;
      why := format('%s judges %s and %s runs %s %s, the step of %s that produces it; the gate '
                 || 'governs its use %s, not before it exists',
                    p_gate_id, v_subject, p_step_id,
                    case when p_step_id = v_producer then 'at' else 'before' end,
                    v_producer, s.workflow_id,
                    case when v_predicate = 'EVIDENCE_REQUIRED'
                         then 'after the producing step' else 'from the producing step onward' end);
      return next; return;
    end if;
  end if;

  applies := true;
  why := format('%s (%s, scope %s) applies to %s', g.gate_id, g.gate_type, g.workflow_scope, p_step_id);
  return next;
end
fn_phase_d_fixture_value:
-- A fixture value of the right SHAPE for a column, and visibly a fixture. Nothing here is a
  -- plausible-looking real value: a probe row that reads as production data is how demo rows end up
  -- being counted as customers.
  select case
    when p_ftype in ('jsonb','json')                     then jsonb_build_object('fixture', p_label)
    when p_tcat = 'A'                                    then jsonb_build_array('ZZ DEMO')
    when p_ftype = 'uuid'                                then to_jsonb(gen_random_uuid()::text)
    when p_ftype like '%timestamp%'                      then to_jsonb(now()::text)
    when p_ftype = 'boolean'                             then to_jsonb(false)
    when p_ftype in ('numeric','integer','bigint','smallint','double precision','real')
                                                         then to_jsonb(1)
    when p_ftype like '%email%'                          then to_jsonb('zz-phase-d-' || p_label || '@example.invalid')
    else to_jsonb('ZZ DEMO — ' || p_label)
  end;
fn_phase_d_handoff_state:
with live as (select count(*) n from public.phase_b_handoff),
       con  as (select count(*) n from public.phase_d_handoff_contract)
  select 'effective_handoffs_contracted', (select n::text from live),
         (select n::text from con), (select n from con) = (select n from live)
  union all
  select 'contracts_with_no_live_handoff', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_contract c
           where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_b_handoff h where h.handoff_id = c.handoff_id)),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_handoff_contract c
                      where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_b_handoff h
                                         where h.handoff_id = c.handoff_id))
  union all
  select 'contracts_whose_packet_is_only_boilerplate', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_contract
           where distinguishing_key in ('source_business_object_version','acceptance_evidence',
                                        'unresolved_blockers','requested_next_action')),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_handoff_contract
                      where distinguishing_key in ('source_business_object_version','acceptance_evidence',
                                                   'unresolved_blockers','requested_next_action'))
  union all
  select 'distinct_distinguishing_keys', (select n::text from live),
         (select count(distinct distinguishing_key)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_contract),
         (select count(distinct distinguishing_key) from public.phase_d_handoff_contract)
           = (select n from live)
  union all
  select 'contracts_drifted_from_the_frozen_packet', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_contract c
            join public.phase_b_handoff h on h.handoff_id = c.handoff_id
           where c.required_packet_sha256
                 <> encode(sha256(convert_to(h.required_packet,'UTF8')),'hex')),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_handoff_contract c
                       join public.phase_b_handoff h on h.handoff_id = c.handoff_id
                      where c.required_packet_sha256
                            <> encode(sha256(convert_to(h.required_packet,'UTF8')),'hex'))
  union all
  select 'contracts_with_no_parsed_sla_target', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_contract where sla_target is null),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_handoff_contract where sla_target is null)
  union all
  select 'contracts_where_accountability_does_not_move', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_contract
           where accountable_before_accept = accountable_after_accept),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_handoff_contract
                      where accountable_before_accept = accountable_after_accept)
  union all
  select 'acceptances_that_opened_no_step_run', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_acceptance
           where outcome = 'accepted' and opened_step_run_id is null),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_handoff_acceptance
                      where outcome = 'accepted' and opened_step_run_id is null)
  union all
  select 'handoff_runs_with_two_phase_d_decisions', '0',
         (select coalesce(count(*),0)::text from (
            select handoff_run_id from public.phase_d_handoff_acceptance
             group by handoff_run_id having count(*) > 1) x),
         not exists (select 1 from (
            select handoff_run_id from public.phase_d_handoff_acceptance
             group by handoff_run_id having count(*) > 1) x)
  union all
  select 'cancelled_runs_with_an_open_handoff', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_c_workflow_run r
           where r.state = 'cancelled'
             and exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_handoff_run hr
                          where hr.run_id = r.run_id and hr.status = 'open')),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_workflow_run r
                      where r.state = 'cancelled'
                        and exists (select 1 from public.phase_c_handoff_run hr
                                     where hr.run_id = r.run_id and hr.status = 'open'))
  union all
  -- DISCLOSED. The frozen kernel exposes fn_kernel_handoff_accept and no rejection routine, and
  -- fn_phase_c_handoff_decide is a kernel-internal primitive Phase D may not call. So a Phase D
  -- rejection is durable and refuses to advance the workflow, and the kernel-side handoff run stays
  -- open. Counting it here is the disclosure; closing it is a Phase C change request.
  select 'phase_d_rejections_the_kernel_still_shows_open', 'informational — no kernel rejection door',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_handoff_acceptance a
            join public.phase_c_handoff_run h on h.handoff_run_id = a.handoff_run_id
           where a.outcome = 'rejected' and h.status = 'open'), true;
fn_phase_d_fixture_state:
select 'fixture_stages_declared', '>= 20',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_fixture_stage),
         (select count(*) from public.phase_d_fixture_stage) >= 20
  union all
  select 'stages_naming_an_unbound_object', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s
           where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_business_object_binding b
                              where b.object_id = s.object_id)),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s
                      where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_business_object_binding b
                                         where b.object_id = s.object_id))
  union all
  select 'stages_requiring_a_stage_that_does_not_exist', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s, unnest(s.requires_stages) r
           where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_fixture_stage p where p.stage_key = r)),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s, unnest(s.requires_stages) r
                      where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_fixture_stage p
                                         where p.stage_key = r))
  union all
  select 'stages_depending_on_a_later_stage', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s, unnest(s.requires_stages) r
            join public.phase_d_fixture_stage p on p.stage_key = r
           where p.stage_no >= s.stage_no),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s, unnest(s.requires_stages) r
                       join public.phase_d_fixture_stage p on p.stage_key = r
                      where p.stage_no >= s.stage_no)
  union all
  select 'supplier_account_can_write_verified', 'true',
         (select (column_map ? 'verified')::text from public.phase_d_object_write_map
           where object_id = 'supplier_account'),
         (select column_map ? 'verified' from public.phase_d_object_write_map
           where object_id = 'supplier_account')
  union all
  -- REPLACES `inquiry_can_write_rfq_ready`. rfq_ready is derived by trg_rfq_complete, so mapping it
  -- is a promise the map cannot keep; what the writer must cover is the FACTS fn_rfq_score reads.
  select 'inquiry_writer_covers_the_readiness_facts', 'emirate, scope_type, budget, trades mapped',
         (select string_agg(k, ', ' order by k) from unnest(array['emirate','scope_type','budget','trades']) k
           where (select column_map ? k from public.phase_d_object_write_map where object_id='inquiry')),
         (select column_map ?& array['emirate','scope_type','budget','trades']
            from public.phase_d_object_write_map where object_id = 'inquiry')
  union all
  select 'inquiry_writer_maps_a_derived_column', '0',
         (select (column_map ? 'rfq_ready')::int::text from public.phase_d_object_write_map
           where object_id = 'inquiry'),
         not (select column_map ? 'rfq_ready' from public.phase_d_object_write_map
               where object_id = 'inquiry')
  union all
  select 'fixture_rows_surviving_in_business_tables', '0',
         (select coalesce(sum(surviving_rows),0)::text from public.fn_phase_d_fixture_residue()),
         coalesce((select sum(surviving_rows) from public.fn_phase_d_fixture_residue()), 0) = 0
  union all
  select 'fixture_stage_targeting_public_notifications', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s
            join public.phase_d_business_object_binding b on b.object_id = s.object_id
           where b.canonical_relation = 'public.notifications'),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_fixture_stage s
                       join public.phase_d_business_object_binding b on b.object_id = s.object_id
                      where b.canonical_relation = 'public.notifications')
  union all
  select 'canonical_object_writes_that_can_reach_a_notification_trigger', 'informational',
         (select count(*)::text from public.fn_phase_d_outbound_exposure()), true
  union all
  select 'fixture_identities_carrying_a_contact_detail', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.customers c
           where c.full_name like 'ZZ DEMO — %'
             and (coalesce(c.email,'') <> '' or coalesce(c.phone,'') <> '')),
         not exists (select 1 from public.customers c
                      where c.full_name like 'ZZ DEMO — %'
                        and (coalesce(c.email,'') <> '' or coalesce(c.phone,'') <> ''));
fn_phase_d_outbound_exposure:
-- Which write-map target relations carry a trigger whose function body inserts into the outbound
  -- notification table. This reads the TRIGGER BODY, which is where the row actually comes from —
  -- a check that read the write map would never see it, and that is how this stayed invisible.
  select wm.target_relation,
         t.tgname,
         true,
         wm.object_id
    from public.phase_d_object_write_map wm
    join pg_trigger t on t.tgrelid = wm.target_relation::regclass and not t.tgisinternal
    join pg_proc  p on p.oid = t.tgfoid
   where p.prosrc ~* 'insert\s+into\s+(public\.)?notifications'
   order by 1, 2;
fn_phase_d_fixture_inquiry_payload:
-- The generic six, and the three keys public.category_specs marks required for `general`
  -- (describe, property, scope) — read from the table, not guessed. The verdict is still
  -- fn_rfq_score's; this supplies facts, not a readiness flag.
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'summary',   format('ZZ DEMO — %s inquiry', p_label),
    'spec',      jsonb_build_object(
                   'describe','ZZ DEMO fixture requirement described in full: supply and installation of a general works package to the stated scope and quantities.',
                   'property','Commercial fit-out, Dubai',
                   'scope','ZZ DEMO fixture scope of works with sufficient descriptive detail for the readiness scorer to register scope_detail',
                   'quantity','1 lot'),
    'category',  'general',
    'emirate',   'Dubai',
    'scope_type','supply_and_install',
    'budget',    'AED 100,000 - 200,000',
    'trades',    '["general"]'::jsonb);
fn_phase_d_case_state:
with steps as (select count(*) n from public.phase_b_workflow_step),
       res   as (select count(*) n from public.phase_d_step_case_result)
  -- The denominator is derived, never typed: if the frozen step count moves, this reports it.
  select 'per_step_cases_recorded', ((select n from steps) * 7)::text,
         (select n::text from res), (select n from res) = (select n from steps) * 7
  union all
  select 'steps_with_fewer_than_seven_cases', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from (
            select step_id from public.phase_d_step_case_result
             group by step_id having count(*) <> 7) x),
         not exists (select 1 from (
            select step_id from public.phase_d_step_case_result
             group by step_id having count(*) <> 7) x)
  union all
  select 'cases_failing', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_step_case_result where not passed),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_step_case_result where not passed)
  union all
  -- A negative case that reports no machine code is a prose assertion.
  select 'negative_cases_with_no_refusal_code', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_step_case_result
           where case_kind <> 'positive' and passed and coalesce(refused_with,'') in ('','(none)')),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_step_case_result
                      where case_kind <> 'positive' and passed
                        and coalesce(refused_with,'') in ('','(none)'))
  union all
  select 'cases_decided_at_the_step_contract', 'informational',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_step_case_result
           where decided_at = 'step_contract'), true
  union all
  select 'cases_decided_at_a_shared_boundary', 'informational',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_step_case_result
           where decided_at in ('executor_boundary','kernel_boundary','structural_constraint')), true;
fn_phase_d_event_state:
with ev as (select count(*) n from public.phase_b_event),
       rc as (select count(*) n from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation),
       -- D45. The 54 self-loops split cleanly, and the split is what makes one half a defect and the
       -- other half the frozen graph. `sl` resolves each self-looping event to the step it belongs
       -- to and to that step's declared successor, from the frozen registry only.
       sl as (
         -- phase_d_event_reconciliation has no step_id column. The step is in the event id, and it
         -- parses for all 54 with nothing left over — measured, not assumed:
         -- no_step_parsed 0, no_step_row 0, 15 end the workflow, 39 same owner, 0 different owner.
         select r.event_id, r.producer,
                s.step_id, s.next_step_if_pass,
                (select s2.accountable_role_id from public.phase_b_workflow_step s2
                  where s2.step_id = s.next_step_if_pass) as successor_owner
           from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation r
           join public.phase_b_workflow_step s
             on s.step_id = substring(r.event_id from 'EV-(W[0-9]+-S[0-9]+)')
          where r.is_self_loop
       )
  select 'events_reconciled', (select n::text from ev), (select n::text from rc),
         (select n from rc) = (select n from ev)
  union all
  select 'reconciliations_with_no_frozen_event', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation r
           where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_b_event e where e.event_id = r.event_id)),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation r
                      where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_b_event e
                                         where e.event_id = r.event_id))
  union all
  select 'events_with_no_factual_state_change', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
           where factual_state_change = '(the frozen registry states no trigger)'),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
                      where factual_state_change = '(the frozen registry states no trigger)')
  union all
  -- D45. WAS: 'event_self_loops', expected 0, measured 54 — every one of them legitimate.
  -- The expectation is unchanged; the subject is the case that would be a defect.
  select 'self_loop_after_handing_the_work_on', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from sl
           where coalesce(next_step_if_pass,'') not in ('','WORKFLOW_COMPLETE')
             and successor_owner is not null
             and successor_owner is distinct from producer),
         not exists (select 1 from sl
                      where coalesce(next_step_if_pass,'') not in ('','WORKFLOW_COMPLETE')
                        and successor_owner is not null
                        and successor_owner is distinct from producer)
  union all
  -- and the 54 stay visible, with the two components that account for all of them, so narrowing the
  -- check above hides nothing.
  select 'event_self_loops_total', 'informational — the frozen graph, not a defect',
         (select count(*)::text from sl) || ' (' ||
         (select count(*)::text from sl where coalesce(next_step_if_pass,'') in ('','WORKFLOW_COMPLETE'))
         || ' end the workflow, ' ||
         (select count(*)::text from sl where coalesce(next_step_if_pass,'') not in ('','WORKFLOW_COMPLETE')
                                          and successor_owner is not distinct from producer)
         || ' hand to a successor the same role owns)', true
  union all
  select 'self_loops_whose_successor_step_does_not_resolve', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from sl
           where coalesce(next_step_if_pass,'') not in ('','WORKFLOW_COMPLETE')
             and successor_owner is null),
         not exists (select 1 from sl
                      where coalesce(next_step_if_pass,'') not in ('','WORKFLOW_COMPLETE')
                        and successor_owner is null)
  union all
  -- THE CHECK THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. A row may not say it was observed unless the outbox says so.
  select 'registry_only_events_reported_runtime_observed', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
           where runtime_observation = 'OBSERVED_IN_OUTBOX' and emissions_observed = 0),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
                      where runtime_observation = 'OBSERVED_IN_OUTBOX' and emissions_observed = 0)
  union all
  select 'events_with_no_registered_cancellation_writer', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
           where cancellation_behaviour = 'NO REGISTERED CANCELLATION WRITER'),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
                      where cancellation_behaviour = 'NO REGISTERED CANCELLATION WRITER')
  union all
  select 'events_with_no_dedupe_key', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
           where coalesce(btrim(dedupe_key),'') = ''),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
                      where coalesce(btrim(dedupe_key),'') = '')
  union all
  -- DISCLOSED, AND THE WHOLE POINT. The gap between what the structure claims and what has happened
  -- is a number the founder can see rather than a word that hides it. It is NOT ratcheted to zero:
  -- closing it means running the business automation that is deliberately held.
  select 'events_structurally_connected_but_never_observed', 'informational — automation is held',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
           where structural_status = 'CONNECTED' and runtime_observation = 'NEVER_OBSERVED'), true
  union all
  select 'events_observed_at_runtime', 'informational',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_event_reconciliation
           where runtime_observation = 'OBSERVED_IN_OUTBOX'), true;
fn_phase_d_adapter_state:
select 'external_effect_steps', '12',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_step_effect
           where expected_effect_type = 'EXTERNAL_EFFECT_INTENT'),
         (select count(*) from public.phase_d_step_effect
           where expected_effect_type = 'EXTERNAL_EFFECT_INTENT') = 12
  union all
  -- THE CHECK THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. No step may claim a built adapter while any of the fourteen
  -- fields is absent. It is not a ratchet: the moment all fourteen are PRESENT this permits
  -- READY_DISABLED again, and until then it forbids it.
  select 'steps_claiming_a_built_adapter_while_a_field_is_absent', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_step_effect
           where implementation_depth = 'EXTERNAL_ADAPTER_READY_DISABLED'
             and exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_external_adapter_field
                          where state <> 'PRESENT')),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_step_effect
                      where implementation_depth = 'EXTERNAL_ADAPTER_READY_DISABLED'
                        and exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_external_adapter_field
                                     where state <> 'PRESENT'))
  union all
  select 'adapter_contract_fields_reconciled', '14',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_external_adapter_field),
         (select count(*) from public.phase_d_external_adapter_field) = 14
  union all
  select 'adapter_contract_fields_present', 'informational',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_external_adapter_field where state='PRESENT'), true
  union all
  select 'adapter_contract_fields_absent_or_partial', 'informational — D9 of the brief is not started',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_external_adapter_field where state<>'PRESENT'), true
  union all
  -- provider_mode must have no way to become a send.
  select 'effect_ledger_rows_in_a_live_provider_mode', '0',
         (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_effect_ledger where provider_mode = 'live'),
         not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_effect_ledger where provider_mode = 'live');
fn_phase_d_outbound_state:
with pd_rel as (
  select distinct b.canonical_relation as relation
    from public.phase_d_business_object_binding b
   where b.relation_kind = 'EXISTING_TABLE'
),
scanned as (
  select 'public.' || c.relname as relation, tg.tgname as trigger_name, p.proname as function_name,
         pg_get_triggerdef(tg.oid) as triggerdef
    from pg_trigger tg
    join pg_proc  p on p.oid = tg.tgfoid
    join pg_class c on c.oid = tg.tgrelid
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
   where not tg.tgisinternal and n.nspname = 'public'
     and p.prosrc ~* 'net\.http_(post|get)'
     and ('public.' || c.relname) in (select relation from pd_rel)
),
sup as (select * from public.phase_d_outbound_door where disposition = 'SUPPRESSED_BY_ITS_OWN_GUARD'),
unr as (select * from public.phase_d_outbound_door where disposition = 'NOT_REACHED_BY_ANY_PHASE_D_WRITE_MAP')

-- 1. THE DENOMINATOR. Every outbound trigger the live scan finds on a Phase D canonical relation
--    must be registered. A new one appearing turns this red instead of quietly re-opening the door.
select 'every_outbound_trigger_on_a_phase_d_relation_is_registered',
       (select count(*)::text from scanned),
       (select count(*)::text from scanned s
         join public.phase_d_outbound_door d
           on d.relation = s.relation and d.trigger_name = s.trigger_name),
       case when (select count(*) from scanned)
               = (select count(*) from scanned s join public.phase_d_outbound_door d
                    on d.relation = s.relation and d.trigger_name = s.trigger_name)
            then 'GREEN' else 'RED' end,
       coalesce((select string_agg(s.relation || '.' || s.trigger_name, ', ')
                   from scanned s
                  where not exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_outbound_door d
                                     where d.relation = s.relation and d.trigger_name = s.trigger_name)),
                'every scanned outbound trigger is registered')

union all
select 'no_registered_door_names_a_trigger_that_does_not_exist',
       '0',
       (select count(*)::text from public.phase_d_outbound_door d
         where not exists (select 1 from scanned s
                            where s.relation = d.relation and s.trigger_name = d.trigger_name)),
       case when exists (select 1 from public.phase_d_outbound_door d
                          where not exists (select 1 from scanned s
                                             where s.relation = d.relation and s.trigger_name = d.trigger_name))
            then 'RED' else 'GREEN' end,
       'a registry row for a trigger that is gone would suppress a column for no reason'

-- 2. SUPPRESSED DOORS. The guard column must be real and must be declared in the write map, or the
--    writer cannot set it and the suppression is a comment rather than a mechanism.
union all
select 'every_guard_column_exists_on_its_relation',
       (select count(*)::text from sup),
       (select count(*)::text from sup d
         join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = d.relation::regclass
                            and a.attname = d.guard_column and a.attnum > 0 and not a.attisdropped),
       case when (select count(*) from sup)
               = (select count(*) from sup d
                    join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = d.relation::regclass
                                       and a.attname = d.guard_column and a.attnum > 0 and not a.attisdropped)
            then 'GREEN' else 'RED' end,
       'a guard column the relation does not have cannot suppress anything'

union all
select 'every_guard_column_is_declared_in_the_write_map',
       (select count(*)::text from sup),
       (select count(*)::text
          from sup d
          join public.phase_d_object_write_map wm on wm.target_relation = d.relation
         where wm.column_map ? d.guard_column),
       case when (select count(*) from sup)
               = (select count(*) from sup d
                    join public.phase_d_object_write_map wm on wm.target_relation = d.relation
                   where wm.column_map ? d.guard_column)
            then 'GREEN' else 'RED' end,
       'the writer may only touch a column the map declares; a suppression behind the map''s back is the defect this check exists for'

union all
select 'suppression_expression_is_evaluated_not_a_literal',
       (select count(*)::text from sup),
       (select count(*)::text from sup d where d.suppression_sql ~ '^[a-z_]+\('),
       case when (select count(*) from sup)
               = (select count(*) from sup d where d.suppression_sql ~ '^[a-z_]+\(')
            then 'GREEN' else 'RED' end,
       'each suppression is a function call the writer evaluates at write time, so now() is the write''s own clock'

-- 3. UNREACHABLE DOORS. "No Phase D write can reach this" is a claim, and these two checks are what
--    make it checkable. The named column must actually appear in the trigger's own definition, and
--    it must NOT be declared in the relation's write map. Add that column to a write map and this
--    goes red on the next board run rather than silently opening a door.
union all
select 'every_unreachable_reason_names_a_column_its_trigger_actually_tests',
       (select count(*)::text from unr),
       (select count(*)::text from unr d join scanned s
          on s.relation = d.relation and s.trigger_name = d.trigger_name
         where s.triggerdef ilike '%' || d.unreachable_because_column || '%'),
       case when (select count(*) from unr)
               = (select count(*) from unr d join scanned s

fn_phase_d_object_identity_state:
with wm as (select * from public.phase_d_object_write_map where operation = 'UPSERT_STATE'),
uq as (
  select 'public.' || t.relname as rel, ic.relname as idx_name,
         array_agg(a.attname::text order by a.attnum) as cols
    from pg_index i
    join pg_class ic on ic.oid = i.indexrelid
    join pg_class t  on t.oid  = i.indrelid
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace and n.nspname = 'public'
    join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = i.indrelid and a.attnum = any(i.indkey)
   where i.indisunique
   group by 1, 2
),
resolvable as (
  select wm.object_id,
         -- pass 1: the key column is mapped, so the writer can probe the value it will write
         (wm.column_map ? wm.key_column) as by_key_column,
         -- pass 2: some other unique index is entirely covered by the map
         exists (select 1 from uq
                  where uq.rel = wm.target_relation
                    and uq.cols <> array[wm.key_column]
                    and (select bool_and(wm.column_map ? c) from unnest(uq.cols) c)) as by_natural_key
    from wm
)
select 'every_upsert_state_map_can_resolve_an_identity',
       (select count(*)::text from resolvable),
       (select count(*)::text from resolvable where by_key_column or by_natural_key),
       case when exists (select 1 from resolvable where not (by_key_column or by_natural_key))
            then 'RED' else 'GREEN' end,
       coalesce((select string_agg(object_id, ', ' order by object_id) from resolvable
                  where not (by_key_column or by_natural_key)),
                'every UPSERT_STATE map resolves an identity')
       || ' — an UPSERT_STATE that resolves no identity can only ever INSERT, so its second write is'
       || ' a duplicate row rather than a state move. Owner: Phase D. Closing it needs an identity'
       || ' the business declares, not one a harness invents.'

union all

fn_phase_d_reference_fold_state:
with declared as (

  -- phase_d_step_effect.effect_relation is a REGISTRY name and for a store-backed object that is
  -- the view, public.v_obj_<object>. The DRIVER compares against the physical table, because
  -- fn_phase_d_object_write returns public.phase_d_object_record:record_id=N at runtime. Both are
  -- correct in their own place; putting the runtime name into the registry comparison reported 40
  -- healthy steps as mismatched, including every step of W02, W06, W08, W10 and W11 — five
  -- workflows that CLOSE. Two vocabularies for one relation, which is the same trap this file
  -- exists to close, met once more while writing the check for it.
  select e.step_id, e.workflow_id, e.effect_object_id,
         b.canonical_relation as object_relation,
         e.effect_relation
    from public.phase_d_step_effect e
    join public.phase_d_business_object_binding b on b.object_id = e.effect_object_id
   where e.effect_object_id is not null
),
mismatch as (
  select * from declared
   where effect_relation is not null

     and effect_relation is distinct from object_relation
)

                            and p.prosrc like '%v_produced_rel is distinct from v_object_rel%')
