fn_phase_d_founder_authority_fixture:
declare
  v_run   bigint := public.fn_phase_d_fixture_context();
  v_label text   := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'label','')),'');
  v_id    bigint;
  v_msg   bigint;
  v_text  text;
  v_trace bigint;   -- G19: the root trace the guard requires before the command may move
begin
  if v_run is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_founder_authority_fixture: no verified Phase D fixture context. A founder command fixture exists only inside an audited fixture run, inside a transaction that is aborted. (pd_fixture_no_test_context)'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  if v_label is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_founder_authority_fixture: label is required (pd_fixture_label_missing)'
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  v_text := format('PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH — Phase D fixture command for run %s (%s). '
                || 'This is not an instruction from the founder. It exists so that the six rules '
                || 'which resolve founder_authority_ref against public.founder_command have a row '
                || 'to resolve, and it is created inside a transaction that is aborted.',
                   v_run, v_label);

  -- founder_identity is DELIBERATELY a string that resolves to nobody. E39's finding was that a
  -- guard authenticating a string is not authenticating an actor; writing the founder's real
  -- identity here would be the same mistake made on purpose.
  insert into public.founder_command_message
    (founder_identity, raw_text, raw_text_hash, client_idempotency_key, channel)
  values ('PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH',
          v_text,
          encode(sha256(convert_to(v_text,'UTF8')),'hex'),
          format('phase_d_fixture:%s:%s', v_run, v_label),
          'phase_d_fixture')
  returning message_id into v_msg;

  insert into public.founder_command
    (message_id, intent_id, outcome, command_owner_role_id, state, priority, primary_role_id,
     founder_initiated_only, refund_semantics)
  values (v_msg,
          format('PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH:%s', v_label),
          'PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH — a Phase D fixture founder command. It is not an instruction from the founder, it authorises nothing, and it is created inside a transaction that is aborted.',
          'chief_of_staff',
          'received',
          'low',
          'chief_of_staff',
          false,
          false)
  returning command_id into v_id;

  -- G19. THE ROOT TRACE, OPENED THE WAY THE ROUTER OPENS IT.
  -- Without this the command is stuck at 'received' for the rest of its life:
  -- fn_founder_command_trace_guard refuses every later transition with "cannot leave received
  -- without a root trace", and that refusal is correct. The command is created at received above
  -- (the one state the guard allows trace-less at birth) and the trace is stamped on it here, in
  -- the same transaction, which is the sequence the guard's own comment describes.
  v_trace := public.fn_phase_c_trace_write('TRACE-FOUNDER-COMMAND', jsonb_build_object(
    'subject_kind',   'founder_command',
    'subject_ref',    v_id::text,
    'command_id',     v_id,
    'actor_role_id',  'chief_of_staff',
    'system_actor_id','fn_phase_d_founder_authority_fixture',
    'state_before',   '',
    'state_after',    'received',
    'status',         'open',
    'evidence_refs',  jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object(
      'phase_d_fixture_run', v_run, 'label', v_label,
      'note', 'PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH — the root trace of a Phase D fixture founder command. It records that this command exists inside an aborted fixture transaction and authorises nothing.'))));

  update public.founder_command set trace_id = v_trace where command_id = v_id;

  perform public.fn_phase_d_scenario_record_write(jsonb_build_object(
    'fixture_id',        'PDS-founder_authority',
    'fixture_version',   1,
    'source_checksum',   encode(sha256(convert_to(v_text,'UTF8')),'hex'),
    'object_id',         'founder_command_fixture',
    'business_key',      v_id::text,
    'owner_ref',         'chief_of_staff',
    'ownership_scope',   'COMPANY',
    'state',             'received',
    'canonical_relation','public.founder_command',
    'canonical_service', 'fn_phase_d_founder_authority_fixture',
    'result_reference',  format('public.founder_command:command_id=%s', v_id),
    'contributes_ref',   'founder_authority_ref',
    'contributes_kind',  'RESULT_KEY',
    'contributed_value', format('founder_command:%s', v_id),
    'expected_effect',   'BR-003, BR-021..BR-024 and BR-043 resolve founder_authority_ref against public.founder_command and find this row. It authorises nothing: founder AUTHENTICATION is fn_phase_c_require_founder, which reads a verified auth subject and never this table.'));

  return jsonb_build_object('ok', true, 'command_id', v_id, 'message_id', v_msg,
    'founder_authority_ref', format('founder_command:%s', v_id),
    'founder_identity_on_the_message', 'PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH — resolves to nobody',
    'founder_initiated_only', false, 'refund_semantics', false,
    'note','a fixture command; it satisfies "a founder command exists" and nothing else');
end

fn_phase_d_outcome_overdue_report:
select
    o.id,
    o.actor,
    o.dept_key,
    coalesce(nullif(btrim(o.subject_type),'') || ':' || coalesce(o.subject_id::text,'(no id)'),
             '(no subject recorded)'),
    o.due_at,
    greatest(0, (extract(epoch from (now() - o.due_at)) / 86400)::int),
    -- The workflow that owns it, where the subject actually names one.
    coalesce(
      (select r.workflow_id from public.phase_c_workflow_run r
        where o.subject_type in ('workflow_run','phase_c_workflow_run')
          and r.run_id::text = o.subject_id::text),
      (select w.workflow_id from public.phase_b_workflow w
        where w.workflow_id = o.subject_id::text),
      '(the record names ' || coalesce(nullif(btrim(o.subject_type),''),'no subject type')
        || ', which is not a workflow run)'),
    -- The accountable role, from the department that owns the outcome.
    coalesce(
      (select d.lead_agent from public.org_departments d where d.dept_key = o.dept_key),
      (select a.role from public.org_agents a where a.agent_key = o.actor),
      o.actor,
      '(no accountable role resolves from actor or department)'),
    coalesce(o.expected_metric, '(none declared)'),
    coalesce(o.verdict, '(null)'),
    -- WHY IT IS PAUSED. One sentence, and it is about this record rather than about the estate.
    case
      when o.closed_at is not null
        then 'the record is closed; it is overdue only in the sense that its due date has passed'
      when coalesce(o.verdict,'') <> 'pending'
        then format('the record already carries verdict %s, and public.fn_outcome_evaluate only walks records whose verdict is pending', o.verdict)
      else 'the daily evaluation cron outcome_evaluate_daily is inactive by founder instruction, so nothing has graded it'
    end,
    -- THE HOLD, READ FROM cron.job RATHER THAN ASSERTED.
    (select case when j.active then 'ACTIVE — this report is out of date'
                 else format('HELD — cron job %s (%s) is inactive by founder instruction of 21 Aug 2026', j.jobid, j.jobname) end
       from cron.job j where j.jobname = 'outcome_evaluate_daily'),
    -- WHAT ACTIVATION WOULD DO, derived from the evaluator's own selection predicate.
    case
      when coalesce(o.verdict,'') <> 'pending'
        then 'NOTHING — the cron selects verdict = pending and due_at <= now(); this record would be passed by'
      when o.expected_kpi_id is null
        then 'GRADE IT unmeasurable — no KPI is attached, so there is no measure_sql to read a current value from'
      when (select k.measure_sql from public.employee_kpi k where k.id = o.expected_kpi_id) is null
        then 'GRADE IT unmeasurable — the attached KPI carries no measure_sql'
      when o.baseline_value is null
        then 'GRADE IT unmeasurable — no baseline_value was recorded, so no delta can be computed'
      else 'GRADE IT improved, worse or flat by running the attached KPI''s measure_sql and comparing against the recorded baseline'
    end
  from public.outcome_record o
  where o.due_at < now() and o.closed_at is null
  order by o.due_at;

fn_phase_d_ref:
declare
  s        public.phase_d_object_reference_strategy%rowtype;
  b        public.phase_d_business_object_binding%rowtype;
  v_obj    text := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'object_id','')),'');
  v_ident  text := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'identity','')),'');
  v_ver    int  := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'version','')),'')::int;
  v_owner  text := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'owner_ref','')),'');
begin
  if v_obj is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_ref: object_id is required (pd_ref_unknown_object)'
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  select * into s from public.phase_d_object_reference_strategy where object_id = v_obj;
  if not found then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_ref: % is not one of the 56 frozen business objects, so no reference strategy exists for it (pd_ref_unknown_object)',
      v_obj using errcode = '23503';
  end if;
  select * into b from public.phase_d_business_object_binding where object_id = v_obj;

  -- THE IDENTITY IS REQUIRED AND IS NEVER INVENTED. A reference with no identity is the defect this
  -- whole contract exists to remove: it is what let a resolver pick whichever key was nearest.
  if v_ident is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_ref: % needs an identity (%). A reference with no identity is not a reference. (pd_ref_unresolved)',
      v_obj,
      case s.canonical_identity_type
        when 'OBJECT_ID_BUSINESS_KEY_VERSION' then 'its business key'
        else 'its ' || s.physical_relation || '.' || s.physical_pk_column end
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  -- F46. ONE FIELD THAT ALWAYS HOLDS THE IDENTITY, WHATEVER THE STORAGE KIND.
  --
  -- The round-trip proof of section 2 found this on its first run, which is what it is for. The
  -- envelope carried the identity in physical_ref.pk_value on the way IN and the physical row id in
  -- the same field on the way OUT, because for a PHASE_D_STORE object those are different things:
  -- the identity is object_id + business_key + version, and the physical row is
  -- phase_d_object_record.record_id, which nobody knows until the object is resolved. Three of seven
  -- round trips compared the two and reported "wrong identity" on objects that had resolved
  -- perfectly.
  --
  -- canonical_identity is now the single field every consumer reads. It is the business key for a
  -- PHASE_D_STORE object and the relation's primary key for the other two kinds, and no caller has
  -- to know which -- that is the whole point of recording the strategy once. physical_ref now
  -- describes where the object physically lives and carries pk_value only when the caller actually
  -- knows it; for the store it is filled in by fn_phase_d_ref_resolve.
  return jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object(
    'object_id',          v_obj,
    'storage_kind',       s.storage_kind,
    'canonical_identity', v_ident,
    'business_key',       v_ident,
    'version',            coalesce(v_ver, 1),
    'physical_ref', jsonb_build_object(
                      'schema',    s.physical_schema,
                      'relation',  case when s.storage_kind = 'PHASE_D_STORE'
                                        then 'phase_d_object_record' else s.physical_relation end,
                      'pk_column', case when s.storage_kind = 'PHASE_D_STORE'
                                        then 'record_id' else s.physical_pk_column end,
                      'pk_value',  case when s.storage_kind = 'PHASE_D_STORE'
                                        then null else v_ident end),
    'owner_scope',  b.ownership_scope,
    'owner_ref',    v_owner,
    'source_object_ref', p_input->'source_object_ref',
    'trace_id',     nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'trace_id','')),''),
    'fixture_run_id', nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'fixture_run_id','')),'')::bigint));
end

fn_phase_d_kernel_object_fixture:
declare
  v_run_ctx bigint := public.fn_phase_d_fixture_context();
  v_label   text   := nullif(btrim(coalesce(p_input->>'label','')),'');
  v_wf      text;
  v_step    text;
  v_start   jsonb;
  v_run     bigint;
  v_step_run bigint;
  v_handoff bigint;
  v_made    int := 0;
  v_note    text := '';
begin
  if v_run_ctx is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_kernel_object_fixture: no verified Phase D fixture context. A kernel run fixture exists only inside an audited fixture run, inside a transaction that is aborted. (pd_fixture_no_test_context)'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  if v_label is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_kernel_object_fixture: label is required (pd_fixture_label_missing)'
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  -- DERIVED: the lowest-numbered workflow whose first step opens a handoff. Naming one here would
  -- make this stage a fact about a workflow rather than about the kernel.
  select h.from_step_id, split_part(h.from_step_id, '-', 1)
    into v_step, v_wf
    from public.phase_b_handoff h
   where h.from_step_id like '%-S01'
   order by h.from_step_id limit 1;
  if v_wf is null then
    -- No first step in the frozen registry opens a handoff. Fall back to the lowest workflow, which
    -- still creates the run and the step run; the handoff is then honestly absent.
    select w.workflow_id into v_wf from public.phase_b_workflow w order by w.workflow_id limit 1;
    v_note := 'no frozen first step opens a handoff, so handoff_record is not created by this stage';
  end if;

  v_start := public.fn_kernel_workflow_start(jsonb_build_object(
    'workflow_id',        v_wf,
    'business_object_id', 'phase_d_fixture:' || v_label,
    'source_kind',        'autonomous',
    'source_ref',         format('zz-phase-d-kernel-%s', v_label),
    'requested_by',       (select w.accountable_role_id from public.phase_b_workflow w
                            where w.workflow_id = v_wf),
    'trigger_ctx',        jsonb_build_object('driver','fn_phase_d_kernel_object_fixture',
                                             'path','kernel doors only')));
  v_run := (v_start->>'run_id')::bigint;
  if v_run is null then
    raise exception 'fn_phase_d_kernel_object_fixture: the kernel returned no run_id for %. Refusing to record a run that was not created. (pd_fixture_kernel_run_absent)',
      v_wf using errcode = '23502';
  end if;

  select sr.step_run_id into v_step_run from public.phase_c_workflow_step_run sr
   where sr.run_id = v_run order by sr.step_run_id limit 1;

  -- The kernel opens a handoff when the step that declares one COMPLETES. That is the door, and it
  -- is the same one the driver and the handler use.
  if v_step is not null and v_step_run is not null then
    begin
      perform public.fn_kernel_step_complete(jsonb_build_object(
        'step_run_id', v_step_run,
        'actor_role_id', (select s.accountable_role_id from public.phase_b_workflow_step s
                           where s.step_id = v_step),
        -- The kernel requires an idempotency key and is right to: the same completion arriving
        -- twice must close one step, not two. It is derived from the step run, so a replay of this
        -- fixture inside one transaction cannot produce a second handoff.
        'idempotency_key', format('phase_d_kernel_fixture:%s:%s', v_label, v_step_run),
        'outcome','pass',
        -- The kernel refuses a completion that does not carry the step's declared inputs, an
        -- output, evidence and a requested action. It is right to, and the shape below is the one
        -- fn_phase_d_drive_workflow already uses through the same door: no business content is
        -- supplied, only the bookkeeping the kernel's own contract requires.
        'inputs', jsonb_build_object('driver','fn_phase_d_kernel_object_fixture',
                                     'note','no business content is supplied by this fixture'),
        'output', jsonb_build_object('status','completed',
                                     'output', format('%s completed %s', v_label, v_step)),
        'evidence_refs', jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('fixture_run', v_label)),
        'requested_action','proceed',
        'acceptance_criteria', format('the kernel opened the handoff %s declares', v_step),
        'object_version', 1,
        'note','PHASE_D_FIXTURE_DO_NOT_PUBLISH — completing one step so the kernel opens the handoff whose reference this stage records'));
    exception when others then
      v_note := coalesce(nullif(v_note,''), '') ||
        format(' the kernel declined to complete %s: %s', v_step, left(SQLERRM, 160));
    end;
    select hr.handoff_run_id into v_handoff from public.phase_c_handoff_run hr
     where hr.run_id = v_run order by hr.handoff_run_id limit 1;
  end if;

  -- RECORD ONLY WHAT EXISTS. Each of the three is recorded if and only if the kernel made it.
  if v_run is not null then
    perform public.fn_phase_d_scenario_record_write(jsonb_build_object(
      'fixture_id','PDS-workflow_run', 'fixture_version', 1,
      'source_checksum', encode(sha256(convert_to(v_run::text,'UTF8')),'hex'),
      'object_id','workflow_run', 'business_key', v_run::text, 'owner_ref','kernel',
      'ownership_scope','COMPANY', 'state','open',
      'canonical_relation','public.phase_c_workflow_run',
      'canonical_service','fn_kernel_workflow_start',
      'result_reference', format('public.phase_c_workflow_run:run_id=%s', v_run),
      'contributes_ref', null, 'contributes_kind','RESULT_KEY',
      'contributed_value', v_run::text,
      'canonical_ref', public.fn_phase_d_ref(jsonb_build_object(
        'object_id','workflow_run', 'identity', v_run::text, 'owner_ref','kernel')),
      'expected_effect','The kernel created this run through fn_kernel_workflow_start; no Phase D routine may write public.phase_c_workflow_run.'));
    v_made := v_made + 1;
  end if;

  if v_step_run is not null then
    perform public.fn_phase_d_scenario_record_write(jsonb_build_object(
      'fixture_id','PDS-workflow_step_run', 'fixture_version', 1,
      'source_checksum', encode(sha256(convert_to(v_step_run::text,'UTF8')),'hex'),
      'object_id','workflow_step_run', 'business_key', v_step_run::text, 'owner_ref','kernel',
      'ownership_scope','COMPANY', 'state','open',
      'canonical_relation','public.phase_c_workflow_step_run',
      'canonical_service','fn_kernel_open_step',
      'result_reference', format('public.phase_c_workflow_step_run:step_run_id=%s', v_step_run),
      'contributes_ref', null, 'contributes_kind','RESULT_KEY',
      'contributed_value', v_step_run::text,
      'canonical_ref', public.fn_phase_d_ref(jsonb_build_object(
        'object_id','workflow_step_run', 'identity', v_step_run::text, 'owner_ref','kernel')),
      'expected_effect','The kernel opened this step run inside fn_kernel_workflow_start; no Phase D routine may write public.phase_c_workflow_step_run.'));
    v_made := v_made + 1;
  end if;

  if v_handoff is not null then
    perform public.fn_phase_d_scenario_record_write(jsonb_build_object(
      'fixture_id','PDS-handoff_record', 'fixture_version', 1,
      'source_checksum', encode(sha256(convert_to(v_handoff::text,'UTF8')),'hex'),
      'object_id','handoff_record', 'business_key', v_handoff::text, 'owner_ref','kernel',
      'ownership_scope','COMPANY', 'state','open',
      'canonical_relation','public.phase_c_handoff_run',
      'canonical_service','fn_kernel_step_complete',
      'result_reference', format('public.phase_c_handoff_run:handoff_run_id=%s', v_handoff),
      'contributes_ref', null, 'contributes_kind','RESULT_KEY',
      'contributed_value', v_handoff::text,
      'canonical_ref', public.fn_phase_d_ref(jsonb_build_object(
        'object_id','handoff_record', 'identity', v_handoff::text, 'owner_ref','kernel')),
      'expected_effect','The kernel opened this handoff run when the step that declares it completed; no Phase D routine may write public.phase_c_handoff_run.'));
    v_made := v_made + 1;
  end if;

  return jsonb_build_object('ok', v_made > 0, 'workflow_id', v_wf,
    'run_id', v_run, 'step_run_id', v_step_run, 'handoff_run_id', v_handoff,
    'objects_recorded', v_made, 'note', coalesce(nullif(v_note,''),
    'every row recorded here was created by the frozen kernel through its own doors'));
end
fn_phase_d_outbound_requests_by_this_tra:
declare
  -- The 64-bit id carries the epoch; the 32-bit form is what a row's xmin holds.
  v_top8  bigint := pg_current_xact_id()::text::bigint;
  v_top32 bigint := mod(pg_current_xact_id()::text::bigint, 4294967296);
begin
  return query
  select count(*)::int,
         string_agg(distinct q.method || ' ' || q.url, ', ')
    from net.http_request_queue q
   where q.id > p_after
     -- Anything below our own xid was written before this transaction started and cannot be ours.
     -- Filtering it first also fixes the epoch for the conversion on the next line.
     and q.xmin::text::bigint >= v_top32
     -- A visible row whose writer is still in progress is ours: another in-flight transaction's
     -- rows are not visible here at all, and a committed one reports 'committed'.
     and pg_xact_status(((v_top8 - v_top32) + q.xmin::text::bigint)::text::xid8) = 'in progress';
end
